snapshot.stmt:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times N}\), \(m\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^N\). If \(K=\{q\in\mathbb R^N:q\geq0,\ Aq=m\}\) is nonempty and bounded, then both optima are attained and
\[
 \min_{q\in K}c^\top q
 =\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^r}\{m^\top\eta:A^\top\eta\leq c\}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 4.4 (Strong duality) If a linear programming problem has an optimal solution, so does its dual, and the respective optimal costs are equal.

attestation.note: Exact theorem statement transcribed from Bertsimas and Tsitsiklis, Introduction to Linear Optimization (1997), Chapter 4, p. 148; publisher handle https://athenasc.com/linoptbook.html, corroborated against the web-visible book scan.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 5.1 (CTFTR completeness). A counterfactual probability P*(y* | x*) is transportable from Z and G_Delta if and only if CTFTR returns an expression for it.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 3.5 (CTFIDU+ soundness and completeness). Given an un-nested counterfactual expression Y*, P(Y*=y) is identifiable from a causal diagram G and a set of input distributions A, iff CTFIDU+ returns an expression for it.

snapshot.stmt: For every finite-state recursive SCM \(M^s\) compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\), there is a finite canonical SCM \(N^s\) with the same causal diagram and the same observed state spaces such that every finite joint counterfactual distribution induced by \(N^s\) equals the corresponding distribution induced by \(M^s\).

node.gap: The source theorem is one-domain; it does not itself impose source labels, district invariance, complete Layer-3 menu constraints, or the fixed-alphabet multi-domain optimization fiber.

source.verbatim_statement: Let P \(\subset R[X^{[1]},\ldots,X^{[\omega]},Y]_{\le d}\) be a finite set of s polynomials, where \(X^{[i]}\) is a block of \(k_i\) variables, and Y is a block of \(\ell\) variables. Consider the quantified formula \(\Psi(Y)=(Q_1X^{[1]})\cdots(Q_\omega X^{[\omega]})\Phi(X^{[1]},\ldots,X^{[\omega]},Y)\), where \(\Phi\) is a quantifier-free P-formula. Then there exists a quantifier-free formula \(\Theta(Y)=\bigvee_{i=1}^{I}\bigwedge_{j=1}^{J_i}\bigvee_{n=1}^{N_{ij}}\operatorname{sign}(P_{ijn}(Y))=\sigma_{ijn}\) equivalent to \(\Psi\), where \(P_{ijn}(Y)\) are polynomials in the variables Y and \(\sigma_{ijn}\in\{-1,0,1\}\). Furthermore, \(I\le s^{(k_\omega+1)\cdots(k_1+1)(\ell+1)}d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)O(\ell)}\), \(J_i\le s^{(k_\omega+1)\cdots(k_1+1)}d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)}\), \(N_{ij}\le d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)}\), and the degrees of the polynomials \(P_{ijn}(y)\) are bounded by \(d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)}\). Moreover, there exists an algorithm ([5, Algorithm 14.5] (Quantifier Elimination)) to compute \(\Theta(Y)\) with complexity \(s^{(k_\omega+1)\cdots(k_1+1)(\ell+1)}d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)O(\ell)}\) in D, where D denotes the ring generated by the coefficients of the polynomials in P. If D = Z and \(\tau\) denotes an upper bound on bitsizes of P, then the bitsizes of the integers in the intermediate computations and the output are bounded by \(\tau d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)O(\ell)}\).

thm:partial-district-no-free-transport.proof_tex:
Put
\[
J=D\cap\Delta_s,
\qquad
I=D\setminus\Delta_s.
\]
The displayed hypothesis gives \(J\ne\varnothing\), \(I\ne\varnothing\), and \(D\cap\Delta_s\ne\varnothing\).  Consequently the antecedent \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) in Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\) is false for the designated pair \((s,D)\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\) constrains each domain separately, and Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\) constrains distinct districts within one domain; neither of them equates the focal district response laws in domains \(s\) and \(\star\).  These observations use exactly the retained assumptions after district closure is omitted.

For a row \(\ell:\Omega_D\to\mathbb R\) and a probability vector \(q\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\), define the finite pairing
\[
\langle\ell,q\rangle
=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_D}\ell(\omega)q(\omega).
\tag{1}
\]
Suppose first that \(\ell\) is nonconstant.  Finiteness of \(\Omega_D\), supplied by Definition \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\), gives profiles \(\omega_0,\omega_1\in\Omega_D\) for which
\[
\alpha:=\ell(\omega_0)\ne\ell(\omega_1)=:\beta.
\tag{2}
\]
For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), prescribe the focal district laws of a source-labelled family \(\mathbf M^{(i)}\) by
\[
q_D^{s,(i)}=\delta_{\omega_0},
\qquad
q_D^{\star,(i)}=\delta_{\omega_i},
\tag{3}
\]
where \(\delta_\omega\) is the point mass at \(\omega\).  For every \(t\in\mathcal S\setminus\{s,\star\}\), put
\[
q_D^{t,(i)}=
\begin{cases}
\delta_{\omega_i},&D\cap\Delta_t=\varnothing,\\
\delta_{\omega_0},&D\cap\Delta_t\ne\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\tag{4}
\]
Thus, whenever the antecedent of district-kernel invariance is true for \((t,D)\), equation (4) makes the source law equal to the target law in that same family.  For every district \(D'\ne D\), the nonemptiness of each declared alphabet supplies a tuple of constant response maps and hence an element of \(\Omega_{D'}\).  Choose one such profile \(\bar\omega_{D'}\in\Omega_{D'}\) and set
\[
q_{D'}^{t,(i)}=\delta_{\bar\omega_{D'}}
\quad
\text{for every }t\in\mathcal S\text{ and }i\in\{0,1\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Equation (5) satisfies every remaining instance of district-kernel invariance.

We next verify original-alphabet realization rather than merely prescribing formal probability vectors.  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\), each \(\omega\in\Omega_D\) already consists of deterministic response maps with codomain \(\mathcal X_V\) at every graph-allowed parent configuration, and the same is true of each \(\bar\omega_{D'}\).  In each domain, use the indicated deterministic tables as the structural equations and equip their exogenous inputs with point-mass laws.  A point mass factors across any partition, so the exogenous response blocks of distinct districts are independent, as required by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\).  Every table uses only graph-allowed parents and values in the declared alphabet.  Since \(G\) is acyclic, recursive evaluation in a topological order is unique.  Hence the constructed models are finite recursive SCMs compatible with \(G\) on the original \(\mathcal X\), which verifies Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\).  Equations (3)--(5) verify every true-antecedent instance of Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\).  No observed state has been added.

All district tables and laws in the designated source are the same for \(i=0\) and \(i=1\): the focal source law is \(\delta_{\omega_0}\) by (3), and every nonfocal law is common by (5).  Therefore
\[
M^{s,(0)}=M^{s,(1)}.
\tag{6}
\]
Every observational, interventional, or declared same-source Layer-3 output is a deterministic recursive evaluation followed by marginalization under this source SCM.  Equation (6) therefore implies equality of all complete laws supplied from domain \(s\), not merely equality of one reported row.  In particular,
\[
\langle\ell,q_D^{s,(0)}\rangle
=\langle\ell,q_D^{s,(1)}\rangle
=\alpha.
\tag{7}
\]
The target values, however, are
\[
\langle\ell,q_D^{\star,(0)}\rangle=\alpha,
\qquad
\langle\ell,q_D^{\star,(1)}\rangle=\beta,
\tag{8}
\]
and they differ by (2).  Equations (3)--(8) are the promised equal-source-law, unequal-target, original-alphabet certificate for every nonconstant real row.

Conversely, if \(\ell\equiv c\) on \(\Omega_D\), normalization of every \(q\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\) gives
\[
\langle\ell,q\rangle
=c\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_D}q(\omega)
=c.
\tag{9}
\]
Thus the target value of a constant row is known without any cross-domain information.  Equations (2)--(8) exclude universal source-only determination for every other row, while (9) proves it for constant rows.  This proves the first equivalence.  Notice that the pair is allowed to differ in a target-domain law and in a further source law whose unselected focal district must equal the target.  Accordingly, the conclusion concerns only information supplied from the designated partially selected source; it does not survive automatically if either kind of extra law is observed.

Now add the premise that the response-profile marginal on \(I\) is invariant between the designated source and target.  Let
\[
\pi_I:\Omega_D\longrightarrow\pi_I(\Omega_D)
\]
be coordinate restriction to the response maps of vertices in \(I\).  The added premise is the finite pushforward equality
\[
(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^s=(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^\star.
\tag{10}
\]
Suppose that \(\ell\) is constant on every fiber of \(\pi_I\).  Then the function
\[
\widetilde\ell(u)=\ell(\omega)
\quad\text{for any }\omega\text{ with }\pi_I(\omega)=u
\tag{11}
\]
is well defined on \(\pi_I(\Omega_D)\), and \(\ell=\widetilde\ell\circ\pi_I\).  Grouping finite sums by projection fibers and using (10) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\langle\ell,q_D^s\rangle
&=\sum_{u\in\pi_I(\Omega_D)}
  \widetilde\ell(u)(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^s(u)\\
&=\sum_{u\in\pi_I(\Omega_D)}
  \widetilde\ell(u)(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^\star(u)\\
&=\langle\ell,q_D^\star\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
Hence fiber constancy is sufficient.

For necessity, suppose that fiber constancy fails.  There are then \(\omega_0,\omega_1\in\Omega_D\) such that
\[
\pi_I(\omega_0)=\pi_I(\omega_1),
\qquad
\ell(\omega_0)\ne\ell(\omega_1).
\tag{13}
\]
Repeat the construction (3)--(6) with this pair.  In the model \(\mathbf M^{(i)}\), the source and target pushforwards are respectively
\[
(\pi_I)_{\#}\delta_{\omega_0}
=\delta_{\pi_I(\omega_0)}
=\delta_{\pi_I(\omega_1)}
=(\pi_I)_{\#}\delta_{\omega_i}.
\tag{14}
\]
Thus each model satisfies the added marginal-invariance premise (10), the two models still have identical complete laws in source \(s\), and their target row values differ by (13).  This proves necessity and the second scalar equivalence.

Let \(L\in\mathbb R^{k\times|\Omega_D|}\) be any finite matrix with row functions \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\), and define
\[
Lq=
\bigl(\langle\ell_1,q\rangle,\ldots,
      \langle\ell_k,q\rangle\bigr)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{15}
\]
If every row is fiber-constant, equation (12), applied separately to each \(\ell_j\), gives \(Lq_D^s=Lq_D^\star\).  If some row \(\ell_j\) is not fiber-constant, choose a failing pair for that row and apply (13)--(14); the \(j\)-th target components then differ although the complete designated-source laws agree.  This proves the componentwise matrix equivalence under (10).  Without (10), the same argument uses (2)--(9) and shows that componentwise universal transport is equivalent to every row being constant on all of \(\Omega_D\).

The characterizations are finite algorithms.  Under (10), enumerate, for each row \(j\), all pairs \((\omega,\omega')\in\Omega_D^2\) satisfying \(\pi_I(\omega)=\pi_I(\omega')\), and compare \(\ell_j(\omega)\) with \(\ell_j(\omega')\).  Without (10), enumerate all pairs.  This uses at most \(k|\Omega_D|^2\) equality comparisons.  Rational equality is decided exactly by integer cross multiplication after choosing fraction representations.  For an effectively represented real-algebraic entry, exact equality comparison is part of the stipulated effective representation, so the same finite loop is exact.  Exhaustion without a failure certifies the required constancy.  A failure returns \((j,\omega_0,\omega_1)\), and equations (3)--(8), or (3)--(8) together with (14), construct the two-Dirac certificate.  This is the finite leakage test named by Definition \(\mathrm{def:partial\text{-}district\text{-}leakage\text{-}handle}\).

By Definition \(\mathrm{def:incidence\text{-}row}\), binary event cells are scalar rows and hence are a direct special case.  Rows with entries in \(\{-1,0,1\}\), including pairwise arm gaps, arbitrary real-valued reward rows on the finite profile set, and rows used in finite linear certificates are also scalar rows in \(\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}\); the proved equivalences therefore apply to them without alteration.

As the smallest exact stress check, take binary vertices \(X\) and \(Y\) with ADMG \(X\leftrightarrow Y\), let \(D=\{X,Y\}\), and let \(\Delta_s=\{X\}\).  Choose constant response profiles \(\omega_0=(X=0,Y=0)\) and \(\omega_1=(X=1,Y=0)\), and take \(\ell(\omega)=\mathbf 1\{X(\omega)=1\}\).  The two source laws are both \(\delta_{\omega_0}\), whereas the target laws \(\delta_{\omega_0}\) and \(\delta_{\omega_1}\) give exact target values zero and one.  Their \(I=\{Y\}\) marginals are identical, so the same pair also witnesses the fiber criterion.  Restoring district closure excludes this selection pattern because neither \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) nor \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) holds.  This verifies on the smallest two-profile instance that the omitted condition is load-bearing.  No division, conditioning, positivity premise, or limiting argument is used anywhere in the proof.

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(s\in\mathcal S\setminus\{\star\}\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(0<|D\cap\Delta_s|<|D|\).  Omit district closure, retain recursive compatibility, district factorization, and district-kernel invariance exactly as stated, and restrict the available information to the complete laws supplied from this designated partially selected source \(s\).  For a scalar row \(\ell\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}\), its target value is universally determined by those source laws if and only if \(\ell\) is constant on \(\Omega_D\).  More strongly, every nonconstant \(\ell\) admits two finite source-labelled SCM families on the original declared alphabets \(\mathcal X\) that satisfy all retained assumptions, induce identical complete supplied laws in domain \(s\), and have unequal target values of \(\ell\).  If one additionally requires invariance of the marginal response law on \(I=D\setminus\Delta_s\), then universal transport holds if and only if \(\ell\) is constant on every fiber of the coordinate projection \(\pi_I:\Omega_D\to\pi_I(\Omega_D)\).  For every finite real matrix, componentwise universal transport holds if and only if every row has the corresponding constancy property.  For rational rows, and for real-algebraic rows given by effective representations supporting exact equality comparison, the criterion is decidable by finite enumeration; failure returns a row index and two response profiles giving an original-alphabet two-Dirac certificate.  Thus binary incidence and event rows, \(\{-1,0,1\}\)-valued arm-gap rows, finite real reward rows, and linear-certificate rows are all covered.  The result is only a designated-source-information limitation: it makes no claim after adding target-domain data or data from a wholly unselected source whose district law is tied to the target.

defs.def:district-response-profile: For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), set \(\Omega_D=\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\), the finite set of all tuples \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) of deterministic response maps at every parent configuration allowed by \(G\) and \(\mathcal X\).  For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\) is the joint law of the response maps induced by \(M^s\).  The carrier is query independent and includes every configuration needed by any target, menu, deterministic postprocessor, or later acquired regime.
defs.def:incidence-row:
For every successful row-eligibility record define the separate numerator and context rows
\[
\begin{split}
r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)
&=\mathbf 1\{A_{h,c}\text{ has the common value certified by }
\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\},\\
v_{s,a,D,h}(\omega_D)
&=\mathbf 1\{H_h\text{ has the common value certified by }
\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\},
\end{split}
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
For a complete supplied output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\), an accepting locality trace similarly constructs
\[
r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}=\operatorname{row}_D(C_{a,y}).
\]
The quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) is not an incidence row.
defs.def:partial-district-leakage-handle: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{leak}}\) splits a selected district response kernel across \(D\cap\Delta_s\) and \(D\setminus\Delta_s\), tests whether supplied and target Layer-3 factors depend on a common invariant marginal kernel, and searches the smallest binary crossing perturbation when they do not.

assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).

(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^s=(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^\star.
\tag{10}
\]
Suppose that \(\ell\) is constant on every fiber of \(\pi_I\).  Then the function
\[
\widetilde\ell(u)=\ell(\omega)
\quad\text{for any }\omega\text{ with }\pi_I(\omega)=u
\tag{11}
\]
is well defined on \(\pi_I(\Omega_D)\), and \(\ell=\widetilde\ell\circ\pi_I\).  Grouping finite sums by projection fibers and using (10) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\langle\ell,q_D^s\rangle
&=\sum_{u\in\pi_I(\Omega_D)}
  \widetilde\ell(u)(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^s(u)\\
&=\sum_{u\in\pi_I(\Omega_D)}
  \widetilde\ell(u)(\pi_I)_{\#}q_D^\star(u)\\
&=\langle\ell,q_D^\star\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
Hence fiber constancy is sufficient.

For necessity, suppose that fiber constancy fails.  There are then \(\omega_0,\omega_1\in\Omega_D\) such that
\[
\pi_I(\omega_0)=\pi_I(\omega_1),
\qquad
\ell(\omega_0)\ne\ell(\omega_1).
\tag{13}
\]
Repeat the construction (3)--(6) with this pair.  In the model \(\mathbf M^{(i)}\), the source and target pushforwards are respectively
\[
(\pi_I)_{\#}\delta_{\omega_0}
=\delta_{\pi_I(\omega_0)}
=\delta_{\pi_I(\omega_1)}
=(\pi_I)_{\#}\delta_{\omega_i}.
\tag{14}
\]
Thus each model satisfies the added marginal-invariance premise (10), the two models still have identical complete laws in source \(s\), and their target row values differ by (13).  This proves necessity and the second scalar equivalence.

Let \(L\in\mathbb R^{k\times|\Omega_D|}\) be any finite matrix with row functions \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\), and define
\[
Lq=
\bigl(\langle\ell_1,q\rangle,\ldots,
      \langle\ell_k,q\rangle\bigr)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{15}
\]
If every row is fiber-constant, equation (12), applied separately to each \(\ell_j\), gives \(Lq_D^s=Lq_D^\star\).  If some row \(\ell_j\) is not fiber-constant, choose a failing pair for that row and apply (13)--(14); the \(j\)-th target components then differ although the complete designated-source laws agree.  This proves the componentwise matrix equivalence under (10).  Without (10), the same argument uses (2)--(9) and shows that componentwise universal transport is equivalent to every row being constant on all of \(\Omega_D\).

The characterizations are finite algorithms.  Under (10), enumerate, for each row \(j\), all pairs \((\omega,\omega')\in\Omega_D^2\) satisfying \(\pi_I(\omega)=\pi_I(\omega')\), and compare \(\ell_j(\omega)\) with \(\ell_j(\omega')\).  Without (10), enumerate all pairs.  This uses at most \(k|\Omega_D|^2\) equality comparisons.  Rational equality is decided exactly by integer cross multiplication after choosing fraction representations.  For an effectively represented real-algebraic entry, exact equality comparison is part of the stipulated effective representation, so the same finite loop is exact.  Exhaustion without a failure certifies the required constancy.  A failure returns \((j,\omega_0,\omega_1)\), and equations (3)--(8), or (3)--(8) together with (14), construct the two-Dirac certificate.  This is the finite leakage test named by Definition \(\mathrm{def:partial\text{-}district\text{-}leakage\text{-}handle}\).

By Definition \(\mathrm{def:incidence\text{-}row}\), binary event cells are scalar rows and hence are a direct special case.  Rows with entries in \(\{-1,0,1\}\), including pairwise arm gaps, arbitrary real-valued reward rows on the finite profile set, and rows used in finite linear certificates are also scalar rows in \(\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}\); the proved equivalences therefore apply to them without alteration.

As the smallest exact stress check, take binary vertices \(X\) and \(Y\) with ADMG \(X\leftrightarrow Y\), let \(D=\{X,Y\}\), and let \(\Delta_s=\{X\}\).  Choose constant response profiles \(\omega_0=(X=0,Y=0)\) and \(\omega_1=(X=1,Y=0)\), and take \(\ell(\omega)=\mathbf 1\{X(\omega)=1\}\).  The two source laws are both \(\delta_{\omega_0}\), whereas the target laws \(\delta_{\omega_0}\) and \(\delta_{\omega_1}\) give exact target values zero and one.  Their \(I=\{Y\}\) marginals are identical, so the same pair also witnesses the fiber criterion.  Restoring district closure excludes this selection pattern because neither \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) nor \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) holds.  This verifies on the smallest two-profile instance that the omitted condition is load-bearing.  No division, conditioning, positivity premise, or limiting argument is used anywhere in the proof.

lem:structural-separation-implies-active.proof_tex:
Assume \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\).  If a complete supplied output-cell indicator is independent of \(\omega_D\), then every focal slice is either the zero row or the normalization row.  If it depends only on \(\omega_D\), then every slice is its accepted raw row.  For a deterministic postprocessor this conclusion follows by evaluating its finite preimage indicator, not by adding tuple-cell probabilities to the menu.  In both cases every slice belongs to \(R_D(m_D)\), proving \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).

For strictness, let \(Y_0\) and \(Z\) be independent binary response coordinates in distinct singleton districts, let \(D\) generate \(Y_0\), and supply in the target domain the complete marginal law of \(Y_0\) and the complete joint law of \((Y_0,Z)\).  Write
\[
h_y(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{Y_0=y\},
\qquad
k_z(\omega_{-D})=\mathbf 1\{Z=z\}.
\]
The marginal menu retains \(h_y\), whereas a joint cell has cross-district indicator \(h_yk_z\), so structural separation fails.  After fixing \(\omega_{-D}\), however, its focal slice is either zero or \(h_y\), both in the active row space.  Hence active-slice separation holds.  Independent Bernoulli response blocks realize this menu on the original binary alphabets, proving strictness.

defs.def:active-slice-separated-menu:
For a fixed district \(D\), define its active row space by
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\subseteq\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
For a complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and for
\(\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'}\), define its focal recursive-indicator slice by
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(\omega_D)
=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
The active-slice face-separation predicate \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell and every fixed nonfocal response profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  When \(D\) is the only district, the nonfocal product is the singleton empty profile.
defs.def:district-response-profile: For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), set \(\Omega_D=\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\), the finite set of all tuples \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) of deterministic response maps at every parent configuration allowed by \(G\) and \(\mathcal X\).  For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\) is the joint law of the response maps induced by \(M^s\).  The carrier is query independent and includes every configuration needed by any target, menu, deterministic postprocessor, or later acquired regime.
defs.def:district-separated-menu: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\).  This is a finite syntactic and tabular condition; it excludes an unrecorded cross-district polynomial constraint involving \(q_D^\star\).
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]
defs.def:stacked-menu-system:
Fix \(D\).  Enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete output cell, and extraction record canonically.  A candidate is transport admissible only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  First retain every admissible complete output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\) whose exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) table accepts, with row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}\) and supplied value \(P_a^s(y)\).  Next, for every successful extraction judgment retain separately the numerator pair
\[
(r_{s,a,D,h,c},N_{s,a,D,h,c})
\]
and the context pair
\[
(v_{s,a,D,h},H_{s,a,D,h}).
\]
Never stack the quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) as a linear row.  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) with value one and stack precisely the accepted raw, numerator, and context rows as \(A_D\), with their values in the same order as \(m_D\).  A failed locality, fixing, expression, positivity, or admissibility check contributes no row.  A rejected complete cell remains, without information loss, among the complete polynomial equalities of the exact global fiber.  For a deterministic postprocessor, recursive locality and the raw incidence row use the preimage identity \((1)\) from \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), but the stacked value is the directly supplied output probability \(P_a^s(y)\).
defs.def:finite-extraction-calculus:
The finite extraction calculus has event syntax
\[
\mathsf{XEvent}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\top\mid\bot\mid
\neg\mathsf{XEvent}\mid
\bigsqcup_{j\in J}\mathsf{XEvent}_j\mid
\operatorname{Marg}_{W}(\mathsf{XEvent})\mid
\operatorname{Fix}(\mathsf{FixTrace},\mathsf{XEvent}),
\]
where \(J\) and every marginalized alphabet are finite, and a disjoint-union node carries a complete pointwise disjointness table.  The cell event is
\[
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its probability leaf is the supplied output cell \(P_a^s(y)\).  Only its recursively evaluated indicator is expanded by the finite identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\};
\tag{1}
\]
the tuple-cell probabilities on the right of \((1)\) are not menu generators unless an identity-output tuple descriptor is separately supplied.

Menu expressions have syntax
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{XExpr}::={}&
\operatorname{CellProb}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j
\mid\mathsf{XExpr}-\mathsf{XExpr}
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j\\
&\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\pi_H),
\end{split}
\]
where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\pi_H\) is a separately checkable strict-positivity certificate on its declared compatibility fiber.  A derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) is generated only by an output-cell lookup, the truth-table identity \((1)\), contradiction or sure-event evaluation, finite disjoint additivity, complementation, finite marginalization, multiplication of independent original-district factors, and a checked fixing trace.

A fixing trace is a finite tree whose leaves are event or expression derivations and whose constructors are identity, typed substitution from a fixed finite registry of sound Boolean or fixing identities, finite disjoint sum, finite product, complement, marginalization, conditional quotient with a separately checked positive denominator, composition, and cleared-denominator comparison.  Every constructor stores all of its children and type data.  A comparison node is accepted only when cross-multiplication is legal under its stored denominator certificates and coefficient-by-coefficient normalization gives the zero polynomial.  The identity registry is finite and contains only pointwise Boolean identities, finite total-probability identities, and the fixing identities explicitly verified by recursive substitution of structural response tables.  Thus no constructor contains the semantic equality it is intended to establish.

Positivity certificates are either a positive rational constant after exact normalization, a rational Farkas identity for a linear face, or a displayed finite preordering identity
\[
p-\varepsilon=
\sum_i\tau_i h_i+
\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}\sigma_J
\prod_{j\in J}g_j,
\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
where the declared fiber has equations \(h_i=0\), inequalities \(g_j\geq0\), and every \(\sigma_J\) is checked coefficient by coefficient to be a finite sum of squares.  All polynomial equalities are checked by exact integer or rational coefficient comparison.

For an event \(A\) and a district \(D\), the total procedure \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) enumerates
\[
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\longmapsto
\mathbf 1\{A\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\}
\]
over the complete finite response carriers.  It accepts exactly when every two entries with the same \(\omega_D\) agree, and then returns their common row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\).  Otherwise it returns the first disagreeing pair in the canonical order.  All syntax trees, registries, coefficient vectors, truth tables, and searches are finite and canonically ordered.

assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).

lem:active-slice-implies-baseline-averag.proof_tex:
Choose \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\).  District factorization gives the finite nonfocal product law \(\nu_{-D}^{0,s}\).  Under \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), every focal slice lies in the linear space \(R_D(m_D)\), so
\[
\bar\chi_C^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C,\omega_{-D}}
\in R_D(m_D).
\tag{1}
\]
The same baseline works for every cell and domain, proving \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\).  Composition with the structural-separation lemma gives the full hierarchy.

For strictness, take independent fair binary roots \(X,Z\) feeding the deterministic binary child \(Y=\mathbf 1\{X=Z\}\), and let \(D=\{X\}\).  Supply only the complete target-domain output law of \(Y\).  Then \(A_D=\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) and
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{(1,1)\}.
\]
The two focal slices of \(\{Y=1\}\) are \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\), so active-slice separation fails.  Their average under the fair nonfocal law of \(Z\) is \((1/2,1/2)\in R_D(m_D)\); the complementary output cell is analogous.  Focal saturation permits every law of \(X\) while the fair law of \(Z\) and the structural table of \(Y\) stay fixed, so this single compatible baseline proves \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\).  Thus the second implication is strict on the original binary alphabets.

snapshot.stmt:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow \mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
Together with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\Longrightarrow\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), this gives the convenient hierarchy
\[
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow \mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
The second implication is strict on finite original alphabets: there is a three-vertex binary DAG and a complete target-domain menu for which \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds but \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) fails because two Boolean focal slices outside \(R_D(m_D)\) average to a row inside it under the witnessing nonfocal product law.

defs.def:baseline-averaged-active-slice-menu:
Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\).  For a baseline \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), let
\[
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
=\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}q_{D'}^{0,s}(\omega_{D'}),
\qquad
\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\]
where \(q_{D'}^{0,s}\) is the response-profile law induced by \(M^{0,s}\).  For every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), define the baseline-averaged focal row
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}
\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]

\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell.  The same witnessing baseline must be used for all cells and all feasible replacements of the focal law; a baseline depending on the replacement law is not permitted.
defs.def:compatible-face:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:focal-district-saturated-model-class:
For a fixed district \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete};\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ there is exactly one finite latent block }
U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{storing one full deterministic response map for each vertex in }D
\text{ at every allowed parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation of a vertex in }D
\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&U_D^s\text{ is independent of the exogenous blocks of every }D'\ne D;\\
&\text{every probability law on }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ is permitted for }U_D^s,
\text{ subject only to equality with the target law}\\
&\text{when }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing;\\
&\text{for each }D'\ne D\text{, all structural tables, latent-factor restrictions,}
\text{ and cross-domain equalities remain those of }\mathfrak M
\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The phrase ``every probability law is permitted'' includes closure under replacing the law of \(U_D^\star\) and all its unchanged-source copies while holding all mechanisms and latent laws in districts \(D'\ne D\), and all changed-source copies of \(U_D\), fixed. Define
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]

A derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) is generated only by an output-cell lookup, the truth-table identity \((1)\), contradiction or sure-event evaluation, finite disjoint additivity, complementation, finite marginalization, multiplication of independent original-district factors, and a checked fixing trace.

A fixing trace is a finite tree whose leaves are event or expression derivations and whose constructors are identity, typed substitution from a fixed finite registry of sound Boolean or fixing identities, finite disjoint sum, finite product, complement, marginalization, conditional quotient with a separately checked positive denominator, composition, and cleared-denominator comparison.  Every constructor stores all of its children and type data.  A comparison node is accepted only when cross-multiplication is legal under its stored denominator certificates and coefficient-by-coefficient normalization gives the zero polynomial.  The identity registry is finite and contains only pointwise Boolean identities, finite total-probability identities, and the fixing identities explicitly verified by recursive substitution of structural response tables.  Thus no constructor contains the semantic equality it is intended to establish.

Positivity certificates are either a positive rational constant after exact normalization, a rational Farkas identity for a linear face, or a displayed finite preordering identity
\[
p-\varepsilon=
\sum_i\tau_i h_i+
\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}\sigma_J
\prod_{j\in J}g_j,
\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
where the declared fiber has equations \(h_i=0\), inequalities \(g_j\geq0\), and every \(\sigma_J\) is checked coefficient by coefficient to be a finite sum of squares.  All polynomial equalities are checked by exact integer or rational coefficient comparison.

For an event \(A\) and a district \(D\), the total procedure \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) enumerates
\[
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\longmapsto
\mathbf 1\{A\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\}
\]
over the complete finite response carriers.  It accepts exactly when every two entries with the same \(\omega_D\) agree, and then returns their common row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\).  Otherwise it returns the first disagreeing pair in the canonical order.  All syntax trees, registries, coefficient vectors, truth tables, and searches are finite and canonically ordered.
defs.def:typed-extraction-judgment:
For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal Y_a)\), write
\[
\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)
\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)
\]
exactly when the finite extraction calculus constructs, for every retained \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), a numerator event \(A_{h,c}\), a context event \(H_h\), derivations
\[
\delta_N:A_{h,c}\Downarrow N_{s,a,D,h,c},
\qquad
\delta_H:H_h\Downarrow H_{s,a,D,h},
\]
two accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) traces, the rows those traces construct,
\[
r_{s,a,D,h,c}=\operatorname{row}_D(A_{h,c}),
\qquad
v_{s,a,D,h}=\operatorname{row}_D(H_h),
\]
and an independently checkable certificate \(\pi_h\) that \(H_{s,a,D,h}>0\) on the declared fiber.  The returned kernel entry is the typed expression
\[
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=
\operatorname{Quot}(N_{s,a,D,h,c},H_{s,a,D,h},\pi_h).
\]
The record \(\kappa\) contains only the event and expression derivations, locality tables, constructed rows, and positivity certificates.  It contains neither \(N=r^{\mathsf T}q\), nor \(H=v^{\mathsf T}q\), nor any equivalent semantic equality.  An unavailable cell, undefined fixing, rejected locality table, or uncertified denominator has no successful judgment and creates no row-eligibility record.

assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.

node.statement:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow \mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
Together with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\Longrightarrow\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), this gives the convenient hierarchy
\[
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow \mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
The second implication is strict on finite original alphabets: there is a three-vertex binary DAG and a complete target-domain menu for which \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds but \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) fails because two Boolean focal slices outside \(R_D(m_D)\) average to a row inside it under the witnessing nonfocal product law.
node.justification: This hierarchy makes the sharp single-baseline preservation premise explicit while retaining two increasingly simple sufficient checks.
node.gap: Pointwise active-slice control is stronger than the fixed-baseline construction needs because only averages under the frozen nonfocal product law enter complete-cell probabilities.
node.consumer: The focal projection theorem and its identification, dominance, frontier, and global corollaries use baseline-averaged separation for exact lifting.
node.proof_tex:
Choose \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\).  District factorization gives the finite nonfocal product law \(\nu_{-D}^{0,s}\).  Under \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), every focal slice lies in the linear space \(R_D(m_D)\), so
\[
\bar\chi_C^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C,\omega_{-D}}
\in R_D(m_D).
\tag{1}
\]
The same baseline works for every cell and domain, proving \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\).  Composition with the structural-separation lemma gives the full hierarchy.

For strictness, take independent fair binary roots \(X,Z\) feeding the deterministic binary child \(Y=\mathbf 1\{X=Z\}\), and let \(D=\{X\}\).  Supply only the complete target-domain output law of \(Y\).  Then \(A_D=\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) and
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{(1,1)\}.
\]
The two focal slices of \(\{Y=1\}\) are \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\), so active-slice separation fails.  Their average under the fair nonfocal law of \(Z\) is \((1/2,1/2)\in R_D(m_D)\); the complementary output cell is analogous.  Focal saturation permits every law of \(X\) while the fair law of \(Z\) and the structural table of \(Y\) stay fixed, so this single compatible baseline proves \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\).  Thus the second implication is strict on the original binary alphabets.

thm:finite-layer3-acquisition-obstructio.proof_tex:
Fix a finite checked instance satisfying the hypotheses and fix
\(S\subseteq\mathcal U\).  Joint realizability and
\(\mathrm{def:regime\text{-}block\text{-}acquisition}\) give
\[
\varnothing\ne\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}
\subseteq\mathcal K_S\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\tag{1}
\]
The checked-local-arms record gives the two separate conditions
\(\varepsilon_D>0\) and
\[
d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D
\qquad(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)).
\tag{2}
\]
Thus division is legal throughout every subface in \((1)\), and for any two arms
\[
Q_\rho(q)\geq Q_\sigma(q)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q}{d_D^{\mathsf T}q}
\geq
\frac{n_{\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q}{d_D^{\mathsf T}q}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(n_{\rho,D}-n_{\sigma,D})^{\mathsf T}q\geq0.
\tag{3}
\]
The last step multiplies by the common strictly positive denominator from \((2)\);
it does not define the causal conditional by its numerator.

For a fixed arm, the membership test is exactly
\[
\rho\in\operatorname{PO}(S)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists q\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}\quad
\begin{cases}
q(\omega)\geq0,&\omega\in\Omega_D,\\
A_Dq=m_D,\\
R_eq=p_e,&e\in S,\\
(n_{\rho,D}-n_{\sigma,D})^{\mathsf T}q\geq0,
&\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}.
\end{cases}
\tag{4}
\]
This is a finite linear feasibility problem.  Its feasible set is closed and bounded
because \(A_D\) contains the normalization row with value one.  If it is nonempty,
successively minimizing its finitely many coordinates on the current compact face
produces a singleton face, hence an extreme point.  At an extreme point the equality
rows together with some active inequalities have full column rank: otherwise a
nonzero vector orthogonal to all active rows would allow sufficiently small
movements in both signs while preserving every equality and inequality, contradicting
extremality.  Enumerate the finitely many full-rank active-row subsets.  Gaussian
elimination gives the unique candidate for each subset, and exact sign tests verify
the remaining inequalities.  Effective rational or real-algebraic arithmetic makes
all rank, equality and sign decisions exact.  Hence \((4)\) is computable without a
limit or numerical tolerance.

There are finitely many pairs \((S,\rho)\).  Computing each test \((4)\) determines
every \(\operatorname{PO}(S)\), including
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U)\).  Exact finite cost
comparison then retains all subsets satisfying the equality constraint and having
minimum total cost, including all ties.  This proves the general characterization.

For the obstruction, consider the one-domain binary bow graph on
\(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\) and \(Y\), with
\(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\leftrightarrow Y\).  It is acyclic
and has one district \(D=\{T_{\mathrm{tr}},Y\}\).  A deterministic district profile
is
\[
\omega=(t^{\mathrm{nat}},Y_0,Y_1)\in\{0,1\}^3.
\tag{5}
\]
Supply the complete observational law
\[
P(T_{\mathrm{tr}}=0)=1,
\qquad P(T_{\mathrm{tr}}=1)=0.
\tag{6}
\]
The corresponding raw rows and nonnegativity force zero mass on profiles with
\(t^{\mathrm{nat}}=1\) and impose no restriction on the four active profiles
\[
\omega_1=(0,0,0),\quad
\omega_2=(0,0,1),\quad
\omega_3=(0,1,0),\quad
\omega_4=(0,1,1).
\tag{7}
\]
Thus the base face is the simplex spanned by their four point masses.

This entire face is realizable on the declared binary alphabets.  Given any law
\(q\) on \((7)\), take one finite district latent block \(U_D\sim q\), set
\(T_{\mathrm{tr}}=t^{\mathrm{nat}}(U_D)\), and set
\(Y=Y_{T_{\mathrm{tr}}}(U_D)\); under intervention
\(T_{\mathrm{tr}}=t\), the latter equation returns \(Y_t(U_D)\).  The shared block
is compatible with the bidirected edge and the last equation with the directed edge.
There is one domain, so no transport equality remains to check.  Equivalently, all
cells are local to the only district; nonemptiness and
\(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\) realize every
boundary point as an original-alphabet focal-saturated SCM.

Let \(E=\top\) and take the two arm reward events
\[
B_\rho=\{(Y_0,Y_1)\ne(1,1)\},
\qquad
B_\sigma=\{(Y_0,Y_1)=(1,1)\}.
\tag{8}
\]
On the active profiles, their numerator and evidence rows are
\[
n_{\rho,D}=(1,1,1,0),\qquad
n_{\sigma,D}=(0,0,0,1),\qquad
d_D=(1,1,1,1).
\tag{9}
\]
Thus \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q=1\) and \(\varepsilon_D=1\) is a valid checked lower
bound; zero evidence is impossible.

Let \(\mathcal U=\{e_1,e_2\}\) with unit costs.  Experiment \(e_i\) declares the
Layer-3 tuple \((Y_0,Y_1)\), applies respectively the Boolean postprocessors
\[
F_1=\mathbf1\{Y_0=Y_1\},
\qquad
F_2=\mathbf1\{(Y_0,Y_1)\ne(0,0)\},
\tag{10}
\]
and reveals the complete laws \(P(F_i=1)=1\) and \(P(F_i=0)=0\).  These are
complete Boolean pushforwards, not a disclosure of the unsupplied joint tuple law.
Their output-one rows on \((7)\) are
\[
r_1=(1,0,0,1),
\qquad
r_2=(0,1,1,1),
\tag{11}
\]
and their output-zero rows are the complements.  Normalization makes each complement
equation exactly redundant with the corresponding output-one equation.  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal K_{\varnothing}
 &=\operatorname{conv}\{\delta_{\omega_1},\delta_{\omega_2},
     \delta_{\omega_3},\delta_{\omega_4}\},\\
\mathcal K_{\{e_1\}}
 &=\operatorname{conv}\{\delta_{\omega_1},\delta_{\omega_4}\},\\
\mathcal K_{\{e_2\}}
 &=\operatorname{conv}\{\delta_{\omega_2},\delta_{\omega_3},
     \delta_{\omega_4}\},\\
\mathcal K_{\{e_1,e_2\}}
 &=\{\delta_{\omega_4}\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
The last point mass realizes both complete experiment laws, proving joint
realizability.  By \((9)\), each of
\(\delta_{\omega_1},\delta_{\omega_2},\delta_{\omega_3}\) makes \(\rho\) uniquely
optimal, while \(\delta_{\omega_4}\) makes \(\sigma\) uniquely optimal.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})=
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
\qquad
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=\{\sigma\}.
\tag{13}
\]
It follows that
\[
f(\{e_2\})-f(\varnothing)=0
<1=f(\{e_1,e_2\})-f(\{e_1\}),
\tag{14}
\]
which violates diminishing returns at \(S=\varnothing\),
\(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), and \(e=e_2\).

Finally, \((13)\) says that a subset preserves the full-information possibly-optimal
set if and only if it contains both experiments.  With
\(x_i=\mathbf1\{e_i\in S\}\), the exact problem is
\[
\min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2.
\tag{15}
\]
Its unique feasible binary point is \((1,1)\).  For the continuous relaxation, the
nonnegative multiplier \(y=1\) on the covering inequality proves
\(x_1+x_2\geq2y=2\), and \((1,1)\) attains this lower bound.  This is the claimed
matching certificate.

snapshot.stmt:
For every finite \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) instance with a finite experiment set \(\mathcal U\), effectively rational or real-algebraic rows, menu values, and positive costs, and a jointly realizable complete experiment menu \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}\ne\varnothing\), all minimum-cost Layer-3 regime-block solutions are characterized by enumerating \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\) and, for each arm, solving the finite linear feasibility problem defining \(\operatorname{PO}(S)\).  In general the elimination function \(f\) is not submodular.  In particular, there is a realizable one-domain binary one-district checked instance with two unit-cost experiments, each revealing one complete Boolean postprocessed Layer-3 output law, for which
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
\qquad
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]
Thus the marginal gain of \(e_2\) is zero at \(S=\varnothing\) and one at \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), violating diminishing returns.  For this instance the exact acquisition problem is
\[
\min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2,
\]
with unique solution \((1,1)\) and cost two; the multiplier \(y=1\) for the covering inequality certifies the matching lower bound for its continuous relaxation.

defs.def:district-response-profile: For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), set \(\Omega_D=\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\), the finite set of all tuples \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) of deterministic response maps at every parent configuration allowed by \(G\) and \(\mathcal X\).  For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\) is the joint law of the response maps induced by \(M^s\).  The carrier is query independent and includes every configuration needed by any target, menu, deterministic postprocessor, or later acquired regime.
defs.def:regime-block-acquisition:
Fix a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record.  Each \(e\in\mathcal U\) is a realizable finite block of typed descriptors, possibly with deterministic finite postprocessing.  Acquiring \(e\) reveals the complete finite law of every declared output, including every normalization-dependent complementary cell, equivalently a dependent row-value block \((R_e,p_e)\), at cost \(c_e>0\).  Require joint realizability of the whole experiment menu:
\[
\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}
=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal U\}
\ne\varnothing.
\]
For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define
\[
\mathcal K_S
=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\}.
\]
The checked lower bound \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D>0\) persists on every subface.  Hence every local subset is uniformly positive before acquisition, no subset-specific evidence screen is needed, and one may define the local row-face possibly optimal set by
\[
\operatorname{PO}(S)
=\left\{\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}:
\exists q\in\mathcal K_S\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ 
(n_{\rho,D}-n_{\sigma,D})^{\mathsf T}q\geq0\right\}.
\]
Finally set
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),
\qquad
f(S)=|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|-|\operatorname{PO}(S)|,
\]
and define the local ex-post acquisition problem by
\[
\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}.
\]
This construction is the computationally cheap district row-face layer and is the uniformly-positive special case of subset-screened global acquisition.  It does not declare \(\mathcal K_S\) to be the exact projection of the broad multi-district compatibility fiber: that equality requires the separately stated augmented focal-saturation and baseline-averaged separation hypotheses.
defs.def:target-arm-rows:
For a fixed district \(D\), a total record \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) consists of: a finite nonempty arm set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); for every \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(B_\rho\cap E)\) trace and its constructed row \(n_{\rho,D}\); one accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(E)\) trace and its constructed row \(d_D\); a rational or real-algebraic number \(\varepsilon_D>0\); and an exact certificate that
\[
d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D
\qquad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Only from such a record define, for \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\),
\[
Q_\rho(q)=\frac{n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q}{d_D^{\mathsf T}q},
\qquad
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}.
\]
Separately, for any target cell \(C\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) trace constructs the generic target row \(b_D=\operatorname{row}_D(C)\).  If a required locality trace rejects, the corresponding row, comparison, or target value is undefined rather than silently assigned a row.

\mathcal K_{\{e_2\}}
 &=\operatorname{conv}\{\delta_{\omega_2},\delta_{\omega_3},
     \delta_{\omega_4}\},\\
\mathcal K_{\{e_1,e_2\}}
 &=\{\delta_{\omega_4}\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
The last point mass realizes both complete experiment laws, proving joint
realizability.  By \((9)\), each of
\(\delta_{\omega_1},\delta_{\omega_2},\delta_{\omega_3}\) makes \(\rho\) uniquely
optimal, while \(\delta_{\omega_4}\) makes \(\sigma\) uniquely optimal.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})=
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
\qquad
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=\{\sigma\}.
\tag{13}
\]
It follows that
\[
f(\{e_2\})-f(\varnothing)=0
<1=f(\{e_1,e_2\})-f(\{e_1\}),
\tag{14}
\]
which violates diminishing returns at \(S=\varnothing\),
\(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), and \(e=e_2\).

Finally, \((13)\) says that a subset preserves the full-information possibly-optimal
set if and only if it contains both experiments.  With
\(x_i=\mathbf1\{e_i\in S\}\), the exact problem is
\[
\min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2.
\tag{15}
\]
Its unique feasible binary point is \((1,1)\).  For the continuous relaxation, the
nonnegative multiplier \(y=1\) on the covering inequality proves
\(x_1+x_2\geq2y=2\), and \((1,1)\) attains this lower bound.  This is the claimed
matching certificate.

thm:exact-global-canonical-frontier.proof_tex:
For a saturated compatible family, Assumptions
\(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\) and
\(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\), together with finite total
probability, give for every counterfactual cell \(C\)
\[
P_{M^s}(C)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_D\Omega_D}
\mathbf1_C(\omega)\prod_Dq_D^s(\omega_D)
=\Psi_C^s(\theta^s).
\tag{1}
\]
For a supplied postprocessed output cell,
\(\mathrm{ass:typed\text{-}menu\text{-}realizability}\) gives
\[
P_a^s(y)=\mathcal L_{M^s}(f_a(T_a))(y)
=P_{M^s}\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The deterministic preimage identity evaluates the indicator in \((1)\); it does
not create unsupplied tuple-cell probabilities.  Assumption
\(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\) supplies every equality
\(q_D^s=q_D^\star\) when \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and
\(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}closure}\) makes this an entire-district status.
Consequently the response-law tuple induced by any family in
\(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\) belongs to
\(\Theta(\mathcal P)\).

Conversely, let \(\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\).  For every pair \((s,D)\), take
one finite latent block with carrier \(\Omega_D\) and law \(q_D^s\); make these
blocks independent across original districts and let every structural equation read
its stored deterministic response map.  The observed state spaces remain exactly
\(\mathcal X\), and acyclicity gives unique recursive evaluation.  The second line
of equation \((2)\) in
\(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}fiber}\) imposes all
unchanged-district equalities, while its last line and \((2)\) above impose every
complete menu law.  Hence the family lies in
\(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\), and \((1)\) gives all target cells in
\(\mathcal F\) simultaneously.  This proves the first joint range equality.  Each
summand in \((1)\) uses at most one coordinate of each visited district law, proving
multi-affinity and the stated degree bound.

For arbitrary \(G\), apply
\(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}canonical\text{-}counterfactual\text{-}equivalence}\)
in every domain to the finite joint family of complete response-table
counterfactuals, all supplied cells, and all cells in \(\mathcal F\).  Use the
response-type encoding itself, so an unchanged source district and its target copy
use the same encoding map.  The canonical family preserves all supplied and target
joint counterfactual laws and all required response-law equalities, and therefore
defines a point of \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\).  Conversely, a point of
that fiber consists of one-hot recursive tables, canonical exogenous probability
vectors, every graph-compatible within-district latent restriction, independence
across original districts, all cross-domain response-law equalities, and all
complete menu equations.  Reading these coordinates as an SCM family produces an
element of \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) on the original alphabets, and recursive
evaluation gives \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s\).  This proves the sparse canonical
joint range equality.

Both parameter fibers are closed subsets of a finite product of compact probability
simplices and finite one-hot table sets; hence they are compact.  Their constraints
are finite polynomial sign conditions, so they are semialgebraic.  The corresponding
compatibility hypothesis gives nonemptiness.  Fix either exact row
\((\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)\) in the theorem.  Continuity on compact \(\Lambda\)
gives attained extrema
\[
\ell_T=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
u_T=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star).
\tag{3}
\]
Joint range equality turns \((3)\) into sharp causal bounds and turns their
optimizers into original-alphabet compatible endpoint models.  The target is
identified exactly when \(\ell_T=u_T\).  If they differ, the endpoint models have
unequal target values.  Since probabilities lie in \([0,1]\), a strict improvement
over at least one logical endpoint occurs exactly when \(\ell_T>0\) or \(u_T<1\).
No connectedness premise was used, so no interval-filling conclusion is available.

Apply the same compactness argument to the nonnegative evidence polynomial:
\[
e_-:=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+:=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\tag{4}
\]
The exhaustive cases are
\[
e_+=0,
\qquad
e_-=0<e_+,
\qquad
e_->0.
\tag{5}
\]
They mean, respectively, uniform zero evidence, coexistence of zero and positive
evidence, and uniform strict positivity.  Division on the whole compatibility fiber
is valid only in the third case.  There the ratio is continuous on compact
\(\Lambda\), so it attains the displayed sharp conditional lower and upper bounds.
Moreover,
\[
Q_\sigma^\star-Q_\rho^\star
=\frac{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star-
\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star}{\Xi_E^\star}.
\tag{6}
\]
The denominator in \((6)\) is strictly positive.  Thus the conditional ordering has
exactly the sign of the numerator gap.  A continuous gap is positive everywhere on
compact \(\Lambda\) exactly when its attained minimum is positive; opposite strict
rankings occur exactly when its attained minimum is negative and its attained
maximum is positive.  This proves the safe-pruning characterizations.

Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:district\text{-}cell\text{-}linearity}\) maps every broad
compatible focal law into \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\).  The exact focal equality, the
identity
\[
R_D(m_D)=
\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp},
\tag{7}
\]
the single-baseline preservation calculation, and the realization of every boundary
point are exactly
\(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\).  Lemmas
\(\mathrm{lem:active\text{-}slice\text{-}implies\text{-}baseline\text{-}averaged}\)
and
\(\mathrm{lem:structural\text{-}separation\text{-}implies\text{-}active\text{-}slice}\)
give the two baseline-free sufficient conditions.  The global programs retain every
cross-district polynomial equation; no row-face equality is inferred outside the
focal theorem's hypotheses.  Therefore only distinct optimizers of an exact global
program, or a local face witness under the exact focal projection theorem, produce
the claimed same-menu paired-model certificate.

snapshot.stmt:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
If \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the one-district fiber-projection theorem gives the exact local equality
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\]
and \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) itself entails a nonempty focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber. This equality requires saturation only of the focal district and preserves the graph-compatible restrictions of every \(D'\ne D\). Cross-district coupling of a complete supplied cell is harmless for the fixed-baseline replacement exactly when its baseline-averaged focal row lies in \(R_D(m_D)\), because
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}.
\]
Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is a baseline-free sufficient certificate for this equality. The baseline-averaged predicate is generally baseline-dependent and not directly checkable from menu cells alone; allowing a different baseline for each candidate \(q\) is not asserted. Outside focal-district saturation and baseline-averaged separation, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is certified only as an outer relaxation. This local equality is distinct from the first, all-district-saturated global row, whose Cartesian district variation makes the multi-affine program exact. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside the focal projection theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.

defs.def:active-slice-separated-menu:
For a fixed district \(D\), define its active row space by
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\subseteq\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
For a complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and for
\(\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'}\), define its focal recursive-indicator slice by
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(\omega_D)
=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
The active-slice face-separation predicate \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell and every fixed nonfocal response profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  When \(D\) is the only district, the nonfocal product is the singleton empty profile.
defs.def:baseline-averaged-active-slice-menu:
Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\).  For a baseline \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), let
\[
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
=\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}q_{D'}^{0,s}(\omega_{D'}),
\qquad
\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\]
where \(q_{D'}^{0,s}\) is the response-profile law induced by \(M^{0,s}\).  For every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), define the baseline-averaged focal row
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}
\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
The baseline-averaged active-slice predicate \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when there exists one \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) such that
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell.  The same witnessing baseline must be used for all cells and all feasible replacements of the focal law; a baseline depending on the replacement law is not permitted.
defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:compatible-face:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:district-saturated-model-class:
Define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete for every }D\in\mathcal D(G);\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ and }D\in\mathcal D(G),
\text{ exactly one finite latent block }U_D^s\text{ taking values in }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{stores one full deterministic response map for every vertex in }D
\text{ at every parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation in }D\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&(U_D^s:D\in\mathcal D(G))\text{ are mutually independent within each domain }s;\\
&\text{the class contains every independent choice of one probability law on }
\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ for each permitted district block},\\
&\text{subject only to equality of the laws of }U_D^s\text{ and }U_D^\star
\text{ whenever }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus changed districts may use arbitrary and mutually unrelated response-block laws, unchanged districts use exactly the target response-block law, and no equality with the broad sparse-ADMG class \(\mathfrak M\) is asserted.
defs.def:district-separated-menu: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\).  This is a finite syntactic and tabular condition; it excludes an unrecorded cross-district polynomial constraint involving \(q_D^\star\).
defs.def:exact-global-canonical-fiber:
Use the complete query-independent carriers \(\Omega_D=\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\).  For \(\theta=(q_D^s:s\in\mathcal S,D\in\mathcal D(G))\), define
\[
\Psi_C^s(\theta^s)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\tag{1}
\]
If the indicator visits \(k\) districts, \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district-law blocks and has total degree at most \(k\).  For descriptor \(a\) and output \(y\in\mathcal Y_a\), let
\[
C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its indicator in \((1)\) is evaluated by the finite deterministic preimage, while its menu value is directly \(P_a^s(y)\).  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta:{}&
q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S,D\in\mathcal D(G)),\\
&q_D^s=q_D^\star
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Psi_{C_{a,y}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(y)
\quad\text{for every }s,a,y\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\tag{2}
\]
For a target cell \(T\), set
\[
L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\qquad
U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]
and
\[
\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)=
\Psi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)
-\Psi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star).
\]

For an arbitrary, possibly nonsaturated ADMG \(G\), let \(\vartheta^s=(\mu^s,p^s)\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\).  Its canonical coordinates satisfy
\[
p_U^s(u)\geq0,\quad\sum_up_U^s(u)=1,
\quad \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s\in\{0,1\},
\quad \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s=1,
\]
together with every graph-compatible within-district latent-factor restriction and independence across original districts.  Let \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)\) be the polynomial obtained by finite recursive evaluation and let \(q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)\) be the induced complete district response law.  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\vartheta:{}&
\vartheta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
&q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)
=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Phi_{C_{a,y},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(y)
\quad\text{for every complete supplied output cell}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\tag{3}
\]
Every occurrence of \(\mathcal P\) in \((2)\)--\((3)\) denotes the current complete typed-menu argument, whether it is the base menu or a finite complete-menu augmentation.  Every newly disclosed output cell, including every complementary cell of its finite output law, is imposed simultaneously; no base-menu equation and no complete cell rejected by a local row checker is discarded.  Neither fiber definition presupposes positivity of an evidence event.  The fiber in \((2)\) has district-saturated response-block semantics.  The fiber in \((3)\) retains all internal graph-compatible restrictions of the sparse ADMG.
defs.def:focal-district-saturated-model-class:
For a fixed district \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete};\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ there is exactly one finite latent block }
U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{storing one full deterministic response map for each vertex in }D
\text{ at every allowed parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation of a vertex in }D
\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&U_D^s\text{ is independent of the exogenous blocks of every }D'\ne D;\\
&\text{every probability law on }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ is permitted for }U_D^s,
\text{ subject only to equality with the target law}\\
&\text{when }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing;\\
&\text{for each }D'\ne D\text{, all structural tables, latent-factor restrictions,}
\text{ and cross-domain equalities remain those of }\mathfrak M
\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The phrase ``every probability law is permitted'' includes closure under replacing the law of \(U_D^\star\) and all its unchanged-source copies while holding all mechanisms and latent laws in districts \(D'\ne D\), and all changed-source copies of \(U_D\), fixed. Define
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]
defs.def:saturated-compatibility-fiber:
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}).
\]

assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability:
For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), descriptor \(a\) declares a finite counterfactual tuple \(T_a\), a finite output alphabet \(\mathcal Y_a\), and a deterministic map \(f_a\) into \(\mathcal Y_a\), and
\[
P_a^s=(f_a)_\#\mathcal L_{M^s}(T_a),
\]
where an unpostprocessed descriptor has the identity output map.

node.statement:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
