are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
If \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the one-district fiber-projection theorem gives the exact local equality
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\]
and \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) itself entails a nonempty focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber. This equality requires saturation only of the focal district and preserves the graph-compatible restrictions of every \(D'\ne D\). Cross-district coupling of a complete supplied cell is harmless for the fixed-baseline replacement exactly when its baseline-averaged focal row lies in \(R_D(m_D)\), because
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}.
\]
Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is a baseline-free sufficient certificate for this equality. The baseline-averaged predicate is generally baseline-dependent and not directly checkable from menu cells alone; allowing a different baseline for each candidate \(q\) is not asserted. Outside focal-district saturation and baseline-averaged separation, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is certified only as an outer relaxation. This local equality is distinct from the first, all-district-saturated global row, whose Cartesian district variation makes the multi-affine program exact. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside the focal projection theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.
node.justification: The theorem separates exact all-district multi-affine variation, exact sparse canonical optimization, and exact single-baseline focal-district geometry.
node.gap: Global programs retain every cross-district polynomial equality; locally, a weaker baseline-averaged condition preserves those cells than pointwise active-slice control.
node.consumer: Global bounds and pruning use exact endpoint optimizers, while local LP certificates use focal saturation plus baseline-averaged separation or its baseline-free sufficient checks.
node.proof_tex:
For a saturated compatible family, Assumptions
\(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\) and
\(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\), together with finite total
probability, give for every counterfactual cell \(C\)
\[
P_{M^s}(C)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_D\Omega_D}
\mathbf1_C(\omega)\prod_Dq_D^s(\omega_D)
=\Psi_C^s(\theta^s).
\tag{1}
\]
For a supplied postprocessed output cell,
\(\mathrm{ass:typed\text{-}menu\text{-}realizability}\) gives
\[
P_a^s(y)=\mathcal L_{M^s}(f_a(T_a))(y)
=P_{M^s}\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The deterministic preimage identity evaluates the indicator in \((1)\); it does
not create unsupplied tuple-cell probabilities.  Assumption
\(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\) supplies every equality
\(q_D^s=q_D^\star\) when \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and
\(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}closure}\) makes this an entire-district status.
Consequently the response-law tuple induced by any family in
\(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\) belongs to
\(\Theta(\mathcal P)\).

Conversely, let \(\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\).  For every pair \((s,D)\), take
one finite latent block with carrier \(\Omega_D\) and law \(q_D^s\); make these
blocks independent across original districts and let every structural equation read
its stored deterministic response map.  The observed state spaces remain exactly
\(\mathcal X\), and acyclicity gives unique recursive evaluation.  The second line
of equation \((2)\) in
\(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}fiber}\) imposes all
unchanged-district equalities, while its last line and \((2)\) above impose every
complete menu law.  Hence the family lies in
\(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\), and \((1)\) gives all target cells in
\(\mathcal F\) simultaneously.  This proves the first joint range equality.  Each
summand in \((1)\) uses at most one coordinate of each visited district law, proving
multi-affinity and the stated degree bound.

For arbitrary \(G\), apply
\(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}canonical\text{-}counterfactual\text{-}equivalence}\)
in every domain to the finite joint family of complete response-table
counterfactuals, all supplied cells, and all cells in \(\mathcal F\).  Use the
response-type encoding itself, so an unchanged source district and its target copy
use the same encoding map.  The canonical family preserves all supplied and target
joint counterfactual laws and all required response-law equalities, and therefore
defines a point of \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\).  Conversely, a point of
that fiber consists of one-hot recursive tables, canonical exogenous probability
vectors, every graph-compatible within-district latent restriction, independence
across original districts, all cross-domain response-law equalities, and all
complete menu equations.  Reading these coordinates as an SCM family produces an
element of \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) on the original alphabets, and recursive
evaluation gives \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s\).  This proves the sparse canonical
joint range equality.

Both parameter fibers are closed subsets of a finite product of compact probability
simplices and finite one-hot table sets; hence they are compact.  Their constraints
are finite polynomial sign conditions, so they are semialgebraic.  The corresponding
compatibility hypothesis gives nonemptiness.  Fix either exact row
\((\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)\) in the theorem.  Continuity on compact \(\Lambda\)
gives attained extrema
\[
\ell_T=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
u_T=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star).
\tag{3}
\]
Joint range equality turns \((3)\) into sharp causal bounds and turns their
optimizers into original-alphabet compatible endpoint models.  The target is
identified exactly when \(\ell_T=u_T\).  If they differ, the endpoint models have
unequal target values.  Since probabilities lie in \([0,1]\), a strict improvement
over at least one logical endpoint occurs exactly when \(\ell_T>0\) or \(u_T<1\).
No connectedness premise was used, so no interval-filling conclusion is available.

Apply the same compactness argument to the nonnegative evidence polynomial:
\[
e_-:=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+:=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\tag{4}
\]
The exhaustive cases are
\[
e_+=0,
\qquad
e_-=0<e_+,
\qquad
e_->0.
\tag{5}
\]
They mean, respectively, uniform zero evidence, coexistence of zero and positive
evidence, and uniform strict positivity.  Division on the whole compatibility fiber
is valid only in the third case.  There the ratio is continuous on compact
\(\Lambda\), so it attains the displayed sharp conditional lower and upper bounds.
Moreover,
\[
Q_\sigma^\star-Q_\rho^\star
=\frac{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star-
\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star}{\Xi_E^\star}.
\tag{6}
\]
The denominator in \((6)\) is strictly positive.  Thus the conditional ordering has
exactly the sign of the numerator gap.  A continuous gap is positive everywhere on
compact \(\Lambda\) exactly when its attained minimum is positive; opposite strict
rankings occur exactly when its attained minimum is negative and its attained
maximum is positive.  This proves the safe-pruning characterizations.

Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:district\text{-}cell\text{-}linearity}\) maps every broad
compatible focal law into \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\).  The exact focal equality, the
identity
\[
R_D(m_D)=
\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp},
\tag{7}
\]
the single-baseline preservation calculation, and the realization of every boundary
point are exactly
\(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\).  Lemmas
\(\mathrm{lem:active\text{-}slice\text{-}implies\text{-}baseline\text{-}averaged}\)
and
\(\mathrm{lem:structural\text{-}separation\text{-}implies\text{-}active\text{-}slice}\)
give the two baseline-free sufficient conditions.  The global programs retain every
cross-district polynomial equation; no row-face equality is inferred outside the
focal theorem's hypotheses.  Therefore only distinct optimizers of an exact global
program, or a local face witness under the exact focal projection theorem, produce
the claimed same-menu paired-model certificate.

thm:hybrid-fixed-alphabet-completeness.proof_tex:
Run \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) first.  By
\(\mathrm{thm:recursion\text{-}soundness}\), the run terminates uniquely.  If it
returns an identifying expression \(F\), that theorem gives, according to the query
type,
\[
F(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(T)
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
F(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\mid E)
\tag{1}
\]
for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), with every quotient protected by
its stored nonzero or positive certificate.  Definition
\(\mathrm{def:allowed\text{-}rational\text{-}functional}\) gives
\(F\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\).  This proves the fast path.

Every other local terminal invokes
\[
S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathbb R^N.
\tag{2}
\]
The assumed nonempty broad compatibility fiber and
\(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}frontier}\) imply that
\(S\) is nonempty, compact and real semialgebraic and that its joint target-cell
ranges equal those of the broad original-alphabet compatibility fiber.  The
effective presentations of the supplied rational or real-algebraic cells give exact
arithmetic and sign comparison in their ordered coefficient ring \(\mathbb D\), and
the stipulated ordered embedding into \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) represents the
coefficients without restricting the variables in \((2)\).

Let \(K\) be any real-closed field containing an ordered copy of \(\mathbb D\).
Apply
\(\mathrm{lem:basu\text{-}mohammad\text{-}nezhad\text{-}quantifier\text{-}elimination}\)
over \(K\).  Its algorithm terminates and performs only exact coefficient-ring
operations.  Hence the same finite \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) syntax is equivalent to
the defining formula in every such \(K\), in particular in the ordinary real field.

For an unconditional target put \(p_T=\Phi_{T,\mathrm{can}}^\star\).  Quantifier
elimination applied to
\[
\varphi_T(t)=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge t-p_T(x)=0]
\tag{3}
\]
returns \(\chi_T\) such that, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\chi_T(t)
\Longleftrightarrow
\exists x\in S\;t=p_T(x)
\Longleftrightarrow
\exists\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\;
t=P_{M^\star}(T).
\tag{4}
\]
The second equivalence is exact global joint range equality.  Eliminating the closed
sentence asserting two distinct realizations decides identification exactly.
Continuity on compact \(S\) gives an attained minimum \(\ell_T\) and maximum
\(u_T\).  Therefore
\[
\chi_T(\ell)\wedge
\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow\ell\leq t]
\tag{5}
\]
holds over \(\mathbb R\) exactly for \(\ell=\ell_T\), and the reversed inequality
does the same for \(u_T\).  Quantifier elimination preserves these real
equivalences; it does not require the endpoints or all range points to be algebraic.

For a conditional target set
\[
e(x)=\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(x),
\qquad
n(x)=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(x).
\tag{6}
\]
Probability semantics gives \(e\geq0\) on nonempty \(S\).  Exactly one of
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf Z:&\neg\exists x\in S\;e(x)>0,\\
\mathsf N:&(\exists x\in S\;e(x)=0)\wedge
(\exists x\in S\;e(x)>0),\\
\mathsf P:&\neg\exists x\in S\;e(x)=0
\end{array}
\tag{7}
\]
holds.  The cited quantifier-elimination theorem and exact evaluation of the closed
outputs therefore give the prescribed payload-free status in the first two cases.
Under \(\mathsf Z\), evidence vanishes throughout.  Under \(\mathsf N\), the
conditional is undefined at one compatible law and defined at another, so a
functional on the full fiber must reject division.  Under \(\mathsf P\), continuity
and compactness give
\[
\min_{x\in S}e(x)>0.
\tag{8}
\]
Only then is \(e(x)t-n(x)=0\) equivalent to \(t=n(x)/e(x)\).  Consequently the real
realization of
\[
\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0\wedge e(x)t-n(x)=0]
\tag{9}
\]
is exactly the conditional causal range.  The ratio is continuous by \((8)\), so
the same compactness and endpoint argument as in \((5)\) gives its attained real
extrema, and the closed two-value sentence gives its exact singleton decision.

Only finitely many terminating calls are made.  If either real range is not a
singleton, two distinct attained values exist, and exact canonical range equality
supplies two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families realizing them.  This is an
existence certificate, not witness extraction: the procedure returns no endpoint
number, algebraic sample, cylindrical decomposition trace, canonical parameter, or
paired SCM.  Since every interpretation above is over \(\mathbb R\), no causal
range point was restricted to \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).

snapshot.stmt: Assume \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and every supplied output-cell probability is effectively rational or real algebraic.  Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring they generate, with its effective embedding into \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) for coefficient representation and exact arithmetic.  The \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) outputs of \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) are equivalent to their defining first-order formulas in every real-closed field extension containing \(\mathbb D\), and in particular their realizations over the ordinary real field \(\mathbb R\) are used for the causal conclusions.  For either an unconditional finite target-domain counterfactual cell \(T\) or the conditional query \(Q_\rho^\star=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\mid E)\), the algorithm terminates and returns a \(\mathsf{HybridResult}\).  A fast-path \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)\) has \(F\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) and equals the causal query throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  Otherwise, for the real canonical fiber \(S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\), the fallback returns quantifier-free formulas whose real realizations are exactly the full target range and its attained lower and upper endpoints, together with an exact singleton decision.  For an unconditional target it returns \(\operatorname{UNCOND\_QE}\), and identification holds exactly when the real range is a singleton.  For a conditional target it evaluates the closed sentences \(\mathsf Z\), \(\mathsf N\), and \(\mathsf P\) from \(\mathrm{def:hybrid\text{-}result\text{-}grammar}\): it returns the payload-free terminal \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE\_QE}\) exactly under \(\mathsf Z\), the payload-free terminal \(\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED\_QE}\) exactly under \(\mathsf N\), and only under \(\mathsf P\) forms the conditional real range and returns \(\operatorname{COND\_QE}\).  In the last case evidence is uniformly positive on \(S\), and identification holds exactly when the conditional real range is a singleton.  Exact operations in \(\mathbb D\) compute the output syntax and evaluate every closed quantifier-free decision.  A non-singleton real range implies, by exact canonical range equivalence, two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families with unequal target values; the algorithm is not claimed to output endpoint values, algebraic samples, canonical parameters, or paired SCMs.  A local face failure alone is never used as broad-model nonidentification, and no claim is made that all real range points are algebraic.

defs.def:allowed-rational-functional: The algebra \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) is generated by rational constants and the directly supplied complete output-cell probabilities \(P_a^s(y)\), including deterministic-pushforward output cells, under finite sums, differences, products, and marginalization sums.  It contains a quotient \(F/H\) only together with an independently checked certificate that \(H\ne0\) on the relevant compatibility fiber; a conditional causal output requires the stronger stored certificate \(H>0\) throughout that fiber.  A quantifier-free semialgebraic range or endpoint description returned by the canonical quantifier-elimination fallback is represented by \(\mathsf{HybridResult}\), not declared to belong to \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\).
defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:dctftr-recursion:
Initialize a finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_\rho\cap E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\).  The deterministic priority rules are \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\), and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\), using the rank from \(\mathrm{def:dctftr\text{-}grammar}\) and least-node tie breaking.

The normalization rule expands deterministic output cells only through the pointwise preimage identity and checks Boolean equality.  The ancestor rule records its complete finite marginalization identity.  At split, run \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) for every original district in canonical order.  An accepting trace creates \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\).  If no original district is local, splice the exact original-district expansion
\[
P_{M^\star}(C)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1_C(\omega)
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^\star(\omega_D)
\tag{1}
\]
as a finite sum-product DAG.  No factorization over districts newly formed by an induced subgraph is used.  An enumeration or typing failure returns its typed split failure.

At extraction, enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete supplied output cell, and constructive extraction record.  Retain a candidate only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  Retain a raw output-cell row only when its exhaustive locality table accepts, and retain every derived numerator and context row separately.  Never retain a conditional quotient as a row.  Prepend normalization, construct \((A_D,m_D)\) exactly as in \(\mathrm{def:stacked\text{-}menu\text{-}system}\), and replay the derivations to check each equality in \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\) literally.  Rejected candidates are recorded and remain constraints of the global canonical fiber.

At face identification, compute the forced-zero set by exact linear programming and accept only a checked representation
\[
b_D=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_D+
\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega.
\tag{2}
\]
It then resolves the node to \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}m_D\).  Failure of membership returns \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), whose witness concerns only the local row relaxation; when only normalization survives, the same failed face test is labelled \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\).  Ready sum and product rules use finite additivity and the original-district factorization in \((1)\).

Condition returns uniform zero evidence only with an independent certificate, divides only with an independent certificate of strict positivity throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), returns a displayed compatible zero-evidence model when available, and otherwise returns uncertified positivity.  In priority order, the first seven rules decrease respectively \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi\), fix every earlier coordinate, and create no earlier-phase node; condition decreases \(r_C\) only after the other coordinates vanish.  Every partial operation has its stated failure branch, so \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.
defs.def:dctftr-grammar:
Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, domains, descriptors, districts, assignments, complete response profiles, and generated work-DAG identifiers.  The counterfactual syntax is
\[
\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]V_\alpha=v,
\qquad
\mathsf{Event}::=\top\mid\bot\mid\mathsf{Atom}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},
\]
where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term.  A descriptor declares a finite returned counterfactual tuple \(T_a\), a finite output alphabet \(\mathcal Y_a\), and a deterministic map \(f_a\).  Its output cell is the event \(\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\); the parser uses the pointwise preimage identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\}
\tag{1}
\]
only for normalization, locality tables, and response-profile evaluation.  The expression leaf for this cell is the directly supplied number \(P_a^s(y)\), not a collection of unsupplied tuple-cell probabilities.  Normalized events are canonical disjoint normal forms of consistent unnested atoms, including contradiction and sure-event forms.

Identified expressions have grammar
\[
\mathsf{Expr}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\nu_H),
\]
where \(J\) is finite, \(r\in\mathbb Q\), and \(\nu_H\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate on the declared fiber.  The phase-indexed work-node grammar is
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{Goal}::={}&
\operatorname{Raw}(\tau,e)
\mid\operatorname{Normed}(\tau,e,\nu)
\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(\tau,H,e,\alpha)
\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\\
&\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(\tau,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)
\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),
\end{split}
\]
with \(\tau\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\) and an accepting locality trace \(\ell\) on every row-needed node.  A configuration \(\mathsf{Config}\) is a finite well-typed acyclic DAG of these nodes, two distinguished roots, and a checked transition trace.

For \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), raw, normalized, and ancestor-closed nodes denote their target-domain event probabilities.  A row or face node at \((D,b)\) denotes \(b^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\), a resolved node denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\), and sum and product nodes denote the finite sum and product of their children.  Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root denotations.  Normalization derivations check consistency, unnesting, \((1)\), and finite disjoint Boolean identities pointwise.  Ancestor derivations enumerate every marginalized assignment.  Split derivations expand over the original districts \(\mathcal D(G)\), never over districts newly formed in an induced subgraph.  Extraction derivations are finite \(\mathsf{XEvent}\)- and \(\mathsf{XExpr}\)-trees with exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) tables, separate numerator and context rows, and independent positivity certificates; they contain no semantic row equality.  A face node is well typed only after literal verification of every equation in \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\).  Its row-space and forced-zero certificates use exact rational or real-algebraic linear arithmetic.  Zero, nonzero, and strict-positivity certificates are independently checked rational identities, exact linear certificates, or displayed finite preordering identities; none may consist of the conclusion it certifies.

The terminals are
\[
\mathsf{Result}::=
\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)
\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t).
\]
Failure traces include ill-typed normalization or deterministic-preimage parsing, undefined original-district splitting, failed locality or extraction, \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\).  For a nonterminal configuration define
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}
=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi,r_C)\in\mathbb N^8,
\]
counting respectively raw, normalized, ancestor-closed, row-needed, face-needed, unresolved-sum, unresolved-product nodes, and one terminalization flag; every terminal has rank zero.
defs.def:stacked-menu-system:
Fix \(D\).  Enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete output cell, and extraction record canonically.  A candidate is transport admissible only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  First retain every admissible complete output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\) whose exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) table accepts, with row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}\) and supplied value \(P_a^s(y)\).  Next, for every successful extraction judgment retain separately the numerator pair
\[
(r_{s,a,D,h,c},N_{s,a,D,h,c})
\]
and the context pair
\[
(v_{s,a,D,h},H_{s,a,D,h}).
\]
Never stack the quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) as a linear row.  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) with value one and stack precisely the accepted raw, numerator, and context rows as \(A_D\), with their values in the same order as \(m_D\).  A failed locality, fixing, expression, positivity, or admissibility check contributes no row.  A rejected complete cell remains, without information loss, among the complete polynomial equalities of the exact global fiber.  For a deterministic postprocessor, recursive locality and the raw incidence row use the preimage identity \((1)\) from \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), but the stacked value is the directly supplied output probability \(P_a^s(y)\).
defs.def:finite-extraction-calculus:
The finite extraction calculus has event syntax
\[
\mathsf{XEvent}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\top\mid\bot\mid
\neg\mathsf{XEvent}\mid
\bigsqcup_{j\in J}\mathsf{XEvent}_j\mid
\operatorname{Marg}_{W}(\mathsf{XEvent})\mid
\operatorname{Fix}(\mathsf{FixTrace},\mathsf{XEvent}),
\]
where \(J\) and every marginalized alphabet are finite, and a disjoint-union node carries a complete pointwise disjointness table.  The cell event is
\[
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its probability leaf is the supplied output cell \(P_a^s(y)\).  Only its recursively evaluated indicator is expanded by the finite identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\};
\tag{1}
\]
the tuple-cell probabilities on the right of \((1)\) are not menu generators unless an identity-output tuple descriptor is separately supplied.

Menu expressions have syntax
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{XExpr}::={}&
\operatorname{CellProb}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j
\mid\mathsf{XExpr}-\mathsf{XExpr}
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j\\
&\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\pi_H),
\end{split}
\]
where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\pi_H\) is a separately checkable strict-positivity certificate on its declared compatibility fiber.  A derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) is generated only by an output-cell lookup, the truth-table identity \((1)\), contradiction or sure-event evaluation, finite disjoint additivity, complementation, finite marginalization, multiplication of independent original-district factors, and a checked fixing trace.

A fixing trace is a finite tree whose leaves are event or expression derivations and whose constructors are identity, typed substitution from a fixed finite registry of sound Boolean or fixing identities, finite disjoint sum, finite product, complement, marginalization, conditional quotient with a separately checked positive denominator, composition, and cleared-denominator comparison.  Every constructor stores all of its children and type data.  A comparison node is accepted only when cross-multiplication is legal under its stored denominator certificates and coefficient-by-coefficient normalization gives the zero polynomial.  The identity registry is finite and contains only pointwise Boolean identities, finite total-probability identities, and the fixing identities explicitly verified by recursive substitution of structural response tables.  Thus no constructor contains the semantic equality it is intended to establish.

Positivity certificates are either a positive rational constant after exact normalization, a rational Farkas identity for a linear face, or a displayed finite preordering identity
\[
p-\varepsilon=
\sum_i\tau_i h_i+
\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}\sigma_J
\prod_{j\in J}g_j,
\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
where the declared fiber has equations \(h_i=0\), inequalities \(g_j\geq0\), and every \(\sigma_J\) is checked coefficient by coefficient to be a finite sum of squares.  All polynomial equalities are checked by exact integer or rational coefficient comparison.

For an event \(A\) and a district \(D\), the total procedure \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) enumerates
\[
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\longmapsto
\mathbf 1\{A\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\}
\]
over the complete finite response carriers.  It accepts exactly when every two entries with the same \(\omega_D\) agree, and then returns their common row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\).  Otherwise it returns the first disagreeing pair in the canonical order.  All syntax trees, registries, coefficient vectors, truth tables, and searches are finite and canonically ordered.
defs.def:exact-global-canonical-fiber:
Use the complete query-independent carriers \(\Omega_D=\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\).  For \(\theta=(q_D^s:s\in\mathcal S,D\in\mathcal D(G))\), define
\[
\Psi_C^s(\theta^s)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\tag{1}
\]
If the indicator visits \(k\) districts, \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district-law blocks and has total degree at most \(k\).  For descriptor \(a\) and output \(y\in\mathcal Y_a\), let
\[
C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its indicator in \((1)\) is evaluated by the finite deterministic preimage, while its menu value is directly \(P_a^s(y)\).  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta:{}&
q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S,D\in\mathcal D(G)),\\
&q_D^s=q_D^\star
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Psi_{C_{a,y}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(y)
\quad\text{for every }s,a,y\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\tag{2}
\]
For a target cell \(T\), set
\[
L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\qquad
U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]
and
\[
\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)=
\Psi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)
-\Psi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star).
\]

For an arbitrary, possibly nonsaturated ADMG \(G\), let \(\vartheta^s=(\mu^s,p^s)\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\).  Its canonical coordinates satisfy
\[
p_U^s(u)\geq0,\quad\sum_up_U^s(u)=1,
\quad \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s\in\{0,1\},
\quad \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s=1,
\]
together with every graph-compatible within-district latent-factor restriction and independence across original districts.  Let \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)\) be the polynomial obtained by finite recursive evaluation and let \(q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)\) be the induced complete district response law.  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\vartheta:{}&
\vartheta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
&q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)
=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Phi_{C_{a,y},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(y)
\quad\text{for every complete supplied output cell}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\tag{3}
\]
Every occurrence of \(\mathcal P\) in \((2)\)--\((3)\) denotes the current complete typed-menu argument, whether it is the base menu or a finite complete-menu augmentation.  Every newly disclosed output cell, including every complementary cell of its finite output law, is imposed simultaneously; no base-menu equation and no complete cell rejected by a local row checker is discarded.  Neither fiber definition presupposes positivity of an evidence event.  The fiber in \((2)\) has district-saturated response-block semantics.  The fiber in \((3)\) retains all internal graph-compatible restrictions of the sparse ADMG.
defs.def:hybrid-result-grammar:
Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring generated by the finitely many supplied rational or real-algebraic output-cell probabilities.  Their stipulated effective presentations give exact arithmetic and sign comparison in \(\mathbb D\), and an order-preserving embedding \(\mathbb D\hookrightarrow\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) supplies exact coefficient representations.  A \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) is finite syntax for a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign tests with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\).  For every real-closed field \(K\) containing an ordered copy of \(\mathbb D\), this syntax has the usual realization \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_K\) in its displayed free variables.  In particular, the causal realization used below is \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_{\mathbb R}\) over the ordinary real field; neither canonical probability variables nor free target-value variables are restricted to \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).

The hybrid terminal grammar is exactly
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{HybridResult}::={}&
\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{UNCOND\_QE}(\chi_T,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton})\\
&\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE\_QE}
\mid\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED\_QE}\\
&\mid\operatorname{COND\_QE}(\chi_Q,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton}),
\end{split}
\tag{1}
\]
where each displayed \(\chi\) is a \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) and \(\mathsf{isSingleton}\) is the exact Boolean output of the associated closed first-order sentence.

The deterministic procedure \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) first runs \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).  A successful rational identification is returned as \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}\).  Every other terminal invokes the graph-compatible canonical fiber
\[
S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P).
\]
Every quantifier-elimination call below is made in the first-order language of real-closed fields with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\); its computation performs only exact coefficient operations in \(\mathbb D\), and its returned syntax is interpreted over \(\mathbb R\).  For \(p_T=\Phi_{T,\mathrm{can}}^\star\), apply quantifier elimination to
\[
\varphi_T(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge t-p_T(x)=0]
\tag{2}
\]
and denote the output by \(\chi_T(t)\).  Apply it to the closed sentence
\[
\exists t_1,t_2\,[\chi_T(t_1)\wedge\chi_T(t_2)\wedge t_1\ne t_2]
\tag{3}
\]
and to
\[
\chi_T(\ell)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow\ell\leq t],
\qquad
\chi_T(u)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow t\leq u]
\tag{4}
\]
to form the singleton Boolean and endpoint formulas.

For a conditional target put \(e=\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\) and \(n=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\).  Define
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf Z:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf N:&\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0]
\ \wedge\ \exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf P:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0].
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Three quantifier-elimination calls yield closed quantifier-free formulas whose exact constant sign evaluations decide \(\mathsf Z\), \(\mathsf N\), and \(\mathsf P\).  On any explicitly supplied nonempty canonical fiber, the single closed formula in \(\mathsf P\) is the reusable uniform-positivity decision; the full block in \((5)\) is used when a failed positivity screen must be classified as uniform zero or mixed zero and positive evidence.  The zero, mixed, and positive meanings and the two payload-free terminal labels are unchanged after replacing \(S\) consistently throughout the block.  The first two cases return the corresponding payload-free evidence terminals.  Only in case \(\mathsf P\) is quantifier elimination applied to
\[
\varphi_Q(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0\wedge e(x)t-n(x)=0]
\tag{6}
\]
to form \(\chi_Q(t)\), its singleton Boolean, and endpoint formulas as in \((3)\)--\((4)\).  The procedure returns formulas and decisions only: it returns no explicit endpoint value, algebraic sample, cylindrical algebraic decomposition trace, canonical parameter, or paired SCM.

assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability:
For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), descriptor \(a\) declares a finite counterfactual tuple \(T_a\), a finite output alphabet \(\mathcal Y_a\), and a deterministic map \(f_a\) into \(\mathcal Y_a\), and
\[
P_a^s=(f_a)_\#\mathcal L_{M^s}(T_a),
\]
where an unpostprocessed descriptor has the identity output map.

node.statement: Assume \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and every supplied output-cell probability is effectively rational or real algebraic.  Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring they generate, with its effective embedding into \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) for coefficient representation and exact arithmetic.  The \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) outputs of \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) are equivalent to their defining first-order formulas in every real-closed field extension containing \(\mathbb D\), and in particular their realizations over the ordinary real field \(\mathbb R\) are used for the causal conclusions.  For either an unconditional finite target-domain counterfactual cell \(T\) or the conditional query \(Q_\rho^\star=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\mid E)\), the algorithm terminates and returns a \(\mathsf{HybridResult}\).  A fast-path \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)\) has \(F\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) and equals the causal query throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  Otherwise, for the real canonical fiber \(S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\), the fallback returns quantifier-free formulas whose real realizations are exactly the full target range and its attained lower and upper endpoints, together with an exact singleton decision.  For an unconditional target it returns \(\operatorname{UNCOND\_QE}\), and identification holds exactly when the real range is a singleton.  For a conditional target it evaluates the closed sentences \(\mathsf Z\), \(\mathsf N\), and \(\mathsf P\) from \(\mathrm{def:hybrid\text{-}result\text{-}grammar}\): it returns the payload-free terminal \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE\_QE}\) exactly under \(\mathsf Z\), the payload-free terminal \(\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED\_QE}\) exactly under \(\mathsf N\), and only under \(\mathsf P\) forms the conditional real range and returns \(\operatorname{COND\_QE}\).  In the last case evidence is uniformly positive on \(S\), and identification holds exactly when the conditional real range is a singleton.  Exact operations in \(\mathbb D\) compute the output syntax and evaluate every closed quantifier-free decision.  A non-singleton real range implies, by exact canonical range equivalence, two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families with unequal target values; the algorithm is not claimed to output endpoint values, algebraic samples, canonical parameters, or paired SCMs.  A local face failure alone is never used as broad-model nonidentification, and no claim is made that all real range points are algebraic.
node.justification: This is the fixed-declared-alphabet completeness result: every unresolved local trace is completed by an exact identified value, a zero or nonuniform evidence certificate, or two same-menu original-alphabet SCMs.
node.gap: CTFTR treats heterogeneous Layer-1/2 transport, CTFIDU+ treats one-specification Layer-3 identification, and canonical bounding work does not provide this source-labelled fast-path-plus-exact-fallback transport certificate.
node.consumer: A user receives either an allowed rational formula or a checkable global algebraic certificate and explicit canonical endpoint models, with division rejected unless evidence is uniformly positive.
node.proof_tex:
Run \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) first.  By
\(\mathrm{thm:recursion\text{-}soundness}\), the run terminates uniquely.  If it
returns an identifying expression \(F\), that theorem gives, according to the query
type,
\[
F(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(T)
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
F(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\mid E)
\tag{1}
\]
for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), with every quotient protected by
its stored nonzero or positive certificate.  Definition
\(\mathrm{def:allowed\text{-}rational\text{-}functional}\) gives
\(F\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\).  This proves the fast path.

Every other local terminal invokes
\[
S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathbb R^N.
\tag{2}
\]
The assumed nonempty broad compatibility fiber and
\(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}frontier}\) imply that
\(S\) is nonempty, compact and real semialgebraic and that its joint target-cell
ranges equal those of the broad original-alphabet compatibility fiber.  The
effective presentations of the supplied rational or real-algebraic cells give exact
arithmetic and sign comparison in their ordered coefficient ring \(\mathbb D\), and
the stipulated ordered embedding into \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) represents the
coefficients without restricting the variables in \((2)\).

Let \(K\) be any real-closed field containing an ordered copy of \(\mathbb D\).
Apply
\(\mathrm{lem:basu\text{-}mohammad\text{-}nezhad\text{-}quantifier\text{-}elimination}\)
over \(K\).  Its algorithm terminates and performs only exact coefficient-ring
operations.  Hence the same finite \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) syntax is equivalent to
the defining formula in every such \(K\), in particular in the ordinary real field.

For an unconditional target put \(p_T=\Phi_{T,\mathrm{can}}^\star\).  Quantifier
elimination applied to
\[
\varphi_T(t)=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge t-p_T(x)=0]
\tag{3}
\]
returns \(\chi_T\) such that, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\chi_T(t)
\Longleftrightarrow
\exists x\in S\;t=p_T(x)
\Longleftrightarrow
\exists\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\;
t=P_{M^\star}(T).
\tag{4}
\]
The second equivalence is exact global joint range equality.  Eliminating the closed
sentence asserting two distinct realizations decides identification exactly.
Continuity on compact \(S\) gives an attained minimum \(\ell_T\) and maximum
\(u_T\).  Therefore
\[
\chi_T(\ell)\wedge
\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow\ell\leq t]
\tag{5}
\]
holds over \(\mathbb R\) exactly for \(\ell=\ell_T\), and the reversed inequality
does the same for \(u_T\).  Quantifier elimination preserves these real
equivalences; it does not require the endpoints or all range points to be algebraic.

For a conditional target set
\[
e(x)=\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(x),
\qquad
n(x)=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(x).
\tag{6}
\]
Probability semantics gives \(e\geq0\) on nonempty \(S\).  Exactly one of
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf Z:&\neg\exists x\in S\;e(x)>0,\\
\mathsf N:&(\exists x\in S\;e(x)=0)\wedge
(\exists x\in S\;e(x)>0),\\
\mathsf P:&\neg\exists x\in S\;e(x)=0
\end{array}
\tag{7}
\]
holds.  The cited quantifier-elimination theorem and exact evaluation of the closed
outputs therefore give the prescribed payload-free status in the first two cases.
Under \(\mathsf Z\), evidence vanishes throughout.  Under \(\mathsf N\), the
conditional is undefined at one compatible law and defined at another, so a
functional on the full fiber must reject division.  Under \(\mathsf P\), continuity
and compactness give
\[
\min_{x\in S}e(x)>0.
\tag{8}
\]
Only then is \(e(x)t-n(x)=0\) equivalent to \(t=n(x)/e(x)\).  Consequently the real
realization of
\[
\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0\wedge e(x)t-n(x)=0]
\tag{9}
\]
is exactly the conditional causal range.  The ratio is continuous by \((8)\), so
the same compactness and endpoint argument as in \((5)\) gives its attained real
extrema, and the closed two-value sentence gives its exact singleton decision.

Only finitely many terminating calls are made.  If either real range is not a
singleton, two distinct attained values exist, and exact canonical range equality
supplies two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families realizing them.  This is an
existence certificate, not witness extraction: the procedure returns no endpoint
number, algebraic sample, cylindrical decomposition trace, canonical parameter, or
paired SCM.  Since every interpretation above is over \(\mathbb R\), no causal
range point was restricted to \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).

lem:finite-fixing-calculus-soundness.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted finite fixing trace \(\tau\), fix a domain label \(s\) occurring in the trace, and fix \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). By \(\mathrm{def:compatibility\text{-}fiber}\), the family \(\mathbf M\) satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\). Acyclicity and the finite response carrier of \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\) imply that recursive substitution assigns to every event \(A\) occurring in the trace a total deterministic indicator
\[
 I_A:\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D\longrightarrow\{0,1\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The vertex set, its district partition, every declared state space, and every response-profile set are finite; hence the product and every sum below are finite. Independence of the district response blocks, which is \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\), gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A)
 =\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
 I_A(\omega)\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\tag{2}
\]
Thus each unconditional response-profile event probability is a polynomial with integer coefficients in the finitely many coordinates \(q_D^s(\omega_D)\). The same argument applies separately to every source-labelled probability leaf. Algebraic combinations of leaves are therefore polynomials in the union of their coordinate families; this observation does not posit any joint probability law across distinct domain labels.

We first justify every strict-positivity certificate that can guard a divisor in \(\tau\). Let \(x\) collect the finitely many response-law coordinates named by such a certificate. The typing rules of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\) require its declared compatibility fiber to be represented by checked constraints
\[
 h_i(x)=0\quad(1\le i\le r),
 \qquad
 g_j(x)\ge 0\quad(1\le j\le t),
\tag{3}
\]
and require the response coordinates of every model in that fiber to satisfy these constraints. For a rational-constant certificate, exact normalization verifies a rational lower bound \(\varepsilon>0\) for the certified polynomial \(p\). For a linear face certificate, the checker verifies rational multipliers and the polynomial identity
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\alpha_i h_i(x)
  +\sum_{j=1}^{t}\lambda_j g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,\quad \lambda_j\ge 0.
\tag{4}
\]
For a preordering certificate, it verifies
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\tau_i(x)h_i(x)
  +\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}
    \sigma_J(x)\prod_{j\in J}g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,
\tag{5}
\]
where every displayed \(\sigma_J\) is exactly checked to be a finite sum of squares of rational polynomials. Substitution of (3) into (4) gives \(p(x)\ge\varepsilon>0\). In (5), the equality terms vanish, each factor \(g_j(x)\) is nonnegative, every finite product of those factors is nonnegative, and every \(\sigma_J(x)\) is nonnegative; hence again \(p(x)\ge\varepsilon>0\). The rational-constant case has the same conclusion by its exact comparison. These cases exhaust the positivity constructors in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\). Consequently every context probability used as a divisor by the accepted trace is strictly positive at \(\mathbf M\).

We next verify the probability constructors. The false and true events have indicators zero and one. For a finite pairwise-disjoint family \((A_j:j\in J)\), pointwise equality of indicators gives
\[
 I_{\bigsqcup_{j\in J}A_j}=\sum_{j\in J}I_{A_j},
\]
and substitution in (2) yields
\[
 P_{M^s}\!\left(\bigsqcup_{j\in J}A_j\right)
 =\sum_{j\in J}P_{M^s}(A_j).
\tag{6}
\]
Marginalization is (6) applied to the finite partition indexed by the marginalized variable's declared state space. Pointwise \(I_{A^{\mathsf c}}=1-I_A\), so normalization of (2) gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A^{\mathsf c})=1-P_{M^s}(A).
\tag{7}
\]
An algebraic product constructor preserves equality of already interpreted scalar expressions. If a product is annotated as the probability of a district-split event, its annotation is valid because \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\) makes the indicated district response blocks independent. A type-correct substitution is a homomorphism for rational constants, finite sums, differences, and products, and therefore preserves every checked polynomial identity.

For a conditional constructor with numerator event \(A\cap H\) and context event \(H\), the certificate argument gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(H)>0.
\tag{8}
\]
The quotient is therefore defined, and the definition of conditional probability gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A\mid H)
 =\frac{P_{M^s}(A\cap H)}{P_{M^s}(H)}.
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (2), (6), (7), and (9), by structural induction over the finite trace syntax in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), identify the semantic value of every subexpression of \(\tau\).

Let \(L_\tau\) and \(R_\tau\) be the resulting response-profile expressions at the input and output of the trace, and let \(H_1,\ldots,H_J\) be its distinct divisor expressions. Clearing denominators uses a multiplier
\[
 \Delta_\tau(x)=\prod_{j=1}^{J}H_j(x)^{k_j},
 \qquad k_j\in\mathbb N_{>0},
\tag{10}
\]
with the empty product interpreted as one. By (8),
\[
 \Delta_\tau(x(\mathbf M))>0.
\tag{11}
\]
Acceptance of \(\tau\), by the exact-checker clause of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), means that rational normalization and coefficient comparison verify the formal polynomial identity
\[
 \Delta_\tau L_\tau-\Delta_\tau R_\tau=0.
\tag{12}
\]
All coordinate sets and sums are finite, so substitution of the response-law coordinates \(x(\mathbf M)\) into (12) is valid and yields
\[
 \Delta_\tau(x(\mathbf M))L_\tau(x(\mathbf M))
 =\Delta_\tau(x(\mathbf M))R_\tau(x(\mathbf M)).
\]
Division by the strictly positive quantity in (11) proves
\[
 L_\tau(x(\mathbf M))=R_\tau(x(\mathbf M)).
\]
Since \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) was arbitrary, every accepted finite fixing trace preserves its represented event probability throughout the compatibility fiber, as claimed.

snapshot.stmt: Every finite fixing trace accepted by the extraction calculus preserves the represented event probability.  More precisely, if the trace expands its input and output into finite response-profile expressions, uses division only by a separately certified positive context probability, and its exact checker verifies the cleared-denominator polynomial identity, then the input and output expressions agree in every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).

defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:district-response-profile: For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), set \(\Omega_D=\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\), the finite set of all tuples \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) of deterministic response maps at every parent configuration allowed by \(G\) and \(\mathcal X\).  For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\) is the joint law of the response maps induced by \(M^s\).  The carrier is query independent and includes every configuration needed by any target, menu, deterministic postprocessor, or later acquired regime.
defs.def:finite-extraction-calculus:
The finite extraction calculus has event syntax
\[
\mathsf{XEvent}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\top\mid\bot\mid
\neg\mathsf{XEvent}\mid
\bigsqcup_{j\in J}\mathsf{XEvent}_j\mid
\operatorname{Marg}_{W}(\mathsf{XEvent})\mid
\operatorname{Fix}(\mathsf{FixTrace},\mathsf{XEvent}),
\]
where \(J\) and every marginalized alphabet are finite, and a disjoint-union node carries a complete pointwise disjointness table.  The cell event is
\[
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its probability leaf is the supplied output cell \(P_a^s(y)\).  Only its recursively evaluated indicator is expanded by the finite identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\};
\tag{1}
\]
the tuple-cell probabilities on the right of \((1)\) are not menu generators unless an identity-output tuple descriptor is separately supplied.

Menu expressions have syntax
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{XExpr}::={}&
\operatorname{CellProb}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j
\mid\mathsf{XExpr}-\mathsf{XExpr}
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j\\
&\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\pi_H),
\end{split}
\]
where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\pi_H\) is a separately checkable strict-positivity certificate on its declared compatibility fiber.  A derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) is generated only by an output-cell lookup, the truth-table identity \((1)\), contradiction or sure-event evaluation, finite disjoint additivity, complementation, finite marginalization, multiplication of independent original-district factors, and a checked fixing trace.

A fixing trace is a finite tree whose leaves are event or expression derivations and whose constructors are identity, typed substitution from a fixed finite registry of sound Boolean or fixing identities, finite disjoint sum, finite product, complement, marginalization, conditional quotient with a separately checked positive denominator, composition, and cleared-denominator comparison.  Every constructor stores all of its children and type data.  A comparison node is accepted only when cross-multiplication is legal under its stored denominator certificates and coefficient-by-coefficient normalization gives the zero polynomial.  The identity registry is finite and contains only pointwise Boolean identities, finite total-probability identities, and the fixing identities explicitly verified by recursive substitution of structural response tables.  Thus no constructor contains the semantic equality it is intended to establish.

Positivity certificates are either a positive rational constant after exact normalization, a rational Farkas identity for a linear face, or a displayed finite preordering identity
\[
p-\varepsilon=
\sum_i\tau_i h_i+
\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}\sigma_J
\prod_{j\in J}g_j,
\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
where the declared fiber has equations \(h_i=0\), inequalities \(g_j\geq0\), and every \(\sigma_J\) is checked coefficient by coefficient to be a finite sum of squares.  All polynomial equalities are checked by exact integer or rational coefficient comparison.

For an event \(A\) and a district \(D\), the total procedure \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) enumerates
\[
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\longmapsto
\mathbf 1\{A\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\}
\]
over the complete finite response carriers.  It accepts exactly when every two entries with the same \(\omega_D\) agree, and then returns their common row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\).  Otherwise it returns the first disagreeing pair in the canonical order.  All syntax trees, registries, coefficient vectors, truth tables, and searches are finite and canonically ordered.

assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability:
For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), descriptor \(a\) declares a finite counterfactual tuple \(T_a\), a finite output alphabet \(\mathcal Y_a\), and a deterministic map \(f_a\) into \(\mathcal Y_a\), and
\[
P_a^s=(f_a)_\#\mathcal L_{M^s}(T_a),
\]
where an unpostprocessed descriptor has the identity output map.

More precisely, if the trace expands its input and output into finite response-profile expressions, uses division only by a separately certified positive context probability, and its exact checker verifies the cleared-denominator polynomial identity, then the input and output expressions agree in every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).
node.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted finite fixing trace \(\tau\), fix a domain label \(s\) occurring in the trace, and fix \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). By \(\mathrm{def:compatibility\text{-}fiber}\), the family \(\mathbf M\) satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\). Acyclicity and the finite response carrier of \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\) imply that recursive substitution assigns to every event \(A\) occurring in the trace a total deterministic indicator
\[
 I_A:\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D\longrightarrow\{0,1\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The vertex set, its district partition, every declared state space, and every response-profile set are finite; hence the product and every sum below are finite. Independence of the district response blocks, which is \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\), gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A)
 =\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
 I_A(\omega)\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\tag{2}
\]
Thus each unconditional response-profile event probability is a polynomial with integer coefficients in the finitely many coordinates \(q_D^s(\omega_D)\). The same argument applies separately to every source-labelled probability leaf. Algebraic combinations of leaves are therefore polynomials in the union of their coordinate families; this observation does not posit any joint probability law across distinct domain labels.

We first justify every strict-positivity certificate that can guard a divisor in \(\tau\). Let \(x\) collect the finitely many response-law coordinates named by such a certificate. The typing rules of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\) require its declared compatibility fiber to be represented by checked constraints
\[
 h_i(x)=0\quad(1\le i\le r),
 \qquad
 g_j(x)\ge 0\quad(1\le j\le t),
\tag{3}
\]
and require the response coordinates of every model in that fiber to satisfy these constraints. For a rational-constant certificate, exact normalization verifies a rational lower bound \(\varepsilon>0\) for the certified polynomial \(p\). For a linear face certificate, the checker verifies rational multipliers and the polynomial identity
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\alpha_i h_i(x)
  +\sum_{j=1}^{t}\lambda_j g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,\quad \lambda_j\ge 0.
\tag{4}
\]
For a preordering certificate, it verifies
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\tau_i(x)h_i(x)
  +\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}
    \sigma_J(x)\prod_{j\in J}g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,
\tag{5}
\]
where every displayed \(\sigma_J\) is exactly checked to be a finite sum of squares of rational polynomials. Substitution of (3) into (4) gives \(p(x)\ge\varepsilon>0\). In (5), the equality terms vanish, each factor \(g_j(x)\) is nonnegative, every finite product of those factors is nonnegative, and every \(\sigma_J(x)\) is nonnegative; hence again \(p(x)\ge\varepsilon>0\). The rational-constant case has the same conclusion by its exact comparison. These cases exhaust the positivity constructors in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\). Consequently every context probability used as a divisor by the accepted trace is strictly positive at \(\mathbf M\).

We next verify the probability constructors. The false and true events have indicators zero and one. For a finite pairwise-disjoint family \((A_j:j\in J)\), pointwise equality of indicators gives
\[
 I_{\bigsqcup_{j\in J}A_j}=\sum_{j\in J}I_{A_j},
\]
and substitution in (2) yields
\[
 P_{M^s}\!\left(\bigsqcup_{j\in J}A_j\right)
 =\sum_{j\in J}P_{M^s}(A_j).
\tag{6}
\]
Marginalization is (6) applied to the finite partition indexed by the marginalized variable's declared state space. Pointwise \(I_{A^{\mathsf c}}=1-I_A\), so normalization of (2) gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A^{\mathsf c})=1-P_{M^s}(A).
\tag{7}
\]
An algebraic product constructor preserves equality of already interpreted scalar expressions. If a product is annotated as the probability of a district-split event, its annotation is valid because \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\) makes the indicated district response blocks independent. A type-correct substitution is a homomorphism for rational constants, finite sums, differences, and products, and therefore preserves every checked polynomial identity.

For a conditional constructor with numerator event \(A\cap H\) and context event \(H\), the certificate argument gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(H)>0.
\tag{8}
\]
The quotient is therefore defined, and the definition of conditional probability gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A\mid H)
 =\frac{P_{M^s}(A\cap H)}{P_{M^s}(H)}.
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (2), (6), (7), and (9), by structural induction over the finite trace syntax in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), identify the semantic value of every subexpression of \(\tau\).

Let \(L_\tau\) and \(R_\tau\) be the resulting response-profile expressions at the input and output of the trace, and let \(H_1,\ldots,H_J\) be its distinct divisor expressions. Clearing denominators uses a multiplier
\[
 \Delta_\tau(x)=\prod_{j=1}^{J}H_j(x)^{k_j},
 \qquad k_j\in\mathbb N_{>0},
\tag{10}
\]
with the empty product interpreted as one. By (8),
\[
 \Delta_\tau(x(\mathbf M))>0.
\tag{11}
\]
Acceptance of \(\tau\), by the exact-checker clause of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), means that rational normalization and coefficient comparison verify the formal polynomial identity
\[
 \Delta_\tau L_\tau-\Delta_\tau R_\tau=0.
\tag{12}
\]
All coordinate sets and sums are finite, so substitution of the response-law coordinates \(x(\mathbf M)\) into (12) is valid and yields
\[
 \Delta_\tau(x(\mathbf M))L_\tau(x(\mathbf M))
 =\Delta_\tau(x(\mathbf M))R_\tau(x(\mathbf M)).
\]
Division by the strictly positive quantity in (11) proves
\[
 L_\tau(x(\mathbf M))=R_\tau(x(\mathbf M)).
\]
Since \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) was arbitrary, every accepted finite fixing trace preserves its represented event probability throughout the compatibility fiber, as claimed.

lem:finite-extraction-calculus-soundness.proof_tex:
Fix a domain label \(s\), a checked derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\), and \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). We first prove the positivity assertion needed by quotient nodes. For any accepted positivity certificate, let \(x\) be its finite vector of response-law coordinates and write the checked description of its declared compatibility fiber as
\[
 h_i(x)=0\quad(1\le i\le r),
 \qquad
 g_j(x)\ge 0\quad(1\le j\le t).
\tag{13}
\]
The typing clause of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\) ensures that the coordinates of every model in the declared fiber satisfy (13). An accepted rational-constant certificate exactly verifies \(p(x)\ge\varepsilon\) with \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). An accepted linear face certificate exactly verifies
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\alpha_i h_i(x)
  +\sum_{j=1}^{t}\lambda_j g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,\quad\lambda_j\ge 0,
\tag{14}
\]
and an accepted preordering certificate exactly verifies
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\tau_i(x)h_i(x)
  +\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}
    \sigma_J(x)\prod_{j\in J}g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,
\tag{15}
\]
where each \(\sigma_J\) is exactly checked to be a finite sum of squares of rational polynomials. On (13), the equality terms in (14) and (15) vanish, all remaining factors are nonnegative, and sums of squares are nonnegative. Therefore every admitted constructor gives
\[
 p(x)\ge\varepsilon>0.
\tag{16}
\]
Exact coefficient comparison establishes (14) and (15) as polynomial identities, so substitution of model coordinates cannot invalidate them. Since these cases exhaust the admitted positivity-certificate grammar, every accepted positivity certificate is valid on its declared compatibility fiber.

We now prove
\[
 F(\mathcal P)=P_{M^s}(A)
\tag{17}
\]
by structural induction on the finite derivation tree in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\). At a supplied-cell leaf, descriptor \(a\) declares a finite primitive tuple \(T_a\), a deterministic finite map \(f_a\), and the returned output \(f_a(T_a)\). By \(\mathrm{ass:typed\text{-}menu\text{-}realizability}\), together with the descriptor semantics in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), its supplied law is the pushforward
\[
 P_a^s=(f_a)_\#\operatorname{Law}_{M^s}(T_a).
\tag{18}
\]
Consequently, for each declared output cell \(y\), the leaf generator has the direct semantics
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)(\mathcal P)
 &=P_a^s(y)\\
 &=\operatorname{Law}_{M^s}\!\bigl(f_a(T_a)\bigr)(y)\\
 &=P_{M^s}\!\bigl(f_a(T_a)=y\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
This uses the supplied output law itself. The deterministic preimage equality
\[
 \mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
 =\sum_{t:\,f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\}
\tag{20}
\]
is used only to evaluate event indicators, locality truth tables, and response-profile polynomials. In particular, (20) does not make any probability \(P_{M^s}(T_a=t)\) a supplied menu generator. Such a tuple-cell probability is directly available only if the menu separately contains an identity-output descriptor. This proves the induction claim for every supplied leaf without enlarging \(\mathcal P\). Since the deterministic map \(f_a\) is evaluated after \(T_a\) is returned, this evaluation visits no additional structural parent configuration; the carrier in \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\) therefore suffices for (20).

The contradiction and sure-event leaves have probabilities zero and one. If the induction claim holds for \(A_0\), finite complementarity gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A_0^{\mathsf c})
 =1-P_{M^s}(A_0)
 =1-F_0(\mathcal P).
\tag{21}
\]
If it holds for a finite pairwise-disjoint family \((A_j:j\in J)\), finite additivity gives
\[
 P_{M^s}\!\left(\bigsqcup_{j\in J}A_j\right)
 =\sum_{j\in J}P_{M^s}(A_j)
 =\sum_{j\in J}F_j(\mathcal P).
\tag{22}
\]
The Boolean-normalization constructor forms a finite disjoint truth-table partition, so (21)--(22) prove its case. A marginalization constructor enumerates the finite partition indexed by the marginalized variable's declared nonempty state space and is another application of (22).

For a fixing constructor, the derivation contains an accepted fixing trace and type-correct substitutions for its leaves. By \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}fixing\text{-}calculus\text{-}soundness}\), the trace preserves the represented event probability. Equations (19), (21), and (22), together with the induction hypotheses, identify the semantic values of all substituted leaves, while type-correct substitution preserves rational constants, finite sums, differences, and products. Thus the fixing constructor preserves (17).

An internal kernel quotient is admitted only after checked derivations of its numerator event \(A_0\cap H\) and context event \(H\), together with an independently accepted strict-positivity certificate for that context. The induction hypotheses and (16) give
\[
 F_H(\mathcal P)=P_{M^s}(H)>0.
\tag{23}
\]
Division is therefore legitimate, and the definition of conditional probability yields
\[
 \frac{F_{A_0\cap H}(\mathcal P)}{F_H(\mathcal P)}
 =\frac{P_{M^s}(A_0\cap H)}{P_{M^s}(H)}
 =P_{M^s}(A_0\mid H).
\tag{24}
\]
There is no unguarded division constructor. The supplied-cell, constant, Boolean-normalization, marginalization, fixing, and certified-quotient cases exhaust the checked derivation grammar. This completes the induction and proves (17).

It remains to prove the assertion about \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\). Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) and define
\[
 \Omega_{-D}
 =\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\tag{25}
\]
where an empty product is a singleton. By \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\) and \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\), every factor is finite and recursive evaluation is total. Hence \(A\) has a deterministic indicator
\[
 I_A:\Omega_D\times\Omega_{-D}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}.
\tag{26}
\]
By the exhaustive-checker clause of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) compares
\[
 I_A(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})
 =I_A(\omega_D,\omega'_{-D})
\tag{27}
\]
for every \(\omega_D\in\Omega_D\) and every \(\omega_{-D},\omega'_{-D}\in\Omega_{-D}\). The enumerated set is finite, so the checker terminates. If it accepts, all equalities (27) hold, which is exactly independence of the recursive indicator from the nonfocal response profiles. Conversely, that independence makes every equality (27) true, so the exhaustive checker accepts.

Upon acceptance, let \(\omega_{-D}^{0}\) be the checker's fixed reference profile. Its constructed row is
\[
 \operatorname{row}_D(A)(\omega_D)
 =I_A(\omega_D,\omega_{-D}^{0}).
\tag{28}
\]
Combining (27) and (28) gives, for every \(\omega_D\in\Omega_D\) and every \(\omega_{-D}\in\Omega_{-D}\),
\[
 \operatorname{row}_D(A)(\omega_D)
 =I_A(\omega_D,\omega_{-D}).
\]
If the checker rejects, its first failed comparison in the fixed finite enumeration supplies an explicit triple \((\omega_D,\omega_{-D},\omega'_{-D})\) witnessing dependence on the nonfocal profile. This proves termination, the if-and-only-if acceptance characterization, and correctness of the row constructed upon acceptance.
