The typing clause of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\) ensures that the coordinates of every model in the declared fiber satisfy (13). An accepted rational-constant certificate exactly verifies \(p(x)\ge\varepsilon\) with \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). An accepted linear face certificate exactly verifies
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\alpha_i h_i(x)
  +\sum_{j=1}^{t}\lambda_j g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,\quad\lambda_j\ge 0,
\tag{14}
\]
and an accepted preordering certificate exactly verifies
\[
 p(x)-\varepsilon
 =\sum_{i=1}^{r}\tau_i(x)h_i(x)
  +\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}
    \sigma_J(x)\prod_{j\in J}g_j(x),
 \qquad \varepsilon>0,
\tag{15}
\]
where each \(\sigma_J\) is exactly checked to be a finite sum of squares of rational polynomials. On (13), the equality terms in (14) and (15) vanish, all remaining factors are nonnegative, and sums of squares are nonnegative. Therefore every admitted constructor gives
\[
 p(x)\ge\varepsilon>0.
\tag{16}
\]
Exact coefficient comparison establishes (14) and (15) as polynomial identities, so substitution of model coordinates cannot invalidate them. Since these cases exhaust the admitted positivity-certificate grammar, every accepted positivity certificate is valid on its declared compatibility fiber.

We now prove
\[
 F(\mathcal P)=P_{M^s}(A)
\tag{17}
\]
by structural induction on the finite derivation tree in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\). At a supplied-cell leaf, descriptor \(a\) declares a finite primitive tuple \(T_a\), a deterministic finite map \(f_a\), and the returned output \(f_a(T_a)\). By \(\mathrm{ass:typed\text{-}menu\text{-}realizability}\), together with the descriptor semantics in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), its supplied law is the pushforward
\[
 P_a^s=(f_a)_\#\operatorname{Law}_{M^s}(T_a).
\tag{18}
\]
Consequently, for each declared output cell \(y\), the leaf generator has the direct semantics
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)(\mathcal P)
 &=P_a^s(y)\\
 &=\operatorname{Law}_{M^s}\!\bigl(f_a(T_a)\bigr)(y)\\
 &=P_{M^s}\!\bigl(f_a(T_a)=y\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
This uses the supplied output law itself. The deterministic preimage equality
\[
 \mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
 =\sum_{t:\,f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\}
\tag{20}
\]
is used only to evaluate event indicators, locality truth tables, and response-profile polynomials. In particular, (20) does not make any probability \(P_{M^s}(T_a=t)\) a supplied menu generator. Such a tuple-cell probability is directly available only if the menu separately contains an identity-output descriptor. This proves the induction claim for every supplied leaf without enlarging \(\mathcal P\). Since the deterministic map \(f_a\) is evaluated after \(T_a\) is returned, this evaluation visits no additional structural parent configuration; the carrier in \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\) therefore suffices for (20).

The contradiction and sure-event leaves have probabilities zero and one. If the induction claim holds for \(A_0\), finite complementarity gives
\[
 P_{M^s}(A_0^{\mathsf c})
 =1-P_{M^s}(A_0)
 =1-F_0(\mathcal P).
\tag{21}
\]
If it holds for a finite pairwise-disjoint family \((A_j:j\in J)\), finite additivity gives
\[
 P_{M^s}\!\left(\bigsqcup_{j\in J}A_j\right)
 =\sum_{j\in J}P_{M^s}(A_j)
 =\sum_{j\in J}F_j(\mathcal P).
\tag{22}
\]
The Boolean-normalization constructor forms a finite disjoint truth-table partition, so (21)--(22) prove its case. A marginalization constructor enumerates the finite partition indexed by the marginalized variable's declared nonempty state space and is another application of (22).

For a fixing constructor, the derivation contains an accepted fixing trace and type-correct substitutions for its leaves. By \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}fixing\text{-}calculus\text{-}soundness}\), the trace preserves the represented event probability. Equations (19), (21), and (22), together with the induction hypotheses, identify the semantic values of all substituted leaves, while type-correct substitution preserves rational constants, finite sums, differences, and products. Thus the fixing constructor preserves (17).

An internal kernel quotient is admitted only after checked derivations of its numerator event \(A_0\cap H\) and context event \(H\), together with an independently accepted strict-positivity certificate for that context. The induction hypotheses and (16) give
\[
 F_H(\mathcal P)=P_{M^s}(H)>0.
\tag{23}
\]
Division is therefore legitimate, and the definition of conditional probability yields
\[
 \frac{F_{A_0\cap H}(\mathcal P)}{F_H(\mathcal P)}
 =\frac{P_{M^s}(A_0\cap H)}{P_{M^s}(H)}
 =P_{M^s}(A_0\mid H).
\tag{24}
\]
There is no unguarded division constructor. The supplied-cell, constant, Boolean-normalization, marginalization, fixing, and certified-quotient cases exhaust the checked derivation grammar. This completes the induction and proves (17).

It remains to prove the assertion about \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\). Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) and define
\[
 \Omega_{-D}
 =\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\tag{25}
\]
where an empty product is a singleton. By \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\) and \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\), every factor is finite and recursive evaluation is total. Hence \(A\) has a deterministic indicator
\[
 I_A:\Omega_D\times\Omega_{-D}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}.
\tag{26}
\]
By the exhaustive-checker clause of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) compares
\[
 I_A(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})
 =I_A(\omega_D,\omega'_{-D})
\tag{27}
\]
for every \(\omega_D\in\Omega_D\) and every \(\omega_{-D},\omega'_{-D}\in\Omega_{-D}\). The enumerated set is finite, so the checker terminates. If it accepts, all equalities (27) hold, which is exactly independence of the recursive indicator from the nonfocal response profiles. Conversely, that independence makes every equality (27) true, so the exhaustive checker accepts.

Upon acceptance, let \(\omega_{-D}^{0}\) be the checker's fixed reference profile. Its constructed row is
\[
 \operatorname{row}_D(A)(\omega_D)
 =I_A(\omega_D,\omega_{-D}^{0}).
\tag{28}
\]
Combining (27) and (28) gives, for every \(\omega_D\in\Omega_D\) and every \(\omega_{-D}\in\Omega_{-D}\),
\[
 \operatorname{row}_D(A)(\omega_D)
 =I_A(\omega_D,\omega_{-D}).
\]
If the checker rejects, its first failed comparison in the fixed finite enumeration supplies an explicit triple \((\omega_D,\omega_{-D},\omega'_{-D})\) witnessing dependence on the nonfocal profile. This proves termination, the if-and-only-if acceptance characterization, and correctness of the row constructed upon acceptance.

thm:global-canonical-acquisition-complet.proof_tex:
Let \(S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}\subseteq\mathcal U\).  By
\(\mathrm{def:global\text{-}regime\text{-}block\text{-}acquisition}\), the menu
\(\mathcal P_{T_{\mathrm{exp}}}\) contains every complete cell equation in
\(\mathcal P_S\).  Applying the same equations in
\(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}fiber}\) therefore gives
\[
\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\subseteq
\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{exp}}}\subseteq\Lambda_S.
\tag{1}
\]
Admissibility gives \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\ne\varnothing\), so every fiber in
\((1)\) is nonempty.  Each is a closed subset of the finite canonical parameter
space and hence is compact; all of its constraints are polynomial equalities and
inequalities.

Put
\[
e(\vartheta)=
\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star).
\tag{2}
\]
Recursive probability semantics gives \(e\geq0\) on every canonical fiber.  Apply
the reusable block in \(\mathrm{def:hybrid\text{-}result\text{-}grammar}\) to the
nonempty full fiber \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\).  Exact quantifier elimination from
\(\mathrm{lem:basu\text{-}mohammad\text{-}nezhad\text{-}quantifier\text{-}elimination}\)
decides precisely the mutually exclusive alternatives
\[
 e\equiv0,
\qquad
\bigl(\min e=0<\max e\bigr),
\qquad
e>0\text{ everywhere on }\Lambda_{\mathcal U}.
\tag{3}
\]
The first two alternatives are exactly the two payload-free failures prescribed by
the acquisition definition.  The last alternative is
\(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\mathcal U)\) by
\(\mathrm{def:global\text{-}subset\text{-}positivity}\), so and only so the numerical
full-menu benchmark is defined.

Fix any \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\).  The defining formula
\[
\neg\exists\vartheta\,
\left[\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\wedge e(\vartheta)=0\right]
\tag{4}
\]
is a closed first-order formula over the reals with coefficients in the effective
ordered ring generated by the complete augmented menu.  The cited
quantifier-elimination result makes \((4)\) one exact decision.  If \((4)\) holds,
continuity of \(e\), compactness and nonemptiness give an attained minimum
\[
\epsilon_S:=\min_{\vartheta\in\Lambda_S}e(\vartheta)>0.
\tag{5}
\]
Conversely, \((5)\) excludes a zero and hence implies \((4)\).  Thus the displayed
predicate is exactly uniform strict positivity, including on a boundary fiber.

The inclusion in \((1)\) proves the positivity monotonicity: if
\(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\) holds and \(S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}\), a zero of
\(e\) in \(\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{exp}}}\) would also be a zero in \(\Lambda_S\), a
contradiction.  Suppose both possibly-optimal sets are defined and
\(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})\).  There is then
\(\vartheta\in\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{exp}}}\subseteq\Lambda_S\) satisfying
\[
n_\rho(\vartheta)-n_\sigma(\vartheta)\geq0
\qquad(\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}),
\tag{6}
\]
so the same point witnesses \(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\).  Hence
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})
\subseteq\operatorname{PO}_G(S).
\tag{7}
\]
If \(S\) is feasible and \(S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}\), positivity monotonicity
and \((7)\), applied also to \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}\subseteq\mathcal U\), yield
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(\mathcal U)
\subseteq\operatorname{PO}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})
\subseteq\operatorname{PO}_G(S)
=\operatorname{PO}_G(\mathcal U).
\tag{8}
\]
Thus \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}\) is feasible, proving upward closure.

For a positive \(S\) and fixed \(\rho\), the membership condition is the single
closed existential formula
\[
\exists\vartheta\left[
\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\ \wedge\
\bigwedge_{\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}}
\{n_\rho(\vartheta)-n_\sigma(\vartheta)\geq0\}
\right].
\tag{9}
\]
Every constraint in \((9)\) is polynomial over the same effective ordered
coefficient ring, so quantifier elimination decides it exactly.  Enumerating the
\(2^{|\mathcal U|}\) subsets uses at most that many calls for \((4)\) and at most
\(2^{|\mathcal U|}|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|\) calls for \((9)\).  One existential
call verifies \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\ne\varnothing\), and a fixed number of calls
classifies the full fiber as in \((3)\).  Once the Boolean answers are known, exact
finite comparison of the effectively comparable positive costs retains every
feasible set of least total cost, including ties.  The full set is feasible under
\(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\mathcal U)\), so the optimization has a solution.

We next prove that this numerical program ranks causal conditionals rather than
merely canonical numerator polynomials.  For a positive \(S\), apply
\(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}frontier}\) to the complete
augmented menu \(\mathcal P_S\) and to the joint finite cell collection
\[
\{B_\tau\cap E:\tau\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\}\cup\{E\}.
\tag{10}
\]
It gives equality of the entire range in \((10)\) between \(\Lambda_S\) and
original-alphabet families in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P_S)\).  By \((5)\), for every
pair of arms,
\[
\frac{n_\rho(\vartheta)}{e(\vartheta)}
\geq
\frac{n_\sigma(\vartheta)}{e(\vartheta)}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
n_\rho(\vartheta)-n_\sigma(\vartheta)\geq0.
\tag{11}
\]
The equivalence uses multiplication by the common strictly positive denominator,
not a definition of the causal target.  Joint range equality and \((11)\) prove that
\(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) is exactly the set of arms conditionally optimal in some
broad compatible original-alphabet family.

Suppose now that the augmented information is also represented by a checked local
row system.  By \(\mathrm{def:target\text{-}arm\text{-}rows}\), its base-face
certificate gives
\[
d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D>0
\qquad(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)).
\tag{12}
\]
Every acquired subface lies inside the base face.  Moreover,
\(\mathrm{lem:district\text{-}cell\text{-}linearity}\) maps every broad compatible
model to its local response law in \(\mathcal K_S\) and maps evidence to
\(d_D^{\mathsf T}q\).  Thus \((12)\) makes every corresponding global subset
positive.  A broad witness for \(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) supplies a
\(q\in\mathcal K_S\) satisfying all local numerator inequalities, proving
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\subseteq\operatorname{PO}(S).
\tag{13}
\]
Under the augmented focal projection hypotheses,
\(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\) realizes every
\(q\in\mathcal K_S\) by a family in
\(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P_S)\subseteq\mathcal C(\mathcal P_S)\).
The same numerator and evidence equations reverse \((13)\).  This proves the local
bridge without identifying the row face with the broad fiber outside those
hypotheses.

For non-submodularity, use the one-domain binary bow construction in
\(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}layer3\text{-}acquisition\text{-}obstruction}\).  Its
common evidence is \(\top\), so \(e=1\) on every augmented fiber.  Its explicit
response-block realization gives, for every \(S\subseteq\{e_1,e_2\}\),
\[
\{q_D^\star(\vartheta):\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\}=\mathcal K_S.
\tag{14}
\]
The possibly-optimal table and the increasing marginal gain proved there therefore
hold verbatim for \(\operatorname{PO}_G\) and \(f_G\).  Both experiments, and only
both, reproduce the full possibly-optimal set, so the unique cost is two.

Finally, the promised definability-acquisition check uses the one-domain graph with
one parentless binary vertex \(Y\), hence one singleton district and response
profiles \(Y=0\) and \(Y=1\).  Let
\[
q=P(Y=1),\qquad E=\{Y=1\},
\tag{15}
\]
and let the base menu contain only a constant Boolean output, which imposes no
constraint on \(q\).  Thus \(\Lambda_{\varnothing}=[0,1]\) and \(e(q)=q\).  Take a
single candidate experiment that discloses the complete law of the Boolean output
\(Y\), with \(P(Y=1)=1\) and \(P(Y=0)=0\).  The two complete cells impose exactly
\(q=1\), so \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}=\{1\}\).  Both endpoint response laws are finite
recursive SCMs on the original binary alphabet, so the menu is realizable.  The
base fiber contains both a zero-evidence and a positive-evidence law, whereas the
full fiber has evidence one.  With a singleton arm set the full numerical benchmark
is well defined.  This proves the claimed strict usefulness of full-menu positivity;
with one experiment and one arm it makes no separate non-submodularity claim.

snapshot.stmt:
Assume that the exact global acquisition instance of \(\mathrm{def:global\text{-}regime\text{-}block\text{-}acquisition}\) is admissible.  Then \(\Lambda_S\ne\varnothing\) for every \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), and
\[
S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{exp}}}\subseteq\Lambda_S.
\]
The full-fiber evidence test on \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\) returns uniform zero evidence or mixed zero and positive evidence exactly in those two cases and then defines no numerical full-menu arm-ranking benchmark.  In the remaining case \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\mathcal U)\) holds and the acquisition problem is defined, even if \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\varnothing)\) fails.

For every \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\) is decided exactly by one closed quantifier-elimination call.  Whenever it holds, there exists \(\epsilon_S>0\) such that
\[
\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star)\geq\epsilon_S
\qquad\text{for every }\vartheta\in\Lambda_S,
\]
and, for each \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), membership \(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) is decided exactly by one closed existential formula over the reals.  Moreover,
\[
S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\bigl(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\Longrightarrow
\operatorname{Pos}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})\bigr),
\]
and, when both possibly-optimal sets are defined,
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})
\subseteq\operatorname{PO}_G(S).
\]
Consequently the feasible design family is upward closed.  Exhaustive enumeration returns every minimum-cost solution, including every cost tie, using at most
\[
2^{|\mathcal U|}
\]
subset-positivity quantifier-elimination calls and at most
\[
2^{|\mathcal U|}|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|
\]
membership calls, in addition to one joint-realizability call and a fixed full-fiber status classification.

For every positive subset \(S\), \(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) is exactly the set of arms that are conditionally optimal in at least one original-alphabet SCM family in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P_S)\).  Thus the subset-specific ranking semantics are exact for every finite sparse ADMG.

Whenever the same augmented information is represented by a local \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) system, its checked base-face evidence lower bound makes every subset positive and broad compatibility implies
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\subseteq\operatorname{PO}(S).
\]
If, for that augmented menu, the checked arm events are focal-district local and the focal projection hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\) hold, then equality holds.  Hence the existing local LP acquisition is the uniformly-positive special case and remains an outer pruning relaxation outside those projection hypotheses.

The two-experiment Boolean-pushforward instance of \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}layer3\text{-}acquisition\text{-}obstruction}\) has \(E=\top\), so every subset is positive, its displayed possibly-optimal table also holds with \(\operatorname{PO}_G\), and \(f_G\) is not submodular in general; its unique exact broad-model solution buys both experiments at total cost two.  Separately, there is a realizable one-domain binary singleton-district instance with one complete Boolean-output experiment for which \(\Lambda_{\varnothing}=[0,1]\), the evidence map is \(e(q)=q\), and the acquired law fixes \(q=1\).  Thus base evidence is mixed while the full fiber is uniformly positive; this second instance demonstrates acquisition of definability and is not a second non-submodularity witness.

defs.def:exact-global-canonical-fiber:
Use the complete query-independent carriers \(\Omega_D=\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\).  For \(\theta=(q_D^s:s\in\mathcal S,D\in\mathcal D(G))\), define
\[
\Psi_C^s(\theta^s)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\tag{1}
\]
If the indicator visits \(k\) districts, \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district-law blocks and has total degree at most \(k\).  For descriptor \(a\) and output \(y\in\mathcal Y_a\), let
\[
C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its indicator in \((1)\) is evaluated by the finite deterministic preimage, while its menu value is directly \(P_a^s(y)\).  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta:{}&
q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S,D\in\mathcal D(G)),\\
&q_D^s=q_D^\star
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Psi_{C_{a,y}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(y)
\quad\text{for every }s,a,y\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\tag{2}
\]
For a target cell \(T\), set
\[
L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\qquad
U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]
and
\[
\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)=
\Psi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)
-\Psi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star).
\]

For an arbitrary, possibly nonsaturated ADMG \(G\), let \(\vartheta^s=(\mu^s,p^s)\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\).  Its canonical coordinates satisfy
\[
p_U^s(u)\geq0,\quad\sum_up_U^s(u)=1,
\quad \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s\in\{0,1\},
\quad \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s=1,
\]
together with every graph-compatible within-district latent-factor restriction and independence across original districts.  Let \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)\) be the polynomial obtained by finite recursive evaluation and let \(q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)\) be the induced complete district response law.  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\vartheta:{}&
\vartheta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
&q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)
=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Phi_{C_{a,y},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(y)
\quad\text{for every complete supplied output cell}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\tag{3}
\]
Every occurrence of \(\mathcal P\) in \((2)\)--\((3)\) denotes the current complete typed-menu argument, whether it is the base menu or a finite complete-menu augmentation.  Every newly disclosed output cell, including every complementary cell of its finite output law, is imposed simultaneously; no base-menu equation and no complete cell rejected by a local row checker is discarded.  Neither fiber definition presupposes positivity of an evidence event.  The fiber in \((2)\) has district-saturated response-block semantics.  The fiber in \((3)\) retains all internal graph-compatible restrictions of the sparse ADMG.
defs.def:global-regime-block-acquisition:
Let \(\mathcal U\) be a finite set of physically realizable candidate experiments.  Each \(e\in\mathcal U\) discloses a finite block of complete typed output laws, including every cell of each declared finite output, whose probabilities are effectively rational or real algebraic, and has an effectively comparable cost \(c_e>0\).  For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), let \(\mathcal P_S\) be \(\mathcal P\) augmented by all complete output laws disclosed by experiments in \(S\), and define
\[
\Lambda_S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P_S).
\]
An admissible global acquisition instance is required to satisfy \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\ne\varnothing\).  For every \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), use \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\) from \(\mathrm{def:global\text{-}subset\text{-}positivity}\).

Apply the closed zero, mixed, and positive evidence tests of \(\mathrm{def:hybrid\text{-}result\text{-}grammar}\) to the full fiber \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\).  Uniform zero evidence or mixed zero and positive evidence returns the corresponding payload-free status and leaves the numerical full-menu conditional arm-ranking benchmark undefined.  Only when \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\mathcal U)\) holds define
\[
n_\rho(\vartheta)
=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star).
\]
For a subset \(S\), define its numerical possibly-optimal set only when \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\) holds, by
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)
=\left\{\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}:
\exists\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ 
n_\rho(\vartheta)-n_\sigma(\vartheta)\geq0\right\}.
\]
Set
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full},G}=\operatorname{PO}_G(\mathcal U),
\qquad
f_G(S)=|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|-|\operatorname{PO}_G(S)|
\]
on positive subsets, and define the exact broad-model ex-post acquisition problem by
\[
\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full},G}.
\]
Thus the acquired full menu, rather than the unaugmented menu, is required to establish uniform conditional definability.
defs.def:global-subset-positivity:
For every \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define
\[
\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\neg\exists\vartheta\,
\left[\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\ \wedge\
\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star)=0\right].
\]
The predicate is used only when \(\Lambda_S\ne\varnothing\), and its displayed
closed real formula is evaluated by the exact quantifier-elimination semantics of
\(\mathrm{def:hybrid\text{-}result\text{-}grammar}\).
defs.def:hybrid-result-grammar:
Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring generated by the finitely many supplied rational or real-algebraic output-cell probabilities.  Their stipulated effective presentations give exact arithmetic and sign comparison in \(\mathbb D\), and an order-preserving embedding \(\mathbb D\hookrightarrow\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) supplies exact coefficient representations.  A \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) is finite syntax for a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign tests with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\).  For every real-closed field \(K\) containing an ordered copy of \(\mathbb D\), this syntax has the usual realization \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_K\) in its displayed free variables.  In particular, the causal realization used below is \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_{\mathbb R}\) over the ordinary real field; neither canonical probability variables nor free target-value variables are restricted to \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).

The hybrid terminal grammar is exactly
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{HybridResult}::={}&
\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{UNCOND\_QE}(\chi_T,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton})\\
&\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE\_QE}
\mid\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED\_QE}\\
&\mid\operatorname{COND\_QE}(\chi_Q,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton}),
\end{split}
\tag{1}
\]
where each displayed \(\chi\) is a \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) and \(\mathsf{isSingleton}\) is the exact Boolean output of the associated closed first-order sentence.

The deterministic procedure \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) first runs \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).  A successful rational identification is returned as \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}\).  Every other terminal invokes the graph-compatible canonical fiber
\[
S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P).
\]
Every quantifier-elimination call below is made in the first-order language of real-closed fields with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\); its computation performs only exact coefficient operations in \(\mathbb D\), and its returned syntax is interpreted over \(\mathbb R\).  For \(p_T=\Phi_{T,\mathrm{can}}^\star\), apply quantifier elimination to
\[
\varphi_T(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge t-p_T(x)=0]
\tag{2}
\]
and denote the output by \(\chi_T(t)\).  Apply it to the closed sentence
\[
\exists t_1,t_2\,[\chi_T(t_1)\wedge\chi_T(t_2)\wedge t_1\ne t_2]
\tag{3}
\]
and to
\[
\chi_T(\ell)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow\ell\leq t],
\qquad
\chi_T(u)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow t\leq u]
\tag{4}
\]
to form the singleton Boolean and endpoint formulas.

For a conditional target put \(e=\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\) and \(n=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\).  Define
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf Z:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf N:&\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0]
\ \wedge\ \exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf P:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0].
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Three quantifier-elimination calls yield closed quantifier-free formulas whose exact constant sign evaluations decide \(\mathsf Z\), \(\mathsf N\), and \(\mathsf P\).  On any explicitly supplied nonempty canonical fiber, the single closed formula in \(\mathsf P\) is the reusable uniform-positivity decision; the full block in \((5)\) is used when a failed positivity screen must be classified as uniform zero or mixed zero and positive evidence.  The zero, mixed, and positive meanings and the two payload-free terminal labels are unchanged after replacing \(S\) consistently throughout the block.  The first two cases return the corresponding payload-free evidence terminals.  Only in case \(\mathsf P\) is quantifier elimination applied to
\[
\varphi_Q(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0\wedge e(x)t-n(x)=0]
\tag{6}
\]
to form \(\chi_Q(t)\), its singleton Boolean, and endpoint formulas as in \((3)\)--\((4)\).  The procedure returns formulas and decisions only: it returns no explicit endpoint value, algebraic sample, cylindrical algebraic decomposition trace, canonical parameter, or paired SCM.
defs.def:regime-block-acquisition:
Fix a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record.  Each \(e\in\mathcal U\) is a realizable finite block of typed descriptors, possibly with deterministic finite postprocessing.  Acquiring \(e\) reveals the complete finite law of every declared output, including every normalization-dependent complementary cell, equivalently a dependent row-value block \((R_e,p_e)\), at cost \(c_e>0\).  Require joint realizability of the whole experiment menu:
\[
\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}
=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal U\}
\ne\varnothing.
\]
For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define
\[
\mathcal K_S
=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\}.
\]
The checked lower bound \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D>0\) persists on every subface.  Hence every local subset is uniformly positive before acquisition, no subset-specific evidence screen is needed, and one may define the local row-face possibly optimal set by
\[
\operatorname{PO}(S)
=\left\{\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}:
\exists q\in\mathcal K_S\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ 
(n_{\rho,D}-n_{\sigma,D})^{\mathsf T}q\geq0\right\}.
\]
Finally set
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),
\qquad
f(S)=|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|-|\operatorname{PO}(S)|,
\]
and define the local ex-post acquisition problem by
\[
\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}.
\]
This construction is the computationally cheap district row-face layer and is the uniformly-positive special case of subset-screened global acquisition.  It does not declare \(\mathcal K_S\) to be the exact projection of the broad multi-district compatibility fiber: that equality requires the separately stated augmented focal-saturation and baseline-averaged separation hypotheses.
defs.def:target-arm-rows:
For a fixed district \(D\), a total record \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) consists of: a finite nonempty arm set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); for every \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(B_\rho\cap E)\) trace and its constructed row \(n_{\rho,D}\); one accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(E)\) trace and its constructed row \(d_D\); a rational or real-algebraic number \(\varepsilon_D>0\); and an exact certificate that
\[
d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D
\qquad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Only from such a record define, for \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\),
\[
Q_\rho(q)=\frac{n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q}{d_D^{\mathsf T}q},
\qquad
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}.
\]
Separately, for any target cell \(C\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) trace constructs the generic target row \(b_D=\operatorname{row}_D(C)\).  If a required locality trace rejects, the corresponding row, comparison, or target value is undefined rather than silently assigned a row.

node.statement:
Assume that the exact global acquisition instance of \(\mathrm{def:global\text{-}regime\text{-}block\text{-}acquisition}\) is admissible.  Then \(\Lambda_S\ne\varnothing\) for every \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), and
\[
S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{exp}}}\subseteq\Lambda_S.
\]
The full-fiber evidence test on \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\) returns uniform zero evidence or mixed zero and positive evidence exactly in those two cases and then defines no numerical full-menu arm-ranking benchmark.  In the remaining case \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\mathcal U)\) holds and the acquisition problem is defined, even if \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\varnothing)\) fails.

For every \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\) is decided exactly by one closed quantifier-elimination call.  Whenever it holds, there exists \(\epsilon_S>0\) such that
\[
\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star)\geq\epsilon_S
\qquad\text{for every }\vartheta\in\Lambda_S,
\]
and, for each \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), membership \(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) is decided exactly by one closed existential formula over the reals.  Moreover,
\[
S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\bigl(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\Longrightarrow
\operatorname{Pos}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})\bigr),
\]
and, when both possibly-optimal sets are defined,
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})
\subseteq\operatorname{PO}_G(S).
\]
Consequently the feasible design family is upward closed.  Exhaustive enumeration returns every minimum-cost solution, including every cost tie, using at most
\[
2^{|\mathcal U|}
\]
subset-positivity quantifier-elimination calls and at most
\[
2^{|\mathcal U|}|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|
\]
membership calls, in addition to one joint-realizability call and a fixed full-fiber status classification.

For every positive subset \(S\), \(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) is exactly the set of arms that are conditionally optimal in at least one original-alphabet SCM family in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P_S)\).  Thus the subset-specific ranking semantics are exact for every finite sparse ADMG.

Whenever the same augmented information is represented by a local \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) system, its checked base-face evidence lower bound makes every subset positive and broad compatibility implies
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\subseteq\operatorname{PO}(S).
\]
If, for that augmented menu, the checked arm events are focal-district local and the focal projection hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\) hold, then equality holds.  Hence the existing local LP acquisition is the uniformly-positive special case and remains an outer pruning relaxation outside those projection hypotheses.

The two-experiment Boolean-pushforward instance of \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}layer3\text{-}acquisition\text{-}obstruction}\) has \(E=\top\), so every subset is positive, its displayed possibly-optimal table also holds with \(\operatorname{PO}_G\), and \(f_G\) is not submodular in general; its unique exact broad-model solution buys both experiments at total cost two.  Separately, there is a realizable one-domain binary singleton-district instance with one complete Boolean-output experiment for which \(\Lambda_{\varnothing}=[0,1]\), the evidence map is \(e(q)=q\), and the acquired law fixes \(q=1\).  Thus base evidence is mixed while the full fiber is uniformly positive; this second instance demonstrates acquisition of definability and is not a second non-submodularity witness.
node.justification: This theorem makes sparse-ADMG acquisition exact on every positive augmented broad-model fiber and allows the acquired full menu itself to establish conditional definability.
node.gap: Existing transported-bandit and Layer-3 identification results do not give an exact finite-menu acquisition objective with subset-specific evidence screening over heterogeneous sparse-ADMG canonical fibers.
node.consumer: Exact quantifier elimination screens each candidate subset, preserves every least-cost tie, and returns the cheapest acquired menu matching the positive full-menu arm set.
node.proof_tex:
Let \(S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}\subseteq\mathcal U\).  By
\(\mathrm{def:global\text{-}regime\text{-}block\text{-}acquisition}\), the menu
\(\mathcal P_{T_{\mathrm{exp}}}\) contains every complete cell equation in
\(\mathcal P_S\).  Applying the same equations in
\(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}fiber}\) therefore gives
\[
\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\subseteq
\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{exp}}}\subseteq\Lambda_S.
\tag{1}
\]
Admissibility gives \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\ne\varnothing\), so every fiber in
\((1)\) is nonempty.  Each is a closed subset of the finite canonical parameter
space and hence is compact; all of its constraints are polynomial equalities and
inequalities.

Put
\[
e(\vartheta)=
\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star).
\tag{2}
\]
Recursive probability semantics gives \(e\geq0\) on every canonical fiber.  Apply
the reusable block in \(\mathrm{def:hybrid\text{-}result\text{-}grammar}\) to the
nonempty full fiber \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\).  Exact quantifier elimination from
\(\mathrm{lem:basu\text{-}mohammad\text{-}nezhad\text{-}quantifier\text{-}elimination}\)
decides precisely the mutually exclusive alternatives
\[
 e\equiv0,
\qquad
\bigl(\min e=0<\max e\bigr),
\qquad
e>0\text{ everywhere on }\Lambda_{\mathcal U}.
\tag{3}
\]
The first two alternatives are exactly the two payload-free failures prescribed by
the acquisition definition.  The last alternative is
\(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\mathcal U)\) by
\(\mathrm{def:global\text{-}subset\text{-}positivity}\), so and only so the numerical
full-menu benchmark is defined.

Fix any \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\).  The defining formula
\[
\neg\exists\vartheta\,
\left[\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\wedge e(\vartheta)=0\right]
\tag{4}
\]
is a closed first-order formula over the reals with coefficients in the effective
ordered ring generated by the complete augmented menu.  The cited
quantifier-elimination result makes \((4)\) one exact decision.  If \((4)\) holds,
continuity of \(e\), compactness and nonemptiness give an attained minimum
\[
\epsilon_S:=\min_{\vartheta\in\Lambda_S}e(\vartheta)>0.
\tag{5}
\]
Conversely, \((5)\) excludes a zero and hence implies \((4)\).  Thus the displayed
predicate is exactly uniform strict positivity, including on a boundary fiber.

The inclusion in \((1)\) proves the positivity monotonicity: if
\(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\) holds and \(S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}\), a zero of
\(e\) in \(\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{exp}}}\) would also be a zero in \(\Lambda_S\), a
contradiction.  Suppose both possibly-optimal sets are defined and
\(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})\).  There is then
\(\vartheta\in\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{exp}}}\subseteq\Lambda_S\) satisfying
\[
n_\rho(\vartheta)-n_\sigma(\vartheta)\geq0
\qquad(\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}),
\tag{6}
\]
so the same point witnesses \(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\).  Hence
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})
\subseteq\operatorname{PO}_G(S).
\tag{7}
\]
If \(S\) is feasible and \(S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}\), positivity monotonicity
and \((7)\), applied also to \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}\subseteq\mathcal U\), yield
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(\mathcal U)
\subseteq\operatorname{PO}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})
\subseteq\operatorname{PO}_G(S)
=\operatorname{PO}_G(\mathcal U).
\tag{8}
\]
Thus \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}\) is feasible, proving upward closure.

For a positive \(S\) and fixed \(\rho\), the membership condition is the single
closed existential formula
\[
\exists\vartheta\left[
\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\ \wedge\
\bigwedge_{\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}}
\{n_\rho(\vartheta)-n_\sigma(\vartheta)\geq0\}
\right].
\tag{9}
\]
Every constraint in \((9)\) is polynomial over the same effective ordered
coefficient ring, so quantifier elimination decides it exactly.  Enumerating the
\(2^{|\mathcal U|}\) subsets uses at most that many calls for \((4)\) and at most
\(2^{|\mathcal U|}|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|\) calls for \((9)\).  One existential
call verifies \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\ne\varnothing\), and a fixed number of calls
classifies the full fiber as in \((3)\).  Once the Boolean answers are known, exact
finite comparison of the effectively comparable positive costs retains every
feasible set of least total cost, including ties.  The full set is feasible under
\(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\mathcal U)\), so the optimization has a solution.

We next prove that this numerical program ranks causal conditionals rather than
merely canonical numerator polynomials.  For a positive \(S\), apply
\(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}global\text{-}canonical\text{-}frontier}\) to the complete
augmented menu \(\mathcal P_S\) and to the joint finite cell collection
\[
\{B_\tau\cap E:\tau\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\}\cup\{E\}.
\tag{10}
\]
It gives equality of the entire range in \((10)\) between \(\Lambda_S\) and
original-alphabet families in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P_S)\).  By \((5)\), for every
pair of arms,
\[
\frac{n_\rho(\vartheta)}{e(\vartheta)}
\geq
\frac{n_\sigma(\vartheta)}{e(\vartheta)}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
n_\rho(\vartheta)-n_\sigma(\vartheta)\geq0.
\tag{11}
\]
The equivalence uses multiplication by the common strictly positive denominator,
not a definition of the causal target.  Joint range equality and \((11)\) prove that
\(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) is exactly the set of arms conditionally optimal in some
broad compatible original-alphabet family.

Suppose now that the augmented information is also represented by a checked local
row system.  By \(\mathrm{def:target\text{-}arm\text{-}rows}\), its base-face
certificate gives
\[
d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D>0
\qquad(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)).
\tag{12}
\]
Every acquired subface lies inside the base face.  Moreover,
\(\mathrm{lem:district\text{-}cell\text{-}linearity}\) maps every broad compatible
model to its local response law in \(\mathcal K_S\) and maps evidence to
\(d_D^{\mathsf T}q\).  Thus \((12)\) makes every corresponding global subset
positive.  A broad witness for \(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) supplies a
\(q\in\mathcal K_S\) satisfying all local numerator inequalities, proving
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\subseteq\operatorname{PO}(S).
\tag{13}
\]
Under the augmented focal projection hypotheses,
\(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\) realizes every
\(q\in\mathcal K_S\) by a family in
\(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P_S)\subseteq\mathcal C(\mathcal P_S)\).
The same numerator and evidence equations reverse \((13)\).  This proves the local
bridge without identifying the row face with the broad fiber outside those
hypotheses.

For non-submodularity, use the one-domain binary bow construction in
\(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}layer3\text{-}acquisition\text{-}obstruction}\).  Its
common evidence is \(\top\), so \(e=1\) on every augmented fiber.  Its explicit
response-block realization gives, for every \(S\subseteq\{e_1,e_2\}\),
\[
\{q_D^\star(\vartheta):\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\}=\mathcal K_S.
\tag{14}
\]
The possibly-optimal table and the increasing marginal gain proved there therefore
hold verbatim for \(\operatorname{PO}_G\) and \(f_G\).  Both experiments, and only
both, reproduce the full possibly-optimal set, so the unique cost is two.

Finally, the promised definability-acquisition check uses the one-domain graph with
one parentless binary vertex \(Y\), hence one singleton district and response
profiles \(Y=0\) and \(Y=1\).  Let
\[
q=P(Y=1),\qquad E=\{Y=1\},
\tag{15}
\]
and let the base menu contain only a constant Boolean output, which imposes no
constraint on \(q\).  Thus \(\Lambda_{\varnothing}=[0,1]\) and \(e(q)=q\).  Take a
single candidate experiment that discloses the complete law of the Boolean output
\(Y\), with \(P(Y=1)=1\) and \(P(Y=0)=0\).  The two complete cells impose exactly
\(q=1\), so \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}=\{1\}\).  Both endpoint response laws are finite
recursive SCMs on the original binary alphabet, so the menu is realizable.  The
base fiber contains both a zero-evidence and a positive-evidence law, whereas the
full fiber has evidence one.  With a singleton arm set the full numerical benchmark
is well defined.  This proves the claimed strict usefulness of full-menu positivity;
with one experiment and one arm it makes no separate non-submodularity claim.

lem:district-cell-linearity.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted extraction record, a compatible family \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), and a retained pair \((h,c)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus\text{-}soundness}\), the two constructive derivations in the record satisfy
\[
N_{s,a,D,h,c}(\mathcal P)=P_{M^s}(A_{h,c}),
\qquad
H_{s,a,D,h}(\mathcal P)=P_{M^s}(H_h).
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:typed\text{-}extraction\text{-}judgment}\), the two accepting locality traces have constructed rows \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and \(v_{s,a,D,h}\).  The exhaustive tables in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\) give, for every complete nonfocal response profile \(\omega_{-D}\),
\[
\mathbf 1_{A_{h,c}}(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})
=r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D),
\qquad
\mathbf 1_{H_h}(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})
=v_{s,a,D,h}(\omega_D).
\tag{2}
\]
Recursive compatibility makes the evaluated indicators deterministic after all response profiles are fixed.  District factorization makes the nonfocal response law a probability law independent of the focal block.  Summing \((2)\) first over that law and then over \(q_D^s\), finite total probability yields
\[
P_{M^s}(A_{h,c})=r_{s,a,D,h,c}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s,
\qquad
P_{M^s}(H_h)=v_{s,a,D,h}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s.
\tag{3}
\]
The stored certificate \(\pi_h\) is valid by extraction-calculus soundness and proves the second quantity in \((3)\) strictly positive.  Thus the quotient constructor is legal, and \((1)\)--\((3)\) give
\[
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)
=\frac{N_{s,a,D,h,c}}{H_{s,a,D,h}}
=\frac{r_{s,a,D,h,c}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s}
{v_{s,a,D,h}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s}.
\tag{4}
\]
No row equality was assumed in the extraction record; equations \((3)\) are derived from exhaustive locality and total probability.

For a complete supplied output cell, \(\mathrm{ass:typed\text{-}menu\text{-}realizability}\) gives directly
\[
P_a^s(y)=\mathcal L_{M^s}(f_a(T_a))(y)
=P_{M^s}\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Its accepting locality table, followed by the same total-probability calculation as \((2)\)--\((3)\), gives
\[
P_a^s(y)=(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y})^{\mathsf T}q_D^s.
\tag{6}
\]
The preimage identity is used only to evaluate the indicator in the locality table; no probability \(P(T_a=t)\) is treated as supplied unless separately declared.

If \(s=\star\), equations \((4)\) and \((6)\) already use the target law.  If \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), district-kernel invariance gives \(q_D^s=q_D^\star\).  District closure rules out a partial-district substitution.  These are the only admissible transport cases in the stacked system.  Finally apply \((2)\)--\((3)\) in the target domain to the accepting traces stored by \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\), and to an accepting generic target trace, to obtain
\[
P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E)=n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star,
\quad
P_{M^\star}(E)=d_D^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star,
\quad
P_{M^\star}(C)=b_D^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star.
\tag{7}
\]
By the definitions of the judgment and stacked system, every rejected check creates no row.  This proves every clause.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\).  For every retained \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\),
\[
N_{s,a,D,h,c}=r_{s,a,D,h,c}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s,
\qquad
H_{s,a,D,h}=v_{s,a,D,h}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s>0,
\]
and therefore
\[
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=
\frac{r_{s,a,D,h,c}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s}
{v_{s,a,D,h}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s}.
\]
Only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) may \(q_D^s\) be replaced by \(q_D^\star\).  Every accepted raw supplied output cell satisfies \(P_a^s(y)=(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y})^{\mathsf T}q_D^s\), with the same admissibility requirement for transport.  A \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record gives the target numerator and evidence equations \(P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E)=n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star\) and \(P_{M^\star}(E)=d_D^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star\); an accepted generic target locality trace gives \(P_{M^\star}(C)=b_D^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star\).  Every rejected extraction, locality, positivity, or admissibility check contributes no row.

defs.def:district-response-profile: For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), set \(\Omega_D=\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\), the finite set of all tuples \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) of deterministic response maps at every parent configuration allowed by \(G\) and \(\mathcal X\).  For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\) is the joint law of the response maps induced by \(M^s\).  The carrier is query independent and includes every configuration needed by any target, menu, deterministic postprocessor, or later acquired regime.
defs.def:finite-extraction-calculus:
The finite extraction calculus has event syntax
\[
\mathsf{XEvent}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\top\mid\bot\mid
\neg\mathsf{XEvent}\mid
\bigsqcup_{j\in J}\mathsf{XEvent}_j\mid
\operatorname{Marg}_{W}(\mathsf{XEvent})\mid
\operatorname{Fix}(\mathsf{FixTrace},\mathsf{XEvent}),
\]
where \(J\) and every marginalized alphabet are finite, and a disjoint-union node carries a complete pointwise disjointness table.  The cell event is
\[
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its probability leaf is the supplied output cell \(P_a^s(y)\).  Only its recursively evaluated indicator is expanded by the finite identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\};
\tag{1}
\]
the tuple-cell probabilities on the right of \((1)\) are not menu generators unless an identity-output tuple descriptor is separately supplied.

Menu expressions have syntax
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{XExpr}::={}&
\operatorname{CellProb}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j
\mid\mathsf{XExpr}-\mathsf{XExpr}
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j\\
&\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\pi_H),
\end{split}
\]
where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\pi_H\) is a separately checkable strict-positivity certificate on its declared compatibility fiber.  A derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) is generated only by an output-cell lookup, the truth-table identity \((1)\), contradiction or sure-event evaluation, finite disjoint additivity, complementation, finite marginalization, multiplication of independent original-district factors, and a checked fixing trace.

A fixing trace is a finite tree whose leaves are event or expression derivations and whose constructors are identity, typed substitution from a fixed finite registry of sound Boolean or fixing identities, finite disjoint sum, finite product, complement, marginalization, conditional quotient with a separately checked positive denominator, composition, and cleared-denominator comparison.  Every constructor stores all of its children and type data.  A comparison node is accepted only when cross-multiplication is legal under its stored denominator certificates and coefficient-by-coefficient normalization gives the zero polynomial.  The identity registry is finite and contains only pointwise Boolean identities, finite total-probability identities, and the fixing identities explicitly verified by recursive substitution of structural response tables.  Thus no constructor contains the semantic equality it is intended to establish.

Positivity certificates are either a positive rational constant after exact normalization, a rational Farkas identity for a linear face, or a displayed finite preordering identity
\[
p-\varepsilon=
\sum_i\tau_i h_i+
\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}\sigma_J
\prod_{j\in J}g_j,
\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
where the declared fiber has equations \(h_i=0\), inequalities \(g_j\geq0\), and every \(\sigma_J\) is checked coefficient by coefficient to be a finite sum of squares.  All polynomial equalities are checked by exact integer or rational coefficient comparison.

For an event \(A\) and a district \(D\), the total procedure \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) enumerates
\[
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\longmapsto
\mathbf 1\{A\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\}
\]
over the complete finite response carriers.  It accepts exactly when every two entries with the same \(\omega_D\) agree, and then returns their common row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\).  Otherwise it returns the first disagreeing pair in the canonical order.  All syntax trees, registries, coefficient vectors, truth tables, and searches are finite and canonically ordered.
defs.def:incidence-row:
For every successful row-eligibility record define the separate numerator and context rows
\[
\begin{split}
r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)
&=\mathbf 1\{A_{h,c}\text{ has the common value certified by }
\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\},\\
v_{s,a,D,h}(\omega_D)
&=\mathbf 1\{H_h\text{ has the common value certified by }
\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\},
\end{split}
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
For a complete supplied output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\), an accepting locality trace similarly constructs
\[
r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}=\operatorname{row}_D(C_{a,y}).
\]
The quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) is not an incidence row.
defs.def:stacked-menu-system:
Fix \(D\).  Enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete output cell, and extraction record canonically.  A candidate is transport admissible only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  First retain every admissible complete output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\) whose exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) table accepts, with row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}\) and supplied value \(P_a^s(y)\).  Next, for every successful extraction judgment retain separately the numerator pair
\[
(r_{s,a,D,h,c},N_{s,a,D,h,c})
\]
and the context pair
\[
(v_{s,a,D,h},H_{s,a,D,h}).
\]
Never stack the quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) as a linear row.  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) with value one and stack precisely the accepted raw, numerator, and context rows as \(A_D\), with their values in the same order as \(m_D\).  A failed locality, fixing, expression, positivity, or admissibility check contributes no row.  A rejected complete cell remains, without information loss, among the complete polynomial equalities of the exact global fiber.  For a deterministic postprocessor, recursive locality and the raw incidence row use the preimage identity \((1)\) from \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), but the stacked value is the directly supplied output probability \(P_a^s(y)\).
defs.def:target-arm-rows:
For a fixed district \(D\), a total record \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) consists of: a finite nonempty arm set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); for every \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(B_\rho\cap E)\) trace and its constructed row \(n_{\rho,D}\); one accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(E)\) trace and its constructed row \(d_D\); a rational or real-algebraic number \(\varepsilon_D>0\); and an exact certificate that
\[
d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D
\qquad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Only from such a record define, for \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\),
\[
Q_\rho(q)=\frac{n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q}{d_D^{\mathsf T}q},
\qquad
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}.
\]
Separately, for any target cell \(C\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) trace constructs the generic target row \(b_D=\operatorname{row}_D(C)\).  If a required locality trace rejects, the corresponding row, comparison, or target value is undefined rather than silently assigned a row.
defs.def:typed-extraction-judgment:
For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal Y_a)\), write
\[
\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)
\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)
\]
exactly when the finite extraction calculus constructs, for every retained \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), a numerator event \(A_{h,c}\), a context event \(H_h\), derivations
\[
\delta_N:A_{h,c}\Downarrow N_{s,a,D,h,c},
\qquad
\delta_H:H_h\Downarrow H_{s,a,D,h},
\]
two accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) traces, the rows those traces construct,
\[
r_{s,a,D,h,c}=\operatorname{row}_D(A_{h,c}),
\qquad
v_{s,a,D,h}=\operatorname{row}_D(H_h),
\]
and an independently checkable certificate \(\pi_h\) that \(H_{s,a,D,h}>0\) on the declared fiber.  The returned kernel entry is the typed expression
\[
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=
\operatorname{Quot}(N_{s,a,D,h,c},H_{s,a,D,h},\pi_h).
\]
The record \(\kappa\) contains only the event and expression derivations, locality tables, constructed rows, and positivity certificates.  It contains neither \(N=r^{\mathsf T}q\), nor \(H=v^{\mathsf T}q\), nor any equivalent semantic equality.  An unavailable cell, undefined fixing, rejected locality table, or uncertified denominator has no successful judgment and creates no row-eligibility record.

assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability:
For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), descriptor \(a\) declares a finite counterfactual tuple \(T_a\), a finite output alphabet \(\mathcal Y_a\), and a deterministic map \(f_a\) into \(\mathcal Y_a\), and
\[
P_a^s=(f_a)_\#\mathcal L_{M^s}(T_a),
\]
where an unpostprocessed descriptor has the identity output map.

thm:one-district-fiber-projection.proof_tex:
Fix \(D\), \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), and write \(q=q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\).  Completeness of \(\Omega_D\) gives \(q\geq0\) and \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}q=1\).  By the district-cell lemma, every accepted raw, numerator, and context row in \(A_D\) has the value recorded in \(m_D\), after its recorded source-admissibility proof.  Therefore
\[
A_Dq=m_D,
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\tag{1}
\]

Assume \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) and choose the single baseline \(\mathbf M^0\) in its definition.  This choice itself proves \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\).  Put
\[
K=\mathcal K_D(m_D),\quad q_0=q_D^\star(\mathbf M^0),\quad Z=Z_D(m_D),
\]
and
\[
L=\{v\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}:A_Dv=0,
\ v(\omega)=0\text{ for every }\omega\in Z\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Every difference of two points of \(K\) lies in \(L\).  Conversely, for each \(\omega\notin Z\), choose \(q^\omega\in K\) with \(q^\omega(\omega)>0\).  Their finite average \(\bar q\in K\) is positive on every coordinate outside \(Z\).  If \(v\in L\), sufficiently small \(\epsilon>0\) makes \(\bar q\pm\epsilon v\geq0\); both perturbations remain in \(K\).  Hence
\[
\operatorname{span}(K-K)=L.
\tag{3}
\]
Taking orthogonal complements gives
\[
\operatorname{span}(K-K)^\perp
=L^\perp
=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z\}
=R_D(m_D).
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(q\in K\).  Focal-district saturation permits replacement of the target law of the complete block \(U_D^\star\) by \(q\), and the same replacement in every unchanged source, while holding the focal law fixed in changed sources and holding every nonfocal structural table and latent law fixed.  District closure makes these cases exhaustive.  For a complete supplied output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\) in a domain admissible for \(D\), finite total probability under the fixed nonfocal product law gives
\[
P_{M^{q,s}}(C_{a,y})-P_{M^{0,s}}(C_{a,y})
=(\bar\chi_{C_{a,y}}^{s,\mathbf M^0})^{\mathsf T}(q-q_0).
\tag{5}
\]
The deterministic preimage is used only to evaluate the indicator defining the averaged row.  Baseline-averaged separation puts this row in \(R_D(m_D)\), while \((4)\) makes the right side of \((5)\) zero.  A changed-source focal law was not altered.  Thus every directly supplied output law is preserved.  The resulting family remains on \(\mathcal X\), belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), and induces \(q\).  Combining this surjection with \((1)\) yields
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=K.
\]
The two separation lemmas give the stated baseline-free sufficient conditions.  Without the displayed focal saturation and one-baseline preservation condition, only \((1)\) has been proved.

snapshot.stmt:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Suppose \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds.  This predicate entails \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_D(m_D)
=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}.
\]
For the single witnessing baseline \(\mathbf M^0\) in \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), every transport-admissible complete supplied cell is preserved under replacement of its focal law \(q_0\) by an arbitrary \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) because
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}(q-q_0)=0.
\]
Every boundary point of the row face is therefore induced on the declared alphabets \(\mathcal X\) by a compatible SCM family saturated only at \(D\), while every district \(D'\ne D\) retains its original graph-compatible restrictions.  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence also together with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is a convenient sufficient condition for \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\). defs.def:active-slice-separated-menu:
For a fixed district \(D\), define its active row space by
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\subseteq\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
For a complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and for
\(\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'}\), define its focal recursive-indicator slice by
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(\omega_D)
=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
The active-slice face-separation predicate \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell and every fixed nonfocal response profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  When \(D\) is the only district, the nonfocal product is the singleton empty profile.
defs.def:baseline-averaged-active-slice-menu:
Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\).  For a baseline \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), let
\[
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
=\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}q_{D'}^{0,s}(\omega_{D'}),
\qquad
\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\]
where \(q_{D'}^{0,s}\) is the response-profile law induced by \(M^{0,s}\).  For every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), define the baseline-averaged focal row
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}
\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
The baseline-averaged active-slice predicate \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when there exists one \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) such that
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell.  The same witnessing baseline must be used for all cells and all feasible replacements of the focal law; a baseline depending on the replacement law is not permitted.
defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:compatible-face:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:district-response-profile: For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), set \(\Omega_D=\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\), the finite set of all tuples \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) of deterministic response maps at every parent configuration allowed by \(G\) and \(\mathcal X\).  For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\) is the joint law of the response maps induced by \(M^s\).  The carrier is query independent and includes every configuration needed by any target, menu, deterministic postprocessor, or later acquired regime.
defs.def:district-separated-menu: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\).  This is a finite syntactic and tabular condition; it excludes an unrecorded cross-district polynomial constraint involving \(q_D^\star\).
defs.def:focal-district-saturated-model-class:
For a fixed district \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete};\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ there is exactly one finite latent block }
U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{storing one full deterministic response map for each vertex in }D
\text{ at every allowed parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation of a vertex in }D
\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&U_D^s\text{ is independent of the exogenous blocks of every }D'\ne D;\\
&\text{every probability law on }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ is permitted for }U_D^s,
\text{ subject only to equality with the target law}\\
&\text{when }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing;\\
&\text{for each }D'\ne D\text{, all structural tables, latent-factor restrictions,}
\text{ and cross-domain equalities remain those of }\mathfrak M
\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The phrase ``every probability law is permitted'' includes closure under replacing the law of \(U_D^\star\) and all its unchanged-source copies while holding all mechanisms and latent laws in districts \(D'\ne D\), and all changed-source copies of \(U_D\), fixed. Define
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]

A candidate is transport admissible only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  First retain every admissible complete output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\) whose exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) table accepts, with row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}\) and supplied value \(P_a^s(y)\).  Next, for every successful extraction judgment retain separately the numerator pair
\[
(r_{s,a,D,h,c},N_{s,a,D,h,c})
\]
and the context pair

\]

Prepend \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) with value one and stack precisely the accepted raw, numerator, and context rows as \(A_D\), with their values in the same order as \(m_D\). defs.def:finite-extraction-calculus:
The finite extraction calculus has event syntax
\[
\mathsf{XEvent}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\top\mid\bot\mid
\neg\mathsf{XEvent}\mid
\bigsqcup_{j\in J}\mathsf{XEvent}_j\mid
\operatorname{Marg}_{W}(\mathsf{XEvent})\mid
\operatorname{Fix}(\mathsf{FixTrace},\mathsf{XEvent}),
\]
where \(J\) and every marginalized alphabet are finite, and a disjoint-union node carries a complete pointwise disjointness table.  The cell event is
\[
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its probability leaf is the supplied output cell \(P_a^s(y)\).  Only its recursively evaluated indicator is expanded by the finite identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\};
\tag{1}
\]
the tuple-cell probabilities on the right of \((1)\) are not menu generators unless an identity-output tuple descriptor is separately supplied.

Menu expressions have syntax
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{XExpr}::={}&
\operatorname{CellProb}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j
\mid\mathsf{XExpr}-\mathsf{XExpr}
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j\\
&\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\pi_H),
\end{split}
\]
where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\pi_H\) is a separately checkable strict-positivity certificate on its declared compatibility fiber.  A derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) is generated only by an output-cell lookup, the truth-table identity \((1)\), contradiction or sure-event evaluation, finite disjoint additivity, complementation, finite marginalization, multiplication of independent original-district factors, and a checked fixing trace.

A fixing trace is a finite tree whose leaves are event or expression derivations and whose constructors are identity, typed substitution from a fixed finite registry of sound Boolean or fixing identities, finite disjoint sum, finite product, complement, marginalization, conditional quotient with a separately checked positive denominator, composition, and cleared-denominator comparison.  Every constructor stores all of its children and type data.  A comparison node is accepted only when cross-multiplication is legal under its stored denominator certificates and coefficient-by-coefficient normalization gives the zero polynomial.  The identity registry is finite and contains only pointwise Boolean identities, finite total-probability identities, and the fixing identities explicitly verified by recursive substitution of structural response tables.  Thus no constructor contains the semantic equality it is intended to establish.

Positivity certificates are either a positive rational constant after exact normalization, a rational Farkas identity for a linear face, or a displayed finite preordering identity
\[
p-\varepsilon=
\sum_i\tau_i h_i+
\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}\sigma_J
\prod_{j\in J}g_j,
\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
where the declared fiber has equations \(h_i=0\), inequalities \(g_j\geq0\), and every \(\sigma_J\) is checked coefficient by coefficient to be a finite sum of squares.  All polynomial equalities are checked by exact integer or rational coefficient comparison.

For an event \(A\) and a district \(D\), the total procedure \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) enumerates
\[
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\longmapsto
\mathbf 1\{A\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\}
\]
over the complete finite response carriers.  It accepts exactly when every two entries with the same \(\omega_D\) agree, and then returns their common row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\).  Otherwise it returns the first disagreeing pair in the canonical order.  All syntax trees, registries, coefficient vectors, truth tables, and searches are finite and canonically ordered.
