thm:face-aware-identification.proof_tex:
Let the target locality judgment accept.  By the district-cell lemma,
\[
P_{M^\star}(C)=b_D^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star.
\tag{1}
\]
If
\[
b_D=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_D+
\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega,
\tag{2}
\]
then broad projection gives \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\), while forced-zero coordinates vanish.  Multiplying \((2)\) by \(q_D^\star\) yields the identifying map
\[
P_{M^\star}(C)=\lambda^{\mathsf T}m_D.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus the observed-law functional is proved equal to, rather than defined as, the causal target.

Under \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\), exact focal projection and the orthogonal identity give
\[
b_D^{\mathsf T}q\text{ constant on }\mathcal K_D(m_D)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad b_D\in R_D(m_D).
\tag{4}
\]
If membership fails, \((4)\) supplies two face laws with unequal values, and exact focal projection lifts them to original-alphabet same-menu families while fixing every nonfocal district.  The separation hierarchy supplies the stated simpler checks.  If target locality rejects, \((1)\) is unavailable; without focal projection, row-face witnesses need not lift.  This proves every exact clause and its limitation.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) accepts and constructs \(b_D=\operatorname{row}_D(C)\).  For the broad compatibility fiber, membership in
\[
b_D\in R_D(m_D)
=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\]
is sufficient to identify the causal target \(P_{M^\star}(C)\), with explicit value \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}m_D\) whenever
\[
b_D=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_D+
\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega.
\]
If additionally \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, membership is necessary for constancy on \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\).  On that focal-district-saturated baseline-averaged class, failure yields two original-alphabet compatible SCM families with identical supplied laws and unequal target-cell probabilities while every \(D'\ne D\) retains its baseline graph-compatible restrictions.  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is sufficient for this exact clause.  If target locality rejects, or outside the baseline-averaged focal-projection scope, no such local converse is asserted.

defs.def:active-slice-separated-menu:
For a fixed district \(D\), define its active row space by
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\subseteq\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
For a complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and for
\(\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'}\), define its focal recursive-indicator slice by
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(\omega_D)
=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
The active-slice face-separation predicate \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell and every fixed nonfocal response profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  When \(D\) is the only district, the nonfocal product is the singleton empty profile.
defs.def:baseline-averaged-active-slice-menu:
Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\).  For a baseline \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), let
\[
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
=\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}q_{D'}^{0,s}(\omega_{D'}),
\qquad
\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\]
where \(q_{D'}^{0,s}\) is the response-profile law induced by \(M^{0,s}\).  For every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), define the baseline-averaged focal row
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}
\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
The baseline-averaged active-slice predicate \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when there exists one \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) such that
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell.  The same witnessing baseline must be used for all cells and all feasible replacements of the focal law; a baseline depending on the replacement law is not permitted.
defs.def:compatible-face:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:district-separated-menu: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\).  This is a finite syntactic and tabular condition; it excludes an unrecorded cross-district polynomial constraint involving \(q_D^\star\).
defs.def:finite-extraction-calculus:
The finite extraction calculus has event syntax
\[
\mathsf{XEvent}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\top\mid\bot\mid
\neg\mathsf{XEvent}\mid
\bigsqcup_{j\in J}\mathsf{XEvent}_j\mid
\operatorname{Marg}_{W}(\mathsf{XEvent})\mid
\operatorname{Fix}(\mathsf{FixTrace},\mathsf{XEvent}),
\]
where \(J\) and every marginalized alphabet are finite, and a disjoint-union node carries a complete pointwise disjointness table.  The cell event is
\[
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its probability leaf is the supplied output cell \(P_a^s(y)\).  Only its recursively evaluated indicator is expanded by the finite identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\};
\tag{1}
\]
the tuple-cell probabilities on the right of \((1)\) are not menu generators unless an identity-output tuple descriptor is separately supplied.

Menu expressions have syntax
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{XExpr}::={}&
\operatorname{CellProb}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j
\mid\mathsf{XExpr}-\mathsf{XExpr}
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j\\
&\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\pi_H),
\end{split}
\]
where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\pi_H\) is a separately checkable strict-positivity certificate on its declared compatibility fiber.  A derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) is generated only by an output-cell lookup, the truth-table identity \((1)\), contradiction or sure-event evaluation, finite disjoint additivity, complementation, finite marginalization, multiplication of independent original-district factors, and a checked fixing trace.

A fixing trace is a finite tree whose leaves are event or expression derivations and whose constructors are identity, typed substitution from a fixed finite registry of sound Boolean or fixing identities, finite disjoint sum, finite product, complement, marginalization, conditional quotient with a separately checked positive denominator, composition, and cleared-denominator comparison.  Every constructor stores all of its children and type data.  A comparison node is accepted only when cross-multiplication is legal under its stored denominator certificates and coefficient-by-coefficient normalization gives the zero polynomial.  The identity registry is finite and contains only pointwise Boolean identities, finite total-probability identities, and the fixing identities explicitly verified by recursive substitution of structural response tables.  Thus no constructor contains the semantic equality it is intended to establish.

Positivity certificates are either a positive rational constant after exact normalization, a rational Farkas identity for a linear face, or a displayed finite preordering identity
\[
p-\varepsilon=
\sum_i\tau_i h_i+
\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}\sigma_J
\prod_{j\in J}g_j,
\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
where the declared fiber has equations \(h_i=0\), inequalities \(g_j\geq0\), and every \(\sigma_J\) is checked coefficient by coefficient to be a finite sum of squares.  All polynomial equalities are checked by exact integer or rational coefficient comparison.

For an event \(A\) and a district \(D\), the total procedure \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) enumerates
\[
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\longmapsto
\mathbf 1\{A\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\}
\]
over the complete finite response carriers.  It accepts exactly when every two entries with the same \(\omega_D\) agree, and then returns their common row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\).  Otherwise it returns the first disagreeing pair in the canonical order.  All syntax trees, registries, coefficient vectors, truth tables, and searches are finite and canonically ordered.
defs.def:focal-district-saturated-model-class:
For a fixed district \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete};\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ there is exactly one finite latent block }
U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{storing one full deterministic response map for each vertex in }D
\text{ at every allowed parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation of a vertex in }D
\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&U_D^s\text{ is independent of the exogenous blocks of every }D'\ne D;\\
&\text{every probability law on }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ is permitted for }U_D^s,
\text{ subject only to equality with the target law}\\
&\text{when }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing;\\
&\text{for each }D'\ne D\text{, all structural tables, latent-factor restrictions,}
\text{ and cross-domain equalities remain those of }\mathfrak M
\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The phrase ``every probability law is permitted'' includes closure under replacing the law of \(U_D^\star\) and all its unchanged-source copies while holding all mechanisms and latent laws in districts \(D'\ne D\), and all changed-source copies of \(U_D\), fixed. Define
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:stacked-menu-system:
Fix \(D\).  Enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete output cell, and extraction record canonically.  A candidate is transport admissible only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  First retain every admissible complete output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\) whose exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) table accepts, with row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}\) and supplied value \(P_a^s(y)\).  Next, for every successful extraction judgment retain separately the numerator pair
\[
(r_{s,a,D,h,c},N_{s,a,D,h,c})
\]
and the context pair
\[
(v_{s,a,D,h},H_{s,a,D,h}).
\]
Never stack the quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) as a linear row.  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) with value one and stack precisely the accepted raw, numerator, and context rows as \(A_D\), with their values in the same order as \(m_D\).  A failed locality, fixing, expression, positivity, or admissibility check contributes no row.  A rejected complete cell remains, without information loss, among the complete polynomial equalities of the exact global fiber.  For a deterministic postprocessor, recursive locality and the raw incidence row use the preimage identity \((1)\) from \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), but the stacked value is the directly supplied output probability \(P_a^s(y)\).
defs.def:typed-extraction-judgment:
For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal Y_a)\), write
\[
\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)
\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)
\]
exactly when the finite extraction calculus constructs, for every retained \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), a numerator event \(A_{h,c}\), a context event \(H_h\), derivations
\[
\delta_N:A_{h,c}\Downarrow N_{s,a,D,h,c},
\qquad
\delta_H:H_h\Downarrow H_{s,a,D,h},
\]
two accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) traces, the rows those traces construct,
\[
r_{s,a,D,h,c}=\operatorname{row}_D(A_{h,c}),
\qquad
v_{s,a,D,h}=\operatorname{row}_D(H_h),
\]
and an independently checkable certificate \(\pi_h\) that \(H_{s,a,D,h}>0\) on the declared fiber.  The returned kernel entry is the typed expression
\[
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=
\operatorname{Quot}(N_{s,a,D,h,c},H_{s,a,D,h},\pi_h).
\]

lem:dctftr-transition-preservation.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  At normalization, every rewrite is a checked pointwise Boolean equality; for a postprocessed output the only additional identity is
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Finite total probability proves ancestor marginalization.  At split, recursive determinism and district factorization give the exact original-district formula
\[
P_{M^\star}(C)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1_C(\omega)
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^\star(\omega_D),
\tag{2}
\]
which is exactly the denotation of the successor sum-product DAG.  Thus no factorization for districts of an induced subgraph is invoked.

At extraction, the district-cell lemma proves every accepted raw, numerator, and context row equation after the recorded admissibility proof.  These rows are stacked separately, no quotient is stacked, and literal replay gives
\[
A_Dq_D^\star=m_D.
\tag{3}
\]
Rejected candidates contribute no row.  At face identification, the checked decomposition and the forced zeros give
\[
b_D^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star
=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_Dq_D^\star
+\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega q_D^\star(\omega)
=\lambda^{\mathsf T}m_D.
\tag{4}
\]
Ready sums preserve denotation by finite additivity and ready products by \((2)\).  Condition retains the same two root values and divides only under its independently checked uniform strict-positivity certificate.  Hence every nonterminal rule preserves both root denotations pointwise.

Operationally, the first seven rules fix all earlier rank coordinates and strictly decrease respectively \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi\); condition changes \(r_C=1\) to zero only after those coordinates vanish.  No rule creates an earlier-phase node.  Fixed priority and the least-node convention select one successor.  Every failed parser, original-district enumeration, locality test, extraction, face test, or denominator test has an explicit typed failure branch.  Therefore a least unresolved phase cannot be stuck.  This proves strict rank decrease, uniqueness of successors, denotation preservation, and unreachability of \(\operatorname{STUCK}\).

snapshot.stmt: For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), each nonterminal \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), or \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\) step preserves the ordered pair of root denotations pointwise. The preservation witnesses are respectively the checked normalization derivation, finite ancestor marginalization identity, checked district sum-product derivation, admissible extraction equations \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\), active-face calculation, finite additivity, and district factorization. The \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) rule labels its terminal with the same two root values and divides only under an independent strict-positivity certificate. In the rank \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\), the first seven rules respectively decrease \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi}\) while fixing every earlier coordinate, and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) decreases \(r_C\) after the others vanish; no rule creates an earlier-phase node. The fixed priority and least-applicable-node convention give a unique successor. From a well-typed initial configuration, \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable because every declared partial-operation failure takes its specified \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) branch.

defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:dctftr-grammar:
Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, domains, descriptors, districts, assignments, complete response profiles, and generated work-DAG identifiers.  The counterfactual syntax is
\[
\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]V_\alpha=v,
\qquad
\mathsf{Event}::=\top\mid\bot\mid\mathsf{Atom}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},
\]
where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term.  A descriptor declares a finite returned counterfactual tuple \(T_a\), a finite output alphabet \(\mathcal Y_a\), and a deterministic map \(f_a\).  Its output cell is the event \(\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\); the parser uses the pointwise preimage identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\}
\tag{1}
\]
only for normalization, locality tables, and response-profile evaluation.  The expression leaf for this cell is the directly supplied number \(P_a^s(y)\), not a collection of unsupplied tuple-cell probabilities.  Normalized events are canonical disjoint normal forms of consistent unnested atoms, including contradiction and sure-event forms.

Identified expressions have grammar
\[
\mathsf{Expr}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\nu_H),
\]
where \(J\) is finite, \(r\in\mathbb Q\), and \(\nu_H\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate on the declared fiber.  The phase-indexed work-node grammar is
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{Goal}::={}&
\operatorname{Raw}(\tau,e)
\mid\operatorname{Normed}(\tau,e,\nu)
\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(\tau,H,e,\alpha)
\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\\
&\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(\tau,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)
\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),
\end{split}
\]
with \(\tau\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\) and an accepting locality trace \(\ell\) on every row-needed node.  A configuration \(\mathsf{Config}\) is a finite well-typed acyclic DAG of these nodes, two distinguished roots, and a checked transition trace.

For \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), raw, normalized, and ancestor-closed nodes denote their target-domain event probabilities.  A row or face node at \((D,b)\) denotes \(b^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\), a resolved node denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\), and sum and product nodes denote the finite sum and product of their children.  Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root denotations.  Normalization derivations check consistency, unnesting, \((1)\), and finite disjoint Boolean identities pointwise.  Ancestor derivations enumerate every marginalized assignment.  Split derivations expand over the original districts \(\mathcal D(G)\), never over districts newly formed in an induced subgraph.  Extraction derivations are finite \(\mathsf{XEvent}\)- and \(\mathsf{XExpr}\)-trees with exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) tables, separate numerator and context rows, and independent positivity certificates; they contain no semantic row equality.  A face node is well typed only after literal verification of every equation in \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\).  Its row-space and forced-zero certificates use exact rational or real-algebraic linear arithmetic.  Zero, nonzero, and strict-positivity certificates are independently checked rational identities, exact linear certificates, or displayed finite preordering identities; none may consist of the conclusion it certifies.

The terminals are
\[
\mathsf{Result}::=
\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)
\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t).
\]
Failure traces include ill-typed normalization or deterministic-preimage parsing, undefined original-district splitting, failed locality or extraction, \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\).  For a nonterminal configuration define
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}
=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi,r_C)\in\mathbb N^8,
\]
counting respectively raw, normalized, ancestor-closed, row-needed, face-needed, unresolved-sum, unresolved-product nodes, and one terminalization flag; every terminal has rank zero.
defs.def:dctftr-recursion:
Initialize a finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_\rho\cap E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\).  The deterministic priority rules are \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\), and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\), using the rank from \(\mathrm{def:dctftr\text{-}grammar}\) and least-node tie breaking.

The normalization rule expands deterministic output cells only through the pointwise preimage identity and checks Boolean equality.  The ancestor rule records its complete finite marginalization identity.  At split, run \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) for every original district in canonical order.  An accepting trace creates \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\).  If no original district is local, splice the exact original-district expansion
\[
P_{M^\star}(C)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1_C(\omega)
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^\star(\omega_D)
\tag{1}
\]
as a finite sum-product DAG.  No factorization over districts newly formed by an induced subgraph is used.  An enumeration or typing failure returns its typed split failure.

At extraction, enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete supplied output cell, and constructive extraction record.  Retain a candidate only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  Retain a raw output-cell row only when its exhaustive locality table accepts, and retain every derived numerator and context row separately.  Never retain a conditional quotient as a row.  Prepend normalization, construct \((A_D,m_D)\) exactly as in \(\mathrm{def:stacked\text{-}menu\text{-}system}\), and replay the derivations to check each equality in \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\) literally.  Rejected candidates are recorded and remain constraints of the global canonical fiber.

At face identification, compute the forced-zero set by exact linear programming and accept only a checked representation
\[
b_D=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_D+
\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega.
\tag{2}
\]
It then resolves the node to \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}m_D\).  Failure of membership returns \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), whose witness concerns only the local row relaxation; when only normalization survives, the same failed face test is labelled \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\).  Ready sum and product rules use finite additivity and the original-district factorization in \((1)\).

Condition returns uniform zero evidence only with an independent certificate, divides only with an independent certificate of strict positivity throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), returns a displayed compatible zero-evidence model when available, and otherwise returns uncertified positivity.  In priority order, the first seven rules decrease respectively \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi\), fix every earlier coordinate, and create no earlier-phase node; condition decreases \(r_C\) only after the other coordinates vanish.  Every partial operation has its stated failure branch, so \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.

\]

thm:recursion-soundness.proof_tex:
The two initial roots denote
\[
\bigl(P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E),P_{M^\star}(E)\bigr)
\tag{1}
\]
for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  Induction along the checked trace, using transition preservation, keeps \((1)\) invariant.  Lexicographic order on \(\mathbb N^8\) is well founded, every nonterminal transition strictly decreases the rank, and every successor is unique.  The run is therefore finite and unique.  The exhaustive failure branches established by transition preservation exclude \(\operatorname{STUCK}\).

For an identification terminal, structural induction on the expression derivation shows \(F_B,F_E\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\).  Root preservation gives
\[
F_B(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E),
\qquad
F_E(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(E)
\tag{2}
\]
throughout the compatibility fiber.  Its independent certificate proves \(F_E>0\) there, so division is valid and
\[
\frac{F_B(\mathcal P)}{F_E(\mathcal P)}
=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\mid E)=Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M).
\tag{3}
\]
If a uniform-zero certificate is returned, \((2)\) makes the conditional undefined in every compatible model.  Every other failure occurs before an unavailable equality or positivity assertion is used and performs no division.  Finally, a face-failure witness varies only the outer row face; the one-district projection theorem is needed separately to lift it.  This proves soundness and the stated scope.

snapshot.stmt: For every realizable typed menu with \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), the priority transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has a unique finite run because \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}\in\mathbb N^8\) decreases lexicographically. Every reached configuration has root denotation \((P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If the result is \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\), then \(F_B,F_E\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\), \(\pi\) proves \(F_E>0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), and \(F_B(\mathcal P)/F_E(\mathcal P)=Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M)\) for every compatible model. If \(z\) proves \(F_E=0\) throughout the fiber, the result is \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) and the conditional is undefined. A split failure, failed extraction, normalization-only face failure, denominator witness at zero, or uncertified denominator positivity returns its typed \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) trace and performs no division. A \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\) witness certifies only local district-face variation and implies global nonidentification only when the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem are separately verified. The observed numerical sign of \(F_E\) is never itself a positivity certificate, and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.

It contains a quotient \(F/H\) only together with an independently checked certificate that \(H\ne0\) on the relevant compatibility fiber; a conditional causal output requires the stronger stored certificate \(H>0\) throughout that fiber.  A quantifier-free semialgebraic range or endpoint description returned by the canonical quantifier-elimination fallback is represented by \(\mathsf{HybridResult}\), not declared to belong to \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\).

defs.def:dctftr-recursion:
Initialize a finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_\rho\cap E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\).  The deterministic priority rules are \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\), and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\), using the rank from \(\mathrm{def:dctftr\text{-}grammar}\) and least-node tie breaking.

The normalization rule expands deterministic output cells only through the pointwise preimage identity and checks Boolean equality.  The ancestor rule records its complete finite marginalization identity.  At split, run \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) for every original district in canonical order.  An accepting trace creates \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\).  If no original district is local, splice the exact original-district expansion
\[
P_{M^\star}(C)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1_C(\omega)
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^\star(\omega_D)
\tag{1}
\]
as a finite sum-product DAG.  No factorization over districts newly formed by an induced subgraph is used.  An enumeration or typing failure returns its typed split failure.

At extraction, enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete supplied output cell, and constructive extraction record.  Retain a candidate only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  Retain a raw output-cell row only when its exhaustive locality table accepts, and retain every derived numerator and context row separately.  Never retain a conditional quotient as a row. At face identification, compute the forced-zero set by exact linear programming and accept only a checked representation
\[
b_D=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_D+
\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega.
\tag{2}
\]
It then resolves the node to \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}m_D\).  Failure of membership returns \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), whose witness concerns only the local row relaxation; when only normalization survives, the same failed face test is labelled \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\).  Ready sum and product rules use finite additivity and the original-district factorization in \((1)\).

Condition returns uniform zero evidence only with an independent certificate, divides only with an independent certificate of strict positivity throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), returns a displayed compatible zero-evidence model when available, and otherwise returns uncertified positivity. defs.def:dctftr-grammar:
Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, domains, descriptors, districts, assignments, complete response profiles, and generated work-DAG identifiers.  The counterfactual syntax is
\[
\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]V_\alpha=v,
\qquad
\mathsf{Event}::=\top\mid\bot\mid\mathsf{Atom}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},
\]
where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term.  A descriptor declares a finite returned counterfactual tuple \(T_a\), a finite output alphabet \(\mathcal Y_a\), and a deterministic map \(f_a\).  Its output cell is the event \(\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\); the parser uses the pointwise preimage identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\}
\tag{1}
\]
only for normalization, locality tables, and response-profile evaluation.  The expression leaf for this cell is the directly supplied number \(P_a^s(y)\), not a collection of unsupplied tuple-cell probabilities.  Normalized events are canonical disjoint normal forms of consistent unnested atoms, including contradiction and sure-event forms.

Identified expressions have grammar
\[
\mathsf{Expr}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\nu_H),
\]
where \(J\) is finite, \(r\in\mathbb Q\), and \(\nu_H\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate on the declared fiber.  The phase-indexed work-node grammar is
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{Goal}::={}&
\operatorname{Raw}(\tau,e)
\mid\operatorname{Normed}(\tau,e,\nu)
\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(\tau,H,e,\alpha)
\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\\
&\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(\tau,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)
\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),
\end{split}
\]
with \(\tau\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\) and an accepting locality trace \(\ell\) on every row-needed node.  A configuration \(\mathsf{Config}\) is a finite well-typed acyclic DAG of these nodes, two distinguished roots, and a checked transition trace.

For \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), raw, normalized, and ancestor-closed nodes denote their target-domain event probabilities.  A row or face node at \((D,b)\) denotes \(b^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\), a resolved node denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\), and sum and product nodes denote the finite sum and product of their children.  Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root denotations.  Normalization derivations check consistency, unnesting, \((1)\), and finite disjoint Boolean identities pointwise.  Ancestor derivations enumerate every marginalized assignment.  Split derivations expand over the original districts \(\mathcal D(G)\), never over districts newly formed in an induced subgraph.  Extraction derivations are finite \(\mathsf{XEvent}\)- and \(\mathsf{XExpr}\)-trees with exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) tables, separate numerator and context rows, and independent positivity certificates; they contain no semantic row equality.  A face node is well typed only after literal verification of every equation in \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\).  Its row-space and forced-zero certificates use exact rational or real-algebraic linear arithmetic.  Zero, nonzero, and strict-positivity certificates are independently checked rational identities, exact linear certificates, or displayed finite preordering identities; none may consist of the conclusion it certifies.

The terminals are
\[
\mathsf{Result}::=
\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)
\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t).
\]
Failure traces include ill-typed normalization or deterministic-preimage parsing, undefined original-district splitting, failed locality or extraction, \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\).  For a nonterminal configuration define
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}
=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi,r_C)\in\mathbb N^8,
\]
counting respectively raw, normalized, ancestor-closed, row-needed, face-needed, unresolved-sum, unresolved-product nodes, and one terminalization flag; every terminal has rank zero.
defs.def:stacked-menu-system:
Fix \(D\).  Enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete output cell, and extraction record canonically.  A candidate is transport admissible only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  First retain every admissible complete output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\) whose exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) table accepts, with row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}\) and supplied value \(P_a^s(y)\).  Next, for every successful extraction judgment retain separately the numerator pair
\[
(r_{s,a,D,h,c},N_{s,a,D,h,c})
\]
and the context pair
\[
(v_{s,a,D,h},H_{s,a,D,h}).
\]
Never stack the quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) as a linear row.  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) with value one and stack precisely the accepted raw, numerator, and context rows as \(A_D\), with their values in the same order as \(m_D\).  A failed locality, fixing, expression, positivity, or admissibility check contributes no row.  A rejected complete cell remains, without information loss, among the complete polynomial equalities of the exact global fiber.  For a deterministic postprocessor, recursive locality and the raw incidence row use the preimage identity \((1)\) from \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), but the stacked value is the directly supplied output probability \(P_a^s(y)\).
defs.def:finite-extraction-calculus:
The finite extraction calculus has event syntax
\[
\mathsf{XEvent}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\top\mid\bot\mid
\neg\mathsf{XEvent}\mid
\bigsqcup_{j\in J}\mathsf{XEvent}_j\mid
\operatorname{Marg}_{W}(\mathsf{XEvent})\mid
\operatorname{Fix}(\mathsf{FixTrace},\mathsf{XEvent}),
\]
where \(J\) and every marginalized alphabet are finite, and a disjoint-union node carries a complete pointwise disjointness table.  The cell event is
\[
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its probability leaf is the supplied output cell \(P_a^s(y)\).  Only its recursively evaluated indicator is expanded by the finite identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\};
\tag{1}
\]
the tuple-cell probabilities on the right of \((1)\) are not menu generators unless an identity-output tuple descriptor is separately supplied.

Menu expressions have syntax
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{XExpr}::={}&
\operatorname{CellProb}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j
\mid\mathsf{XExpr}-\mathsf{XExpr}
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j\\
&\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\pi_H),
\end{split}
\]
where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\pi_H\) is a separately checkable strict-positivity certificate on its declared compatibility fiber.  A derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) is generated only by an output-cell lookup, the truth-table identity \((1)\), contradiction or sure-event evaluation, finite disjoint additivity, complementation, finite marginalization, multiplication of independent original-district factors, and a checked fixing trace.

A fixing trace is a finite tree whose leaves are event or expression derivations and whose constructors are identity, typed substitution from a fixed finite registry of sound Boolean or fixing identities, finite disjoint sum, finite product, complement, marginalization, conditional quotient with a separately checked positive denominator, composition, and cleared-denominator comparison.  Every constructor stores all of its children and type data.  A comparison node is accepted only when cross-multiplication is legal under its stored denominator certificates and coefficient-by-coefficient normalization gives the zero polynomial.  The identity registry is finite and contains only pointwise Boolean identities, finite total-probability identities, and the fixing identities explicitly verified by recursive substitution of structural response tables.  Thus no constructor contains the semantic equality it is intended to establish.

Positivity certificates are either a positive rational constant after exact normalization, a rational Farkas identity for a linear face, or a displayed finite preordering identity
\[
p-\varepsilon=
\sum_i\tau_i h_i+
\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}\sigma_J
\prod_{j\in J}g_j,
\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
where the declared fiber has equations \(h_i=0\), inequalities \(g_j\geq0\), and every \(\sigma_J\) is checked coefficient by coefficient to be a finite sum of squares.  All polynomial equalities are checked by exact integer or rational coefficient comparison.

For an event \(A\) and a district \(D\), the total procedure \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) enumerates
\[
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\longmapsto
\mathbf 1\{A\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\}
\]
over the complete finite response carriers.  It accepts exactly when every two entries with the same \(\omega_D\) agree, and then returns their common row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\).  Otherwise it returns the first disagreeing pair in the canonical order.  All syntax trees, registries, coefficient vectors, truth tables, and searches are finite and canonically ordered.

prop:typed-instance-embeddings.proof_tex:
Map every descriptor in the observational or atomic hard-interventional CTFTR restriction to the identical graph, domain, alphabet, intervention, target, and complete supplied output law, with the identity deterministic output map.  This is injective and type preserving.  It is not surjective because \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) supplies a genuine two-world Layer-3 output.  Conditional and stochastic-policy constructors are absent from the restricted source class, so no map for them is asserted.

For the declared CTFIDU+ intersection, set \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\) and apply its stipulated constructor map, again using the identity output map unless the constructor declares a finite postprocessor.  Properness follows from the binary source-labelled family: a single SCM cannot induce both \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).  Published CTFTR soundness and recursion soundness equate both successful outputs with the same query on the first intersection; published CTFIDU+ soundness and recursion soundness do the same on the second.  This proves semantic agreement only and establishes exactly the asserted inclusions and strictness witnesses.

snapshot.stmt: Under the finite semi-Markovian convention, the observational and atomic hard-interventional restriction \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFTR}}\) has a proper typed embedding into \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\). The DCTFTR-expressible intersection \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFIDU+}}\) of the published one-SCM Layer-3 grammar has a proper typed embedding obtained by setting \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\) and applying its declared constructor map. No embedding of the full CTFTR conditional or stochastic-policy grammar, and no embedding of an undeclared CTFIDU+ Layer-2.5 action, is asserted. On either embedded restriction, every successful DCTFTR functional and every successful functional returned by the corresponding published calculus equals the same causal query in every compatible model; syntactic or transition-by-transition equivalence is not asserted. In \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the first restriction cannot accept the genuine cross-world cell \(p\), while the complete source-labelled family with \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\) is not realizable by one SCM and hence is outside the second restriction.

Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so \(D=\{Y\}\) is invariant.  Order
\[
\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}
\]
for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set
\[
A_D=\begin{bmatrix}
1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1
\end{bmatrix},
\qquad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=
\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\leq p\leq1/2\},
\qquad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.
\]
Take \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\),
\[
B_\rho=\{Y_0\ne Y_1\},
\qquad B_\sigma=\{Y_1=1\}.
\]

\[
n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0),\quad
n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1),\quad
d_D=(1,1,1,1),
\]
and \(\varepsilon_D=1\) with the exact identity \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q=1\) on the face; these data form \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\).  Hence
\[

\]

\[

\]
The complete source output law has \(P_{e^\dagger}^s(1)=3/8\) and \(P_{e^\dagger}^s(0)=5/8\).  Its output-one row is
\[

\]
the output-zero row is its normalization-dependent complement, and \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}=\{q(3/8)\}\ne\varnothing\).  Finally set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).

Normalized events are canonical disjoint normal forms of consistent unnested atoms, including contradiction and sure-event forms.

Identified expressions have grammar
\[
\mathsf{Expr}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\nu_H),
\]
where \(J\) is finite, \(r\in\mathbb Q\), and \(\nu_H\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate on the declared fiber.  The phase-indexed work-node grammar is
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{Goal}::={}&
\operatorname{Raw}(\tau,e)
\mid\operatorname{Normed}(\tau,e,\nu)
\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(\tau,H,e,\alpha)
\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\\
&\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(\tau,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)
\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),
\end{split}
\]
with \(\tau\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\) and an accepting locality trace \(\ell\) on every row-needed node.  A configuration \(\mathsf{Config}\) is a finite well-typed acyclic DAG of these nodes, two distinguished roots, and a checked transition trace.

For \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), raw, normalized, and ancestor-closed nodes denote their target-domain event probabilities.  A row or face node at \((D,b)\) denotes \(b^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\), a resolved node denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\), and sum and product nodes denote the finite sum and product of their children.  Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root denotations.  Normalization derivations check consistency, unnesting, \((1)\), and finite disjoint Boolean identities pointwise.  Ancestor derivations enumerate every marginalized assignment.  Split derivations expand over the original districts \(\mathcal D(G)\), never over districts newly formed in an induced subgraph.  Extraction derivations are finite \(\mathsf{XEvent}\)- and \(\mathsf{XExpr}\)-trees with exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) tables, separate numerator and context rows, and independent positivity certificates; they contain no semantic row equality.  A face node is well typed only after literal verification of every equation in \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\).  Its row-space and forced-zero certificates use exact rational or real-algebraic linear arithmetic.  Zero, nonzero, and strict-positivity certificates are independently checked rational identities, exact linear certificates, or displayed finite preordering identities; none may consist of the conclusion it certifies.

The terminals are
\[
\mathsf{Result}::=
\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)
\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t).
\]
Failure traces include ill-typed normalization or deterministic-preimage parsing, undefined original-district splitting, failed locality or extraction, \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\).  For a nonterminal configuration define
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}
=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi,r_C)\in\mathbb N^8,
\]
counting respectively raw, normalized, ancestor-closed, row-needed, face-needed, unresolved-sum, unresolved-product nodes, and one terminalization flag; every terminal has rank zero.
defs.def:stacked-menu-system:
Fix \(D\).  Enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete output cell, and extraction record canonically.  A candidate is transport admissible only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  First retain every admissible complete output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\) whose exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) table accepts, with row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}\) and supplied value \(P_a^s(y)\).  Next, for every successful extraction judgment retain separately the numerator pair
\[
(r_{s,a,D,h,c},N_{s,a,D,h,c})
\]
and the context pair
\[
(v_{s,a,D,h},H_{s,a,D,h}).
\]
Never stack the quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) as a linear row.  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) with value one and stack precisely the accepted raw, numerator, and context rows as \(A_D\), with their values in the same order as \(m_D\).  A failed locality, fixing, expression, positivity, or admissibility check contributes no row.  A rejected complete cell remains, without information loss, among the complete polynomial equalities of the exact global fiber.  For a deterministic postprocessor, recursive locality and the raw incidence row use the preimage identity \((1)\) from \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), but the stacked value is the directly supplied output probability \(P_a^s(y)\).
defs.def:finite-extraction-calculus:
The finite extraction calculus has event syntax
\[
\mathsf{XEvent}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\top\mid\bot\mid
\neg\mathsf{XEvent}\mid
\bigsqcup_{j\in J}\mathsf{XEvent}_j\mid
\operatorname{Marg}_{W}(\mathsf{XEvent})\mid
\operatorname{Fix}(\mathsf{FixTrace},\mathsf{XEvent}),
\]
where \(J\) and every marginalized alphabet are finite, and a disjoint-union node carries a complete pointwise disjointness table.  The cell event is
\[
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its probability leaf is the supplied output cell \(P_a^s(y)\).  Only its recursively evaluated indicator is expanded by the finite identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\};
\tag{1}
\]
the tuple-cell probabilities on the right of \((1)\) are not menu generators unless an identity-output tuple descriptor is separately supplied.

Menu expressions have syntax
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{XExpr}::={}&
\operatorname{CellProb}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j
\mid\mathsf{XExpr}-\mathsf{XExpr}
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j\\
&\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\pi_H),
\end{split}
\]
where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\pi_H\) is a separately checkable strict-positivity certificate on its declared compatibility fiber.  A derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) is generated only by an output-cell lookup, the truth-table identity \((1)\), contradiction or sure-event evaluation, finite disjoint additivity, complementation, finite marginalization, multiplication of independent original-district factors, and a checked fixing trace.

A fixing trace is a finite tree whose leaves are event or expression derivations and whose constructors are identity, typed substitution from a fixed finite registry of sound Boolean or fixing identities, finite disjoint sum, finite product, complement, marginalization, conditional quotient with a separately checked positive denominator, composition, and cleared-denominator comparison.  Every constructor stores all of its children and type data.  A comparison node is accepted only when cross-multiplication is legal under its stored denominator certificates and coefficient-by-coefficient normalization gives the zero polynomial.  The identity registry is finite and contains only pointwise Boolean identities, finite total-probability identities, and the fixing identities explicitly verified by recursive substitution of structural response tables.  Thus no constructor contains the semantic equality it is intended to establish.

Positivity certificates are either a positive rational constant after exact normalization, a rational Farkas identity for a linear face, or a displayed finite preordering identity
\[
p-\varepsilon=
\sum_i\tau_i h_i+
\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}\sigma_J
\prod_{j\in J}g_j,
\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
where the declared fiber has equations \(h_i=0\), inequalities \(g_j\geq0\), and every \(\sigma_J\) is checked coefficient by coefficient to be a finite sum of squares.  All polynomial equalities are checked by exact integer or rational coefficient comparison.

For an event \(A\) and a district \(D\), the total procedure \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) enumerates
\[
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\longmapsto
\mathbf 1\{A\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\}
\]
over the complete finite response carriers.  It accepts exactly when every two entries with the same \(\omega_D\) agree, and then returns their common row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\).  Otherwise it returns the first disagreeing pair in the canonical order.  All syntax trees, registries, coefficient vectors, truth tables, and searches are finite and canonically ordered.

thm:transported-dominance-duality.proof_tex:
The normalization row and nonnegativity make the nonempty face \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) a compact subset of the simplex.  Apply finite linear-programming strong duality with cost \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) to obtain attainment and
\[
\min_{q\geq0:A_Dq=m_D}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q
=\max_{\eta:A_D^{\mathsf T}\eta\leq g_{\rho,\sigma,D}}
m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta.
\tag{1}
\]
These are the primal and dual quantities in the statement by the two definitions.

For a broad compatible model, projection puts \(q_D^\star\) in the face.  The checked-local-arms record and the district-cell lemma give
\[
Q_\sigma^\star-Q_\rho^\star
=\frac{g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star}
{d_D^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star},
\qquad
d_D^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star\geq\varepsilon_D>0.
\tag{2}
\]
For every dual-feasible \(\eta\),
\[
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star
\geq\eta^{\mathsf T}A_Dq_D^\star
=m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus a positive dual value proves broad strict dominance.

Under \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\), every face law lifts to the focal fiber.  Since the minimum in \((1)\) is attained and the denominator in \((2)\) is positive, strict dominance at every lifted law is equivalent to \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)>0\).  Strong duality makes this equivalent to existence of a positive attained dual value.  A negative minimizing law, and when present a positive maximizing law, lift to the asserted original-alphabet reverse-ranking and opposite-ranking witnesses while every nonfocal district remains fixed.  The separation hierarchy gives the simpler sufficient checks.  Without the record, \((2)\) is not defined; without exact focal projection, \((3)\) remains sound but a primal optimizer need not lift.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record is given and \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\).  Then
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=
\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}
\{m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta:A_D^{\mathsf T}\eta
\leq g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\}.
\]
Every feasible dual vector with \(m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta>0\) certifies \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every model in the broad fiber \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  If additionally \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, a positive dual value is also necessary for uniform strict dominance on \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\).  Under that hypothesis, \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\) is attained by an original-alphabet focal-district-saturated SCM with the reverse strict ranking, and
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0<
\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
\]
yields two such same-menu SCM families with opposite rankings while preserving every nonfocal district.  Nonemptiness of the focal fiber together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\), is sufficient for the exact clauses.  Without the total checked-local-arms record the conditional comparison is undefined; without baseline-averaged focal projection, primal optimizers need not lift.

defs.def:active-slice-separated-menu:
For a fixed district \(D\), define its active row space by
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\subseteq\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
For a complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and for
\(\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'}\), define its focal recursive-indicator slice by
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(\omega_D)
=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
The active-slice face-separation predicate \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell and every fixed nonfocal response profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  When \(D\) is the only district, the nonfocal product is the singleton empty profile.
defs.def:baseline-averaged-active-slice-menu:
Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\).  For a baseline \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), let
\[
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
=\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}q_{D'}^{0,s}(\omega_{D'}),
\qquad
\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\]
where \(q_{D'}^{0,s}\) is the response-profile law induced by \(M^{0,s}\).  For every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), define the baseline-averaged focal row
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}
\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
The baseline-averaged active-slice predicate \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when there exists one \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) such that
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell.  The same witnessing baseline must be used for all cells and all feasible replacements of the focal law; a baseline depending on the replacement law is not permitted.
defs.def:district-separated-menu: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\).  This is a finite syntactic and tabular condition; it excludes an unrecorded cross-district polynomial constraint involving \(q_D^\star\).
defs.def:dual-dominance-certificate:
Given a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record, \(\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), a menu-dual dominance certificate at level \(\gamma\) is a vector \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}\) satisfying
\[
A_D^{\mathsf T}\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}
\leq g_{\rho,\sigma,D}
\quad\text{coordinatewise},
\qquad
m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\geq\gamma.
\]
It is not defined in the absence of the total locality and common-evidence record.
defs.def:focal-district-saturated-model-class:
For a fixed district \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete};\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ there is exactly one finite latent block }
U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{storing one full deterministic response map for each vertex in }D
\text{ at every allowed parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation of a vertex in }D
\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&U_D^s\text{ is independent of the exogenous blocks of every }D'\ne D;\\
&\text{every probability law on }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ is permitted for }U_D^s,
\text{ subject only to equality with the target law}\\
&\text{when }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing;\\
&\text{for each }D'\ne D\text{, all structural tables, latent-factor restrictions,}
\text{ and cross-domain equalities remain those of }\mathfrak M
\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The phrase ``every probability law is permitted'' includes closure under replacing the law of \(U_D^\star\) and all its unchanged-source copies while holding all mechanisms and latent laws in districts \(D'\ne D\), and all changed-source copies of \(U_D\), fixed. Define
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:sharp-dominance-margin:
Given a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record and \(\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), define
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
=\min_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q,
\qquad
\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
=\max_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q.
\]
The definitions are made only when the checked record exists; its positivity certificate makes every associated conditional comparison well defined on the face.
defs.def:target-arm-rows:
For a fixed district \(D\), a total record \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) consists of: a finite nonempty arm set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); for every \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(B_\rho\cap E)\) trace and its constructed row \(n_{\rho,D}\); one accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(E)\) trace and its constructed row \(d_D\); a rational or real-algebraic number \(\varepsilon_D>0\); and an exact certificate that
\[
d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D
\qquad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Only from such a record define, for \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\),
\[
Q_\rho(q)=\frac{n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q}{d_D^{\mathsf T}q},
\qquad
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}.
\]
Separately, for any target cell \(C\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) trace constructs the generic target row \(b_D=\operatorname{row}_D(C)\).  If a required locality trace rejects, the corresponding row, comparison, or target value is undefined rather than silently assigned a row.

thm:one-cell-sign-regime-frontier.proof_tex:
The linear image of the nonempty compact convex face under \((r_D^\dagger)^{\mathsf T}\) is a nonempty compact convex subset of \(\mathbb R\), hence a closed interval.  For \(p\in I_D\), strong duality for the row-augmented equality gives
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)
=\max_{\eta,\xi}
\left\{m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta+p\xi:
A_D^{\mathsf T}\eta+r_D^\dagger\xi
\leq g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The dual polyhedron is fixed and rational and has finitely many relevant bases.  On each basis region its value is affine in \((m_D,p)\) with rational coefficients.  Hence \((1)\) is a finite maximum of affine functions and is finite, convex, continuous, and piecewise affine on \(I_D\).

Its nonpositive sublevel set is closed and convex, so it is empty, a point, or a closed interval.  Its complement in \(I_D\) has at most two relative boundary points.  At a boundary, continuity gives value zero and primal-dual attainment supplies both an equality law and a zero-valued dual certificate.  On an adjacent positive piece, the active dual basis has positive value.  The checked record gives \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D>0\), so these numerator signs are exactly the conditional arm-order signs.  Applying exact focal projection to the augmented complete output law lifts a boundary law under its \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\) predicate.  The separation hierarchy gives the two stronger sufficient predicates.  The final limitations follow because neither a conditional comparison nor a causal lifting exists without the corresponding stated premise.

snapshot.stmt: Suppose a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record is given and \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\).  For every realizable additional complete output-cell row \(r_D^\dagger\), \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function.  Its pieces are obtained from feasible bases of the row-augmented dual and have coefficients rational affine in \(m_D\).  Consequently \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of a closed convex subset, which is empty, a point, or a closed interval, and has zero, one, or two relative sign boundaries.  Every boundary has a zero-valued dual menu certificate and a primal row-face law attaining equality; every adjacent strict-pruning side has a positive dual piece.  If the augmented menu at a boundary satisfies \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\), the equality law is realized by an original-alphabet SCM saturated only at \(D\), with every nonfocal district unchanged.  Nonemptiness of the augmented focal fiber together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\), is sufficient for this realization.  Without the checked-local-arms record the frontier is undefined; without baseline-averaged focal projection, no causal lifting of a row-face boundary is asserted.

Given a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record and a realizable additional complete Layer-3 output-cell row \(r_D^\dagger\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\), define
\[
I_D=\{(r_D^\dagger)^{\mathsf T}q:q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
For \(p\in I_D\), define
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)
=\min_{\substack{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\\
(r_D^\dagger)^{\mathsf T}q=p}}
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q,
\qquad
\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+
=\{p\in I_D:\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)>0\}.
\]
Every object is defined only from the checked arm rows and their common strictly positive evidence row.
defs.def:target-arm-rows:
For a fixed district \(D\), a total record \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) consists of: a finite nonempty arm set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); for every \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(B_\rho\cap E)\) trace and its constructed row \(n_{\rho,D}\); one accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(E)\) trace and its constructed row \(d_D\); a rational or real-algebraic number \(\varepsilon_D>0\); and an exact certificate that
\[
d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D
\qquad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Only from such a record define, for \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\),
\[
Q_\rho(q)=\frac{n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q}{d_D^{\mathsf T}q},
\qquad
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}.
\]
Separately, for any target cell \(C\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) trace constructs the generic target row \(b_D=\operatorname{row}_D(C)\).  If a required locality trace rejects, the corresponding row, comparison, or target value is undefined rather than silently assigned a row.

prop:binary-acquisition-check.proof_tex:
\paragraph{Proof.}
Write a generic law on the ordered response-profile carrier in the complete binary instance as
\[
q=(q_{00},q_{01},q_{10},q_{11})^{\mathsf T}.
\]
By the definitions of the binary instance and the compatible face, membership in \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is equivalent to coordinatewise nonnegativity together with
\[
q_{00}+q_{01}+q_{10}+q_{11}=1,
\qquad
q_{10}+q_{11}=\frac12,
\qquad
q_{01}+q_{11}=\frac12.
\tag{2}
\]
Set \(p=q_{11}\).  The last two equations in \((2)\) give
\[
q_{10}=\frac12-p,
\qquad
q_{01}=\frac12-p,
\]
and substitution in the first equation gives
\[
q_{00}
=1-\left(\frac12-p\right)-\left(\frac12-p\right)-p
=p.
\]
Thus every feasible law equals
\[
q(p)=\left(p,\frac12-p,\frac12-p,p\right)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{3}
\]
Coordinatewise nonnegativity in \((3)\) is equivalent to \(0\leq p\leq 1/2\).  Conversely, for every \(p\) in this interval, \((3)\) is nonnegative and satisfies all three equations in \((2)\).  This proves both uniqueness of the parameterization and
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q(p):0\leq p\leq1/2\}.
\tag{4}
\]

The checked-local-arms record in the binary-instance definition supplies
\[
d_D=(1,1,1,1),
\quad
n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0),
\quad
n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1),
\]
and certifies \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q=1>0\) throughout the face.  Hence the divisions in the definition of the two conditional arm values are valid.  Direct substitution of \((3)\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_\rho(q(p))
&=\frac{q_{01}+q_{10}}{1}
=\left(\frac12-p\right)+\left(\frac12-p\right)
=1-2p,\\
Q_\sigma(q(p))
&=\frac{q_{01}+q_{11}}{1}
=\left(\frac12-p\right)+p
=\frac12.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]

By the additional-cell definition, \(r_D^\dagger=(0,0,0,1)\), and therefore
\[
(r_D^\dagger)^{\mathsf T}q(p)=q_{11}=p.
\tag{6}
\]
Equations \((4)\) and \((6)\) yield \(I_D=[0,1/2]\).  For any fixed \(p\in I_D\), the row-augmented feasible set contains exactly the single law \(q(p)\).  Since
\[
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}=(0,0,-1,1),
\]
the definition of the parametric transported margin and \((3)\) imply
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)
=g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q(p)
=-q_{10}+q_{11}
=-\left(\frac12-p\right)+p
=2p-\frac12.
\tag{7}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+
=\left\{p\in[0,1/2]:2p-\frac12>0\right\}
=\left(\frac14,\frac12\right].
\tag{8}
\]

For completeness, let \(\widetilde A_D\) be \(A_D\) with \(r_D^\dagger\) appended as its fourth row and let
\[
\widetilde m_D(p)=\left(1,\frac12,\frac12,p\right)^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
\eta=(0,-1,0,2)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
An exact coordinate calculation gives
\[
\widetilde A_D^{\mathsf T}\eta
=\begin{pmatrix}0\\0\\-1\\1\end{pmatrix}
=g_{\rho,\sigma,D},
\qquad
\widetilde m_D(p)^{\mathsf T}\eta
=-\frac12+2p.
\tag{9}
\]
Thus \(\eta\) is dual feasible with equality in every coordinate.  Moreover, every \(q\) satisfying the augmented row equations obeys
\[
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q
=\eta^{\mathsf T}\widetilde A_Dq
=\eta^{\mathsf T}\widetilde m_D(p)
=2p-\frac12,
\]
so the certificate is exact, in agreement with \((7)\).  At the realized value \(p=3/8\), its certified value is
\[
2\left(\frac38\right)-\frac12=\frac14.
\tag{10}
\]

The endpoint and boundary laws are genuine SCM laws on the declared binary alphabets, rather than formal points introduced by enlarging a state space.  Indeed, for any \(p\in[0,1/2]\), take a finite latent response variable \(U_D\) with values \((Y_0,Y_1)\in\{0,1\}^2\) and law \(q(p)\), and define the binary structural equation for \(Y\) by selecting the coordinate \(Y_{T_{\mathrm{tr}}}\).  Use the same response law in the target and source because \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), keep all nonfocal response blocks independent and fixed, and retain the target and source mechanisms for \(Z\) stated in the binary-instance definition.  The selection set \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\) is a union of the singleton district of \(Z\), so district closure holds; the independent construction gives district factorization.  Because \((2)\) is exactly the base row system, every such SCM induces the base menu.  The additional Boolean output equals one precisely at response type \((1,1)\), and hence its complete source output law is
\[
P_{e^\dagger}^s(1)=q_{11}=p,
\qquad
P_{e^\dagger}^s(0)=1-p.
\tag{11}
\]
In particular, \(p=3/8\) gives the declared probabilities \(3/8\) and \(5/8\).  At the sign boundary, \((3)\) gives
\[
q(1/4)=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4),
\]
and \((5)\) gives equality of the two arm values.  At the two endpoints,
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
&Q_\rho&Q_\sigma\\ \hline
p=0&1&1/2\\
p=1/2&0&1/2
\end{array}
\tag{12}
\]
so \(q(0)\) makes \(\rho\) strictly optimal and \(q(1/2)\) makes \(\sigma\) strictly optimal, both in original-alphabet SCMs.

It remains to check the acquisition conclusion.  Before acquisition, \((12)\) witnesses that each of the two arms is optimal somewhere on \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\).  Since the declared arm set is exactly \(\{\rho,\sigma\}\), the definition of the possibly-optimal set therefore gives
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\{\rho,\sigma\}.
\tag{13}
\]
Acquiring the sole block imposes \(q_{11}=3/8\) by \((11)\).  The unique parameterization \((3)\) then yields
\[
\mathcal K_{\{e^\dagger\}}
=\{q(3/8)\}
=\left\{\left(\frac38,\frac18,\frac18,\frac38\right)^{\mathsf T}\right\}.
\tag{14}
\]
At this law, equation \((5)\) gives
\[
Q_\rho(q(3/8))=\frac14<\frac12=Q_\sigma(q(3/8)).
\tag{15}
\]
There are no other arms.  Thus the acquisition and full-information definitions, together with \((14)\)--\((15)\), give
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\{e^\dagger\})
=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}
=\{\sigma\}.
\]
All conditional values used above are defined because the checked evidence denominator is identically one.  This proves every asserted identity and pruning claim.

snapshot.stmt: For \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the base face has the unique parameterization \(q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p)\), \(0\le p\le1/2\), and \[Q_\rho(q(p))=1-2p,\qquad Q_\sigma(q(p))=1/2,\qquad I_D=[0,1/2],\qquad \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=2p-1/2,\qquad \mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=(1/4,1/2].\] With the augmented row order consisting of the three rows of \(A_D\) followed by \(r_D^\dagger\), the dual vector \((0,-1,0,2)^\top\) represents \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) exactly and has value \(2p-1/2\); at the realized value \(p=3/8\) it certifies margin \(1/4\). The boundary SCM is \(q(1/4)=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)\), while \(q(0)\) makes \(\rho\) strictly optimal and \(q(1/2)\) makes \(\sigma\) strictly optimal on the original binary alphabets. For the sole unit-cost block, \[\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\{\rho,\sigma\},\qquad \mathcal K_{\{e^\dagger\}}=\{q(3/8)\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(\{e^\dagger\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.\] The first equality is witnessed by \(p=0\) for \(\rho\) and \(p=1/2\) for \(\sigma\); at \(p=3/8\), \(Q_\sigma=1/2>1/4=Q_\rho\), and no other arm exists because \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\).

defs.def:binary-check:
Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so \(D=\{Y\}\) is invariant.  Order
\[
\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}
\]
for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set
\[
A_D=\begin{bmatrix}
1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1
\end{bmatrix},
\qquad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=
\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\leq p\leq1/2\},
\qquad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.
\]
Take \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\),
\[
B_\rho=\{Y_0\ne Y_1\},
\qquad B_\sigma=\{Y_1=1\}.
\]
The exhaustive locality tables construct
\[
n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0),\quad
n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1),\quad
d_D=(1,1,1,1),
\]
and \(\varepsilon_D=1\) with the exact identity \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q=1\) on the face; these data form \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\).  Hence
\[
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1).
\]
Let \(\mathcal U=\{e^\dagger\}\), \(c_{e^\dagger}=1\), and let \(e^\dagger\) return the Boolean output
\[
f^\dagger(Y_0,Y_1)=\mathbf 1\{(Y_0,Y_1)=(1,1)\}.
\]
The complete source output law has \(P_{e^\dagger}^s(1)=3/8\) and \(P_{e^\dagger}^s(0)=5/8\).  Its output-one row is
\[
r_D^\dagger=(0,0,0,1),
\]
the output-zero row is its normalization-dependent complement, and \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}=\{q(3/8)\}\ne\varnothing\).  Finally set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).
defs.def:regime-block-acquisition:
Fix a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record.  Each \(e\in\mathcal U\) is a realizable finite block of typed descriptors, possibly with deterministic finite postprocessing.  Acquiring \(e\) reveals the complete finite law of every declared output, including every normalization-dependent complementary cell, equivalently a dependent row-value block \((R_e,p_e)\), at cost \(c_e>0\).  Require joint realizability of the whole experiment menu:
\[
\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}
=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal U\}
\ne\varnothing.
\]
For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define
\[
\mathcal K_S
=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\}.
\]
The checked lower bound \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D>0\) persists on every subface.  Hence every local subset is uniformly positive before acquisition, no subset-specific evidence screen is needed, and one may define the local row-face possibly optimal set by
\[
\operatorname{PO}(S)
=\left\{\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}:
\exists q\in\mathcal K_S\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ 
(n_{\rho,D}-n_{\sigma,D})^{\mathsf T}q\geq0\right\}.
\]
Finally set
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),
\qquad
f(S)=|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|-|\operatorname{PO}(S)|,
\]
and define the local ex-post acquisition problem by
\[
\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}.
\]
This construction is the computationally cheap district row-face layer and is the uniformly-positive special case of subset-screened global acquisition.  It does not declare \(\mathcal K_S\) to be the exact projection of the broad multi-district compatibility fiber: that equality requires the separately stated augmented focal-saturation and baseline-averaged separation hypotheses.

prop:certified-arm-removal.proof_tex: The checked-local-arms record supplies every locality equation and the uniform bound \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D>0\).  Thus the hypotheses of transported dominance duality apply.  Dual feasibility and positive dual value give \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every broad compatible model.  Because \(\sigma\) remains available, \(\rho\) is never maximizing, so deleting it cannot remove a maximizing arm.  If the evidence checker instead proves uniform zero, recursion soundness rejects division and classifies the candidate as undefined.  It is therefore not assigned a numerical rank.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record is given.  If there exists \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) with
\[
A_D^{\mathsf T}\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}
\leq g_{\rho,\sigma,D},
\qquad
m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}>0,
\]
then removing \(\rho\) cannot remove a maximizing arm from \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\).  A candidate comparison for which the common-evidence checker instead certifies uniform zero is excluded as undefined rather than ranked.
